objects.description: Referenced in comments ("ap_get_server_revision / ap_version_t"), but not defined in this header. Per instructions, ignore types not defined here.

Opaque-ish compiled regular expression wrapper used by Apache. Holds an underlying PCRE handle (re_pcre), the number of capturing subexpressions (re_nsub), and an error offset from compilation (re_erroffset). Lifetime is managed by ap_regcomp/ap_regfree. Thread-safety and ownership of re_pcre follow the implementation of the PCRE backend; details not exposed here.

POSIX-style match offset pair for a single capture group: rm_so is the start offset (inclusive) and rm_eo is the end offset (exclusive) within the matched subject. Arrays of these are filled by ap_regexec/ap_regexec_len/ap_regexec_ex and used by higher-level helpers.

Higher-level regular expression object supporting Perl-like syntax and substitution (e.g., /re/flags, s/re/sub/flags) on top of ap_regex_t. Stores the compiled regex (rx), parsed flags, substitution template (subs), last matched subject pointer (match), the number of capture slots (nmatch), and a pointer to capture offsets (pmatch). Must be allocated and managed via ap_rxplus_compile and freed via the APR pool used at creation; match memory validity depends on the lifetime of the input string passed to ap_rxplus_exec.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_slave_t ap_slave_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for an Apache slave process/thread descriptor used with listener management. Definition is not present in this header; details unknown.

Record describing a listening socket used by Apache MPMs. Holds the socket, bind address, accept callback, activity flag, default protocol, owning slave (if any), and flags (AP_LISTEN_*). Instances are linked via the next pointer to form global or bucketed listener lists.

objects.definition: typedef apr_status_t (*accept_function)(void **csd, ap_listen_rec *lr, apr_pool_t *ptrans);
objects.description: Function pointer type for per-listener accept callbacks. Called to accept a connection on a listener; returns apr_status_t and outputs the connection/socket descriptor via csd using the provided transaction pool.

objects.definition: typedef void (ap_mpm_callback_fn_t)(void *baton);
objects.description: Function type for MPM callbacks. Implementations receive a user-provided baton pointer and return no value. Used for timed and poll-based MPM notifications.
Enumeration of MPM child process state transitions: child started, exited, or lost its scoreboard slot while exiting. Used by the child_status hook.

Struct representing a single provider name entry returned by ap_list_provider_names(). It holds the name of a provider within a given group/version. Additional details (like description or module) are not present in this header.

Struct representing a provider group/version pair returned by ap_list_provider_groups(). Each entry identifies a provider registry group and its version string. No additional metadata is defined here.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int ap_slotmem_type_t;
objects.description: Bitmask type indicating slot memory behavior flags (e.g., persist, not MP safe, pregrab, clear in-use). Values are combined using AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_* macros. Underlying type is unsigned int.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_slotmem_instance_t ap_slotmem_instance_t;
objects.description: Opaque/incomplete handle to a slotmem instance managed by a provider. The actual structure is not defined in this header; users interact with it through the provider vtable functions.

objects.definition: typedef apr_status_t ap_slotmem_callback_fn_t(void* mem, void *data, apr_pool_t *pool);
objects.description: Function type for iterating over all slots via the provider’s doall. The callback receives a pointer to the slot memory, a user data pointer, and an APR pool, and returns an apr_status_t.

Vtable for slot memory providers. Exposes operations to create/attach shared slot memory, access and mutate per-slot data, iterate over slots, and manage allocation of slots. Implementations populate function pointers; consumers obtain a provider (via Apache provider framework) and use these calls to operate on ap_slotmem_instance_t handles.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_socache_instance_t ap_socache_instance_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a small-object cache instance provided by a socache provider. Only a forward declaration is present here; the concrete structure is provider-specific and defined elsewhere.

Hints passed to a socache provider at initialization to describe expected usage patterns: average ID length, average object size, and a suggested expiry cleanup interval. Providers may ignore these hints.

objects.definition:
typedef apr_status_t (ap_socache_iterator_t)(ap_socache_instance_t *instance,
                                             server_rec *s,
                                             void *userctx,
                                             const unsigned char *id,
                                             unsigned int idlen,
                                             const unsigned char *data,
                                             unsigned int datalen,
                                             apr_pool_t *pool);
objects.description: Function type for iterator callbacks used by providers to report cached id/data pairs during iteration. Returns APR status; non-success halts iteration and is returned to the caller.

Provider vtable defining the small-object cache interface. Implementations fill in these function pointers to create, initialize, destroy, store, retrieve, remove, report status, and iterate entries of a cache instance.

Record describing a monitored server slot for Apache's heartbeat/lbmethod modules. Stores the server IP as a string (up to MAXIPSIZE, sized for worst-case IPv6 text), current busy and ready counts, the last-seen timestamp (apr_time_t), and an identifier. Used by mod_heartmonitor and mod_lbmethod_heartbeat to exchange/load-balance status. Construction is by plain allocation/initialization; no special constructors or destructors are defined here. Ensure ip is NUL-terminated and seen is set to an appropriate apr_time_now() value when updating. Other semantics (e.g., units/meaning of busy/ready) are not specified in this header.
Tag name for the same struct defined by the typedef; included here to reflect the struct tag alias. Prefer using hm_slot_server_t via the typedef.
Numeric httpd version descriptor with major/minor/patch and optional suffix. Filled by ap_get_server_revision().

objects.definition: typedef apr_uint64_t ap_method_mask_t;
objects.description: Bitmask type (64-bit) used to represent sets of HTTP methods in request handling and Allow headers.
Holds the set of known (bitmask) and extension (array) HTTP methods for a context such as a request.

objects.definition: typedef apr_uint64_t ap_request_bnotes_t;
objects.description: 64-bit bitfield of per-request binary flags (e.g., strong ETag or trusted content-type).
Cached outcome of processing .htaccess for a directory path, linked per request for quick lookup.
Top-level server process context: main and config pools, argv/argc, program name.
Core HTTP request object passed to modules/filters. Owns pools, headers, metadata, URI/mapping, I/O filter chains, and bookkeeping for body handling and flags.
Enumeration for connection keepalive preference/state.
Represents a client connection: addressing, logging, filter chains, allocator, state, lifetime and MPM-related info.
Wrapper structure for a slave connection reference within multiplexed connections.

objects.definition:
typedef enum  {
    CONN_STATE_KEEPALIVE,
    CONN_STATE_PROCESSING,
    CONN_STATE_HANDLER,
    CONN_STATE_WRITE_COMPLETION,
    CONN_STATE_SUSPENDED,
    CONN_STATE_LINGER,
    CONN_STATE_LINGER_NORMAL,
    CONN_STATE_LINGER_SHORT,
    CONN_STATE_ASYNC_WAITIO,
    CONN_STATE_NUM,
    CONN_STATE_CHECK_REQUEST_LINE_READABLE  = CONN_STATE_KEEPALIVE,
    CONN_STATE_READ_REQUEST_LINE            = CONN_STATE_PROCESSING,
} conn_state_e;
objects.description: Enumeration of connection lifecycle states used by MPM and core to coordinate processing and lingering behaviors.
Enumeration indicating whether the next async/event operation should read or write.
Holds the current state and I/O sense for a connection, used primarily by event-capable MPMs.
Linked list of vhost address bindings and names for a server_rec.
Per-server logging configuration: per-module levels and global level.
Per-(virtual)server configuration and metadata: logging, vhost bindings, defaults, timeouts, names, and request limits.
Holds current server load indicators: idle/busy percentages, total bytes and access count. Populated by ap_get_sload().
Load average snapshot (1, 5, 15 minutes). Populated by ap_get_loadavg().
Name/value pair from application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies, with potentially large values held in a bucket brigade. Produced by ap_parse_form_data().
State for directory matching/wildcard expansion APIs, including pools, callback, flags and recursion depth.

objects.definition:
enum cmd_how {
    RAW_ARGS,
    TAKE1,
    TAKE2,
    ITERATE,
    ITERATE2,
    FLAG,
    NO_ARGS,
    TAKE12,
    TAKE3,
    TAKE23,
    TAKE123,
    TAKE13,
    TAKE_ARGV
};
objects.description: Enumeration of how a directive's arguments should be parsed (arity/style). Used by command_rec to declare directive signatures.
Holds context and helpers passed to directive handlers while parsing configuration: pools, server, current directive, override flags, path/regex, etc.
Type for directive handler callback(s). Either a union of specific function pointer signatures (preferred) or a generic function pointer when designated initializers are unavailable.
Describes a single configuration directive: its name, handler function, data, required override context, argument parsing mode, and usage/help text.
Abstraction of a readable config-like stream with getc/gets/close callbacks, name, and current line number. Used by the config parser and htaccess handling.
Core module descriptor for httpd modules, containing API versioning, linkage, factory/merge callbacks for dir/server configs, directive table, and hook registration entry point.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_conf_vector_t ap_conf_vector_t;
objects.description: Opaque per-scope configuration vector holding per-module config pointers, indexed by module_index. Only forward-declared here; allocated/managed via helper APIs.
Pairs a module symbol name with its module* for listing/reporting prelinked modules.

objects.definition: AP_DECLARE_DATA extern const apr_bucket_type_t ap_bucket_type_eoc;
objects.description: External declaration of the End Of Connection (EOC) apr_bucket type used to mark connection-termination buckets. Note: this is only a declaration of a const object defined elsewhere; no new type is defined here.
Connection record structure used throughout the Apache HTTP Server core to represent a network connection. Only referenced in this header; its definition lives elsewhere (not defined in this file).
Authorization requirement entry used by the core/auth modules. Holds the methods mask to which the requirement applies and the original "Require ..." line text.

Per-request configuration data owned by the core module. Carries look-ahead brigade, per-request notes array, custom responses, effective document roots/context, and flags controlling delivery/charset behavior.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned char allow_options_t;
objects.description: Bitmask type for Options directive flags in per-dir config. Values are combined OPT_* macros.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int overrides_t;
objects.description: Bitmask type for AllowOverride/AllowOverrideList behavior in per-dir config.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long etag_components_t;
objects.description: Bitmask type controlling which file attributes participate in ETag generation (e.g., mtime, inode, size, digest).
Enumeration controlling whether and how the server signature is appended to error/autoindex pages.

Per-directory configuration for the core module. Contains path/match info, Options/AllowOverride bits, resource limits, hostname/URL canonicalization, content-type/handler/filters, ETag controls, performance flags, conditional sections, logging, range limits, CGI passing, and input buffer sizing.

Per-server core configuration holding document root, access file name, <Directory>/<Location> sections, recursion limits, protocol and logging configuration, HTTP behavior toggles, protocol list/order, async filter flags, flush thresholds, and host/path normalization settings.
Enumeration of management/metrics value types supplied via the get_mgmt_items hook.
Union holding a management value in string, long, or hash form, paired with ap_mgmt_type_e.
Descriptor for a named management/metrics item exposed by modules via the get_mgmt_items hook.
Context information passed to error log providers/handlers, including server/connection/request, source location, log level, status, and other flags.
Vtable for pluggable error log providers. Defines init, writer, and argument parsing callbacks plus flags.

objects.definition:
typedef int ap_errorlog_handler_fn_t(const ap_errorlog_info *info,
                                     const char *arg, char *buf, int buflen);
objects.description: Function type for external error log format handlers that render a field given context and an argument into a buffer.
Registration record for a custom errorlog format handler (function plus flags).
Compiled element of an error log format string, capturing the handler, its argument, flags, and minimum log level.

objects.definition: typedef struct piped_log piped_log;
objects.description: Opaque type representing a piped logging facility used by httpd to spawn and communicate with an external logging process. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined elsewhere in the codebase. Use the provided API to open, close, and access the pipe file descriptors; do not access fields directly.

Opaque-typedef plus full struct defining the ingredients to build an HTTP ETag for a resource: optional vary-list validator, request time, file info/path/fd, and a flag to force weak tags. Used with ap_make_etag_ex().
Enumeration of condition-evaluation results for HTTP conditional headers (If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since, If-Unmodified-Since, If-Range).
APR bucket payload structure that carries an HTTP error status and optional message through the filter stack.
APR bucket payload for carrying an HTTP request line and headers through the filter stack.
APR bucket payload that encapsulates an HTTP response status, optional reason, headers and notes.
APR bucket payload for transporting a set of HTTP headers via brigades/filters.

objects.definition: AP_DECLARE_DATA extern const apr_bucket_type_t ap_bucket_type_eor;
objects.description: Extern declaration of the End-Of-Request (EOR) apr_bucket type used by Apache’s bucket brigades. This is not a new type definition but an extern instance of apr_bucket_type_t identifying EOR buckets.

apr_bucket is referenced by functions that create/make EOR buckets. It is not defined in this header; therefore it is ignored for type extraction. Note: No definition present here. (Informational entry to note absence.)

objects.definition: struct ap_conf_vector_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration of Apache HTTP Server’s configuration vector type, representing a per-context configuration container. Only an incomplete type is present in this header; its layout is defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef void ap_ssl_ocsp_copy_resp(const unsigned char *der, apr_size_t der_len, void *userdata);
objects.description: Function type for callbacks receiving OCSP response data in DER form. Implementations must copy the data during the call if they need it later, as the buffer lifetime is not guaranteed beyond the invocation.

objects.definition: typedef int(*ap_vhost_iterate_conn_cb)(void* baton, conn_rec* conn, server_rec* s);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked for each name-based virtual host associated with a given connection. The callback receives an opaque user baton, the current connection, and the current server, and returns 0 to continue iteration or non-zero to stop.
Enumeration of authentication outcomes for username/password and related authn lookups. Values indicate grant/deny, user presence, general errors, or that the request was otherwise handled.
Enumeration of token-authentication outcomes. Aliases some authn_status values and adds token-specific results such as mismatch, expired, and invalid.
Enumeration of authorization outcomes, including deny/grant, neutral (no decision), general error, and deny due to missing authenticated user.
Vtable of authentication provider callbacks for user/password verification and realm-hash lookup. Implementations fill function pointers to integrate with mod_auth’s authn framework.
Linked list node holding the name of an authn provider and a pointer to its authn_provider vtable. Used to chain multiple providers.
Vtable of token-authentication provider callbacks. Implementations supply check_token to validate tokens of a given type and return an autht_status.
Linked list node holding the name of a token-auth provider and a pointer to its autht_provider vtable. Used to chain multiple token providers.
Opaque filter registration record type for Apache filter framework. Not defined in this header; only extern handles are declared. Definition resides elsewhere in the Apache HTTP Server headers.
Opaque filter instance/context type used by Apache filter framework. Referenced as parameter to filters declared here; not defined in this header.
APR bucket brigade container type used to pass buckets through filters. Only referenced here; definition is in APR-util headers.
Apache request record type representing an HTTP request/response exchange. Only referenced here; actual definition is in httpd core headers.
Bucket type representing an HTTP response metadata bucket. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.

Per-directory configuration structure for mod_request. It stores settings controlling request body retention: keep_body (an apr_off_t size/flag/value) and keep_body_set (whether keep_body was explicitly configured). Exact semantics depend on mod_request, but typically used to decide whether and how much of the request body to keep for later use.

objects.definition:
typedef void ap_reclaim_callback_fn_t(int childnum, pid_t pid,
                                      ap_generation_t gen);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks invoked for each terminated child process by ap_reclaim_child_processes() and ap_relieve_child_processes(). The function receives the child slot number, pid, and server generation.
Pipe-of-death structure used by MPMs to signal child processes to exit. Holds input/output pipe file handles and the owning pool.

objects.definition: typedef enum { AP_MPM_PODX_NORESTART, AP_MPM_PODX_RESTART, AP_MPM_PODX_GRACEFUL } ap_podx_restart_t;
objects.description: Enumeration indicating the type of restart/termination to signal via the extended pipe-of-death APIs: no restart, immediate restart, or graceful restart.

objects.definition: typedef int ap_generation_t;
objects.description: Generation index type for server children. Each startup or restart increments the generation. Children in the same generation share configuration. Integer typedef stored in scoreboards and related APIs.
Enumeration describing whether the scoreboard is in shared memory (SB_SHARED) or not (SB_NOT_SHARED). Set by the MPM at scoreboard creation.

Per-worker (typically per-thread) scoreboard slot carrying runtime status, counters, timing, and short textual descriptors for the client, request, vhost, and protocol. Some fields are optional depending on build macros. Intended to be updated by MPMs and read by status/reporting code.
Global scoreboard segment with server- and thread-limit, the currently running generation and the time of last restart. Mostly written by the parent and read by children/tools.

objects.definition:
typedef struct process_score process_score;
struct process_score {
    pid_t pid;
    ap_generation_t generation; /* generation of this child */
    char quiescing;         /* the process whose pid is stored above is
                             * going down gracefully
                             */
    char not_accepting;     /* the process is busy and is not accepting more
                             * connections (for async MPMs)
                             */
    apr_uint32_t connections;       /* total connections (for async MPMs) */
    apr_uint32_t write_completion;  /* async connections in write completion */
    apr_uint32_t lingering_close;   /* async connections in lingering close */
    apr_uint32_t keep_alive;        /* async connections in keep alive */
    apr_uint32_t suspended;         /* connections suspended by some module */
    apr_uint32_t wait_io;           /* async connections waiting an IO in the MPM */
};
objects.description: Per-process scoreboard slot describing a child process’s PID, generation, and aggregate async-connection state indicators and counters. Mostly managed by the parent/MPM.
Top-level in-memory layout providing pointers into the scoreboard’s global, per-process, and per-worker sections. Stored in ap_scoreboard_image and used to navigate the scoreboard.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_sb_handle_t ap_sb_handle_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle used by MPMs and modules to reference a specific scoreboard child/thread slot without exposing internal layout. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; definition is elsewhere.

Node type for Apache HTTP Server’s configuration tree. Each node represents a single active directive, with fields linking siblings (next), children (first_child), and parent to form a tree. It stores directive name, its arguments, source location (filename, line_num), optional module-private data, and an optimization pointer (last) typically set only on the first/root node to speed appends. Allocation/ownership semantics and lifetime are not specified here; typically managed by the server’s configuration processing.

Opaque APR character set translation handle referenced by this header via extern declarations ap_hdrs_to_ascii and ap_hdrs_from_ascii. The actual type is defined in apr_xlate.h, not in this header. Included here only as an extern pointer type used for translating HTTP headers between local charset and ASCII on EBCDIC systems. Details of construction/management are outside this header.

Opaque-ish helper struct used by the Apache cookie utility to track cookie processing state for a request: the current request (r), the cookie name, the encoded cookie value, a table of cookies to add (new_cookies), and a flag indicating a duplicated cookie. The exact lifecycle is managed by the cookie API functions; there is no dedicated constructor/destructor exposed in this header. Note: request_rec and apr_table_t are external types declared elsewhere.
Typedef is not defined in this header; it is referenced from APR. Ignored per instructions. No custom type defined here.
Forward-declared/defined elsewhere (httpd.h). Not defined in this header; should be ignored per instructions.

Fixed 8-byte FastCGI record header. Fields are stored as single bytes in network order fragments (request id and content length split into high/low bytes). Used to pack/unpack FastCGI records and to compute framing. Purpose and layout are fully specified here.

Payload body for FastCGI BEGIN_REQUEST records. Encodes the role (split into two bytes), a flags byte (e.g., keep-connection), and five reserved bytes that must be sent as zero. Used when initiating a FastCGI request.
Enumeration of input filtering modes indicating how upstream should read data (by bytes, by line, speculative, exhaustive, etc.). Used by input filters with ap_get_brigade().

Opaque/linked-list node representing an installed filter in a request/connection filter chain. Holds the filter definition (frec), per-instance context (ctx), links to next filter, and associated request/connection. Modules typically receive this from add_*_filter calls and pass it to ap_get_brigade/ap_pass_brigade.

objects.definition:
typedef apr_status_t (*ap_out_filter_func)(ap_filter_t *f,
                                           apr_bucket_brigade *b);
objects.description: Function pointer type for output filter callbacks. Processes a brigade and passes/produces downstream data; returns apr_status_t.

objects.definition:
typedef apr_status_t (*ap_in_filter_func)(ap_filter_t *f,
                                          apr_bucket_brigade *b,
                                          ap_input_mode_t mode,
                                          apr_read_type_e block,
                                          apr_off_t readbytes);
objects.description: Function pointer type for input filter callbacks. Pulls data from next filter/source into a brigade given mode, blocking behavior, and size; returns apr_status_t.

objects.definition: typedef int (*ap_init_filter_func)(ap_filter_t *f);
objects.description: Function pointer type for optional filter initialization callback invoked before handlers (content filters) or as specified by protocol. Returns HTTP status/OK.
Union holding either an output or input filter function pointer. Stored in ap_filter_rec_t to represent the registered callback.
Enumeration of filter classes used for ordering and constraints (resource/content-set/protocol/transcode/connection/network).
Enumeration indicating whether a filter is input or output.
Registered filter definition/metadata: name, function(s), type/class, protocol flags, direction, provider chain, and linkage. Created by ap_register_*_filter* and referenced by installed filters.

objects.definition: typedef struct ap_filter_provider_t ap_filter_provider_t;
objects.description: Forward-declared provider record used by mod_filter to dispatch to implementations. Definition is not present in this header; details unknown.

objects.definition: struct ap_filter_private;
objects.description: Opaque/private per-filter-instance data referenced from ap_filter_t->priv. Definition is intentionally hidden in this header.

objects.definition: struct ap_filter_conn_ctx;
objects.description: Opaque/forward-declared private context stored in conn_rec for filters. Definition not provided here.
Enumeration of LDAP alias dereferencing behaviors mapped to SDK constants. Used to control how alias entries are handled during LDAP operations.

objects.definition:
typedef struct util_ldap_connection_t {
    LDAP *ldap;
    apr_pool_t *pool;                   /* Pool from which this connection is created */
#if APR_HAS_THREADS
    apr_thread_mutex_t *lock;           /* Lock to indicate this connection is in use */
#endif

    const char *host;                   /* Name of the LDAP server (or space separated list) */
    int port;                           /* Port of the LDAP server */
    deref_options deref;                /* how to handle alias dereferening */

    const char *binddn;                 /* DN to bind to server (can be NULL) */
    const char *bindpw;                 /* Password to bind to server (can be NULL) */

    int bound;                          /* Flag to indicate whether this connection is bound yet */

    int secure;                         /* SSL/TLS mode of the connection */
    apr_array_header_t *client_certs;   /* Client certificates on this connection */

    const char *reason;                 /* Reason for an error failure */

    struct util_ldap_connection_t *next;
    struct util_ldap_state_t *st;        /* The LDAP vhost config this connection belongs to */
    int keep;                            /* Will this connection be kept when it's unlocked */

    int ChaseReferrals;                 /* [on|off] (default = AP_LDAP_CHASEREFERRALS_ON)*/
    int ReferralHopLimit;               /* # of referral hops to follow (default = AP_LDAP_DEFAULT_HOPLIMIT) */
    apr_time_t freed;                   /* the time this conn was placed back in the pool */
    apr_pool_t *rebind_pool;            /* frequently cleared pool for rebind data */
    int must_rebind;                    /* The connection was last bound with other then binddn/bindpw */
    request_rec *r;                     /* request_rec used to find this util_ldap_connection_t */
    apr_time_t last_backend_conn;       /* the approximate time of the last backend LDAP request */
} util_ldap_connection_t;
objects.description: Represents a single LDAP connection, including server address, bind credentials, deref policy, security mode, client certs, and bookkeeping for pooling and reuse. Fields link it into a list and associate it with per-server LDAP state.
Lightweight configuration bundle for LDAP behavior such as referral chasing, hop limit, and client certificates.
Global/per-vhost LDAP state for mod_ldap: connection list, cache configuration and handles, SSL and verification settings, timeouts and retry policy, and synchronization primitives.
Simple struct used to store a single group attribute label/name for mod_auth_ldap processing.

No custom types are defined in this header. It only declares two functions (ap_md5 and ap_md5_binary) and includes apr_md5.h. The types referenced (apr_pool_t) are declared elsewhere. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes defined here.

Not a custom type; this is a pointer-to-pointer to char used as return type for ap_create_environment. Ignored per instructions because it is not defined here. MISSING: No custom types are defined in this header file.
Referenced from function parameters but not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions because it is not defined here. MISSING: No definition available in this header.
Referenced APR type; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions. MISSING: No definition available in this header.
Referenced APR type; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions. MISSING: No definition available in this header.
Referenced APR type; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions. MISSING: No definition available in this header.
Referenced APR type; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions. MISSING: No definition available in this header.

Resizable, pool-managed buffer for strings or binary data. Tracks capacity (avail), current length (strlen or AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN), underlying pool, and internal allocation info. Use ap_varbuf_init to initialize, ap_varbuf_grow to expand capacity, ap_varbuf_strmemcat/strcat to append, ap_varbuf_pdup to duplicate content into pool memory, ap_varbuf_regsub for regex-based substitution append, ap_varbuf_cfg_getline to read and append a line, and ap_varbuf_free to release large allocations early. After ap_varbuf_free, the struct must be re-initialized before reuse.

objects.definition: struct ap_varbuf_info;
objects.description: Opaque, forward-declared helper structure holding allocation strategy/state for ap_varbuf. Not defined in this header; contents are private to the implementation.

No custom data types are defined in this header. The only symbols present are includes and the declaration of the function ap_xml_parse_input. Any types referenced (such as request_rec and apr_xml_doc) are declared in other headers and are not defined here.
Enumeration of supported character encodings for libapreq. Values indicate the encoding used for names/data processed by the library.
Enumeration controlling how multiple strings are joined together (as-is, url-encoded, url-decoded, or quoted).
Enumeration specifying match behavior: full or partial matches.
Enumeration selecting expiration date formatting style (HTTP/RFC 2616 vs. Netscape cookie format).

Struct representing a name/value pair with lengths and a flexible array member-like data buffer. Used for parsed request values (e.g., parameters, cookies). The data buffer is sized by the allocator; data is not NUL-terminated unless allocated so. The struct is typically embedded or allocated with enough trailing space to hold dlen bytes.

Server-side cookie object supporting both legacy Netscape and RFC cookie specifications. Holds metadata (path, domain, port, comment, commentURL), lifetime (max_age, where -1 indicates a session cookie), internal flags (version/secure/HttpOnly/tainted and possibly others via APREQ flags), and the underlying apreq_value_t payload (name/value, stored in v). Constructed via apreq_cookie_make; manipulated/serialized via provided API. Memory is allocated from an APR pool; instances are typically stored in apr_table_t jars. Note: apr_time_t and apreq_value_t are defined elsewhere.

Function declaration returning a C string describing an apr_status_t error, including APREQ_ERROR_* codes. This is not a type; no custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, classes) are defined in this header.

No enums, structs, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. Only preprocessor macros for error codes (APREQ_ERROR_*) and a function declaration are present. Types like apr_status_t are referenced from external headers (apr_errno.h) and are not defined here.

Opaque-ish handle representing a request context for libapreq2. It binds a module implementation (vtable), an APR pool for lifetime management, and a bucket allocator used by I/O brigades. Modules may allocate additional data following this struct, so the runtime size can vary. Users call inline helpers or module methods via this handle to access cookies, args, body params, parser, limits, and temp dir.

Vtable describing the required operations a module must implement to work with apreq_handle_t. It provides accessors for cookies, args, body, lookups by name, parser management, hook installation, limits (brigade/read), and temp directory management. Instances are typically defined using the APREQ_MODULE(pre, mmn) convenience macro, which maps symbol names with a prefix to the struct fields.

Parameter/file-upload record combining header metadata (info), an optional upload brigade (upload) for file spooling, per-item flags (charset, taint, app bits), and the underlying name/value tuple (v). Used as the canonical value type stored in parameter tables returned by libapreq2 parsers. The struct’s lifecycle is typically bound to an APR pool provided at construction. Unknowns: exact semantics of flags bits and apreq_value_t internals are defined elsewhere (apreq.h).

Hook object invoked by a parser whenever data arrives for a file-upload parameter. Supports chaining via next, uses an APR pool for allocation, and carries a user context pointer passed to the hook function. Details such as lifecycle and ownership outside this header are not fully specified.

Request body parser instance describing how to parse incoming bucket brigades for a specific Content-Type. Holds parser function, resource handles (pool, bucket allocator), limits, temp directory, a linked list of hooks, and an internal context pointer.

objects.definition: typedef apr_status_t (*apreq_parser_function_t)(APREQ_PARSER_ARGS);
objects.description: Function pointer type for parser callbacks: signature apr_status_t (*)(apreq_parser_t *parser, apr_table_t *t, apr_bucket_brigade *bb). Returned status typically APR_INCOMPLETE, APR_SUCCESS, or an APR error. Not owned by any struct directly as an object; used as a field within apreq_parser_t.

objects.definition: typedef apr_status_t (*apreq_hook_function_t)(APREQ_HOOK_ARGS);
objects.description: Function pointer type for hook callbacks: signature apr_status_t (*)(apreq_hook_t *hook, apreq_param_t *param, apr_bucket_brigade *bb). Used by apreq_hook_t to process data chunks and may modify brigades.

Context object for the apreq_hook_find_param hook. Initialize name with the sought parameter name, set param to NULL, and prev to the address of the previous hook in the chain. The hook will assign param when found and then remove itself using prev.

functions.name: ap_pcre_version_string
functions.description: Return a textual PCRE version string. Use AP_REG_PCRE_COMPILED for the version used at compile-time or AP_REG_PCRE_LOADED for the version of the PCRE library loaded at runtime. Intended to help diagnose mismatches between build-time and runtime PCRE.
requirements: which must be either AP_REG_PCRE_COMPILED or AP_REG_PCRE_LOADED
Caller must not modify the returned string (treat it as read-only)

functions.name: ap_regcomp_get_default_cflags
functions.description: Retrieve the current default compile flags used by ap_regcomp when AP_REG_NO_DEFAULT is not specified. Returns a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* flags.

functions.name: ap_regcomp_set_default_cflags
functions.description: Set the default compile flags used by ap_regcomp (unless overridden by AP_REG_NO_DEFAULT). Flags are AP_REG_* values; unsupported bits will be ignored by ap_regcomp.
requirements: cflags is a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* values

functions.name: ap_regcomp_default_cflag_by_name
functions.description: Map a textual AP_REG flag suffix to its numeric value (e.g., name="ICASE" -> AP_REG_ICASE). Returns 0 if the name is unknown.
requirements: name points to a NUL-terminated string naming a flag without the AP_REG_ prefix (e.g., "ICASE")

functions.name: ap_regcomp
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_regcomp(ap_regex_t *preg, const char *regex, int cflags);
functions.description: Compile a POSIX-style/PCRE regular expression into an ap_regex_t. Supports AP_REG_ICASE and AP_REG_NEWLINE (other flags are ignored unless handled by defaults). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: preg must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to ap_regex_t storage
regex must be a valid, NUL-terminated regular expression string
cflags is a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* flags; only AP_REG_ICASE and AP_REG_NEWLINE affect compilation (others are ignored per documentation)
On success, the compiled regex in preg must later be released with ap_regfree

functions.name: ap_regexec
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_regexec(const ap_regex_t *preg, const char *string, apr_size_t nmatch, ap_regmatch_t *pmatch, int eflags);
functions.description: Execute a regex match on a NUL-terminated string using a pre-compiled ap_regex_t. Optionally returns match offsets in pmatch. Returns 0 on match, AP_REG_NOMATCH otherwise.
requirements: preg must point to a regex previously compiled by ap_regcomp
string must be a valid, NUL-terminated string
If nmatch > 0, pmatch must point to an array of at least nmatch ap_regmatch_t elements; if pmatch is NULL, nmatch should be 0
eflags is a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* flags; only AP_REG_NOTBOL and AP_REG_NOTEOL are honored (others are ignored)

functions.name: ap_regexec_len
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_regexec_len(const ap_regex_t *preg, const char *buff, apr_size_t len, apr_size_t nmatch, ap_regmatch_t *pmatch, int eflags);
functions.description: Execute a regex match on a character buffer of given length (not required to be NUL-terminated). Optionally returns match offsets in pmatch. Returns 0 on match, AP_REG_NOMATCH otherwise.
requirements: preg must point to a regex previously compiled by ap_regcomp
buff must point to a buffer with at least len accessible bytes
If nmatch > 0, pmatch must point to an array of at least nmatch ap_regmatch_t elements; if pmatch is NULL, nmatch should be 0
eflags is a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* flags; only AP_REG_NOTBOL and AP_REG_NOTEOL are honored (others are ignored)

functions.name: ap_regexec_ex
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_regexec_ex(const ap_regex_t *preg, const char *buff, apr_size_t len, apr_size_t pos, apr_size_t nmatch, ap_regmatch_t *pmatch, int eflags);
functions.description: Execute a regex match on a buffer of given length starting at a specified offset. Buffer need not be NUL-terminated. Returns 0 on match, AP_REG_NOMATCH otherwise.
requirements: preg must point to a regex previously compiled by ap_regcomp
buff must point to a buffer with at least len accessible bytes
pos must be less than or equal to len (start offset within the buffer)
If nmatch > 0, pmatch must point to an array of at least nmatch ap_regmatch_t elements; if pmatch is NULL, nmatch should be 0
eflags is a bitwise OR of AP_REG_* flags; only AP_REG_NOTBOL and AP_REG_NOTEOL are honored (others are ignored)

functions.name: ap_regerror
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_size_t) ap_regerror(int errcode, const ap_regex_t *preg, char *errbuf, apr_size_t errbuf_size);
functions.description: Translate an error code from ap_regcomp or ap_regexec into a human-readable message. Writes into errbuf if provided and returns the length of the message (which may exceed errbuf_size).
requirements: errcode must be a value returned by ap_regcomp or ap_regexec (e.g., AP_REG_ESPACE, AP_REG_INVARG, AP_REG_NOMATCH)
errbuf points to a buffer of size errbuf_size if errbuf_size > 0; may be NULL if errbuf_size is 0
preg may be NULL or a pointer to the regex involved, for context
Caller should check the return value to know if truncation occurred (message length > errbuf_size)

functions.name: ap_regname
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_regname(const ap_regex_t *preg, apr_array_header_t *names, const char *prefix, int upper);
functions.description: Collect the names of named subpatterns in a compiled regex into an APR array. Optionally prefixes each name and optionally uppercases them. Returns implementation-defined status code (non-zero on success in typical APR style, exact semantics not explicitly documented here).
requirements: preg must point to a regex previously compiled by ap_regcomp and containing zero or more named subpatterns
names must be a valid apr_array_header_t* created from an APR pool (will be appended to)
prefix may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; if provided, it is prepended to each name
If upper is non-zero, names will be uppercased; otherwise left as-is

functions.name: ap_regfree
functions.description: Free resources associated with a compiled regex created by ap_regcomp.
requirements: preg must point to an ap_regex_t that was previously initialized by ap_regcomp
Do not use preg for matching after calling ap_regfree unless recompiled

functions.name: ap_rxplus_compile
functions.description: Parse and compile a higher-level, Perl-like regex pattern into an ap_rxplus_t. Supports forms like "match", "/match/flags", and substitution "s/pat/repl/flags". Returns NULL on syntax or compile error.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool for all allocations
pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated string using supported forms
The returned ap_rxplus_t is pool-allocated and remains valid while the pool is alive; do not free manually

functions.name: ap_rxplus_exec
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_rxplus_exec(apr_pool_t *pool, ap_rxplus_t *rx, const char *pattern, char **newpattern);
functions.description: Apply a compiled ap_rxplus_t to an input string. For matching, returns 0 (no match) or 1 (match). For transforming patterns with the 'g' flag, may return >1 (number of matches). If the operation modifies the string (e.g., substitution), newpattern receives the modified copy allocated from pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool for any allocations (e.g., for newpattern)
rx must be a non-NULL pointer returned by ap_rxplus_compile
pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated input string and must remain in scope for regex memory to be valid as noted
If newpattern is non-NULL and the operation is a transformation, *newpattern will be set to an allocated string from pool; caller must not free it manually
Subsequent calls that rely on captured matches (e.g., ap_rxplus_match/pmatch) require that pattern remains valid (not freed or out-of-scope)

functions.name: ap_rxplus_nmatch
functions.description: Return the number of captured matches currently stored in the regex memory from the last ap_rxplus_exec call. Note: in non-DOXYGEN builds this is provided as a macro: #define ap_rxplus_nmatch(rx) (((rx)->match != NULL) ? (rx)->nmatch : 0).
requirements: rx must be a non-NULL pointer to a compiled ap_rxplus_t
Valid only after a prior call to ap_rxplus_exec; otherwise may return 0

functions.name: ap_rxplus_match
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_rxplus_match(ap_rxplus_t *rx, int n, int *len, const char **match);
functions.description: Retrieve the nth captured match from the regex memory of the last ap_rxplus_exec call. Returns the pointer to the substring within the original pattern and its length via out-parameters.
requirements: rx must be a non-NULL pointer to a compiled ap_rxplus_t with a prior successful ap_rxplus_exec
n must be between 0 and ap_rxplus_nmatch(rx) inclusive (0 is the entire match)
pattern (the original input passed to ap_rxplus_exec) must still be in scope and unmodified, as returned pointers reference it
len and match must be valid pointers if provided; function writes length to *len and pointer to *match

functions.name: ap_rxplus_pmatch
functions.description: Return a pool-allocated copy of the nth captured match from the last ap_rxplus_exec call.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool for allocation
rx must be a non-NULL pointer to a compiled ap_rxplus_t with a prior successful ap_rxplus_exec
n must be between 0 and ap_rxplus_nmatch(rx) inclusive

functions.name: ap_accept_error_is_nonfatal
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the given APR status code corresponds to an accept() error that should be treated as non-fatal for the process, typically controlled by the AcceptErrorsNonFatal configuration. Intended to be used when handling errors from accept() to decide whether to continue running.
requirements: rv must be a valid apr_status_t returned from an accept()-related operation (e.g., apr_socket_accept).
Caller should branch on the integer return value: non-zero means the error is non-fatal, zero means it is fatal.

functions.name: ap_listen_pre_config
functions.description: Initializes default state for the global listeners list before configuration is processed. Typically invoked during the pre-configuration phase to reset or prepare listener-related globals.
requirements: Must be called during the server’s pre-configuration phase, before any listener setup occurs.
No arguments; no return value.

functions.name: ap_setup_listeners
functions.description: Creates, binds, and listens on all configured listening sockets by iterating the global ap_listeners list. Returns the number of sockets successfully opened.
requirements: s should be a valid pointer to the global server_rec.
Must be called after listeners have been configured (e.g., after parsing Listen directives) and before accepting connections.
Caller should check the returned count; zero indicates no sockets were opened.

functions.name: ap_duplicate_listeners
functions.description: Duplicates the configured listeners into multiple buckets (arrays of ap_listen_rec*) when supported (e.g., based on CPU cores and SO_REUSEPORT) and/or configured via ListenCoresBucketsRatio. The resulting number of duplicated listener buckets will match *num_buckets (either provided or computed).
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool for all allocations.
s must be a valid pointer to the global server_rec.
buckets must be a valid out-parameter; on success it will point to an array of ap_listen_rec** representing the buckets.
num_buckets is in/out: if *num_buckets is 0 on input, the function computes an appropriate value; if positive, that value is preserved and used.
Caller must handle the returned apr_status_t and free resources via the given APR pool’s lifetime rules.

functions.name: ap_close_listeners
functions.description: Closes all sockets in the global ap_listen_rec list. Intended for shutdown or restart paths.
requirements: Should be called when listeners are no longer needed (e.g., during shutdown or restart).
No parameters; no return value.

functions.name: ap_close_listeners_ex
functions.description: Closes all sockets in the provided ap_listen_rec list rather than the global list.
requirements: listeners may be NULL or a valid list head; if non-NULL it must point to a well-formed ap_listen_rec linked list created by the server.
Caller should ensure no other code is concurrently using these sockets when closing.

functions.name: ap_close_selected_listeners
functions.description: Closes a selected subset of listeners associated with the provided slave/context. Specific selection semantics are not documented in this header (FIXMEDOC).
requirements: ap_slave_t pointer must refer to a valid slave/context as expected by the MPM. Further requirements are unknown due to missing documentation.
Caller should handle the integer return value; success/failure semantics are unknown due to missing documentation.

functions.name: ap_set_listenbacklog
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_listenbacklog(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for ListenBacklog. Parses and applies the maximum length of the pending connection queue (listen(2) backlog). Returns NULL on success or an error string on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; external modules should not call this directly.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms for the directive context.
arg must be a single token representing the backlog length (string form of an integer).
Caller must check the returned const char*; NULL indicates success, a non-NULL string is an error message.

functions.name: ap_set_listentcpdeferaccept
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_listentcpdeferaccept(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for ListenTCPDeferAccept. Parses and applies the TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT socket option value where supported. Returns NULL on success or an error string on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; not intended for external use.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
arg must be a single token representing the value for TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT (string form; OS/platform dependent).
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_set_listencbratio
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_listencbratio(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for ListenCoresBucketsRatio. Parses and applies the ratio between online CPU cores and the number of listener buckets. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; not intended for external use.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
arg must be a single token representing the ratio (string form; expected to be a positive numeric value).
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_set_listener
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_listener(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, int argc, char *const argv[]);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for Listen. Parses one or more arguments specifying address/port and an optional protocol, and registers a listener. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing via the Listen directive.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
argc/argv must contain the directive arguments: a port or IP:port and optionally a protocol string, per Apache’s Listen syntax.
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_set_send_buffer_size
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_send_buffer_size(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for SendBufferSize. Parses and sets the socket send buffer size in bytes. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; not intended for external use.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
arg must be a single token representing a buffer size in bytes (string form of a positive integer).
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_set_receive_buffer_size
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_receive_buffer_size(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for ReceiveBufferSize. Parses and sets the socket receive buffer size in bytes. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; not intended for external use.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
arg must be a single token representing a buffer size in bytes (string form of a positive integer).
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_set_accept_errors_nonfatal
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_accept_errors_nonfatal(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, int flag);
functions.description: Configuration directive handler for AcceptErrorsNonFatal. Enables/disables treating certain accept() errors as non-fatal. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: Called by the core during configuration parsing; not intended for external use.
cmd must be a valid cmd_parms.
flag must be an integer boolean (0 or non-zero) indicating whether to treat some accept errors as non-fatal.
Caller must check the returned const char* for errors (NULL on success).

functions.name: ap_find_systemd_socket
functions.description: Optional function (available only when built with HAVE_SYSTEMD) to locate a socket passed by systemd for the specified port in the given process context. Intended to integrate with systemd socket activation. Availability and retrieval are via APR optional-function APIs.
requirements: Only available when compiled with HAVE_SYSTEMD; callers must retrieve it via APR optional function mechanisms (APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN) and check for NULL if unavailable at runtime.
process must be a valid process_rec for the running server.
port is the target port (apr_port_t).
Return value semantics (e.g., file descriptor vs. index) are not defined in this header; callers must handle per implementation.

functions.name: ap_systemd_listen_fds
functions.description: Optional function (available only when built with HAVE_SYSTEMD) to query the number of file descriptors passed by systemd (akin to sd_listen_fds). Availability and retrieval are via APR optional-function APIs.
requirements: Only available when compiled with HAVE_SYSTEMD; callers must retrieve it via APR optional function mechanisms and handle absence.
unset_environment indicates whether to unset related environment variables after reading; exact semantics are implementation-defined and not described here.
Caller should use the integer return value as the count of descriptors; error semantics are not defined in this header.

functions.name: ap_os_create_privileged_process
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_os_create_privileged_process(const request_rec *r, apr_proc_t *newproc, const char *progname, const char * const *args, const char * const *env, apr_procattr_t *attr, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Spawn a new process with elevated privileges as requested by another module. Typical usage is from request context to execute an external helper while preserving security constraints. Returns APR status. Details of the privilege model are MPM/platform dependent.
requirements: r must point to a valid, live request_rec (inferred from context: used to identify/request privileges).
newproc must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the created process handle.
progname must be a non-NULL path or executable name resolvable on the target system.
args must be a valid NULL-terminated array of C strings; args[0] should be the program name (args[0] requirement explicitly stated; NULL-termination inferred from APR apr_proc_create patterns).
env must be a valid array of C strings; each string must be NUL-terminated (explicit). The array itself is typically NULL-terminated (inferred from APR apr_proc_create).
attr must be created/initialized with apr_procattr_create and configured as needed before the call (inferred).
p must be a valid APR pool that outlives process creation (inferred).
Check and handle the returned apr_status_t; failures may include APR_EGENERAL and platform-specific errors (inferred).

functions.name: ap_mpm_query
functions.description: Query a property of the current MPM. Pass one of the AP_MPMQ_* query codes and receive the integer result via result. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success, APR_ENOTIMPL if not implemented, or APR_EGENERAL if no mpm-query hook is registered yet.
requirements: query_code must be one of the AP_MPMQ_* constants (e.g., AP_MPMQ_IS_THREADED, AP_MPMQ_MPM_STATE, etc.).
result must be a non-NULL pointer to an int to receive the answer.
May only be called after modules’ register_hooks has run; before that the MPM may not have registered the implementing hook (explicit remark).
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for APR_SUCCESS/APR_ENOTIMPL/APR_EGENERAL and act accordingly.

functions.name: ap_mpm_resume_suspended
functions.description: Request the MPM to resume a previously suspended connection. Only supported by Event MPM; other MPMs typically return APR_ENOTIMPL.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec for a connection managed by the MPM (inferred).
The connection should be in a suspended state; resuming an active/closed connection is undefined (inferred from name/semantics).
Caller must check for APR_ENOTIMPL and other apr_status_t error returns.

functions.name: ap_mpm_register_timed_callback
functions.description: Register a callback function to be invoked by the MPM at a given time. Only supported by Event MPM; others may return APR_ENOTIMPL. The callback is invoked with the provided baton.
requirements: cbfn must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with baton.
baton may be NULL and is passed through to cbfn (inferred).
t specifies the trigger time in APR time units (microseconds); exact semantics (absolute vs relative) are not documented here and may be MPM-specific (unknown detail).
Caller must check for APR_ENOTIMPL and other apr_status_t error returns.
The callback must not assume it runs on any particular thread and must be async-safe with respect to MPM behavior (inferred).

functions.name: ap_mpm_register_poll_callback
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_mpm_register_poll_callback(apr_pool_t *p, const apr_array_header_t *pfds, ap_mpm_callback_fn_t *cbfn, void *baton);
functions.description: Register a callback to be notified when any one of a group of sockets/pipes (apr_pollfd_t entries) becomes readable/writable. On activity, all passed descriptors are removed from the MPM’s pollset and exactly one callback is invoked. Pool p is used for the MPM’s internal allocations and may be cleared by the callback.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool. It may be cleared by cbfn when invoked; the MPM retains no persistent data in it between registrations (explicit remark).
pfds must be a valid apr_array_header_t* array containing apr_pollfd_t entries to monitor (explicit).
cbfn must be a valid function pointer; it will be called once when activity is detected on any single descriptor (explicit).
baton is user data passed to cbfn; may be NULL (inferred).
On success, APR_SUCCESS is returned; APR_ENOTIMPL indicates no async support; other failures may be errors from apr_pollset_add and must be handled (explicit).
Only one callback is issued and all provided fds are removed from the pollset after the first activity (explicit).

functions.name: ap_mpm_register_poll_callback_timeout
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_mpm_register_poll_callback_timeout(apr_pool_t *p, const apr_array_header_t *pfds, ap_mpm_callback_fn_t *cbfn, ap_mpm_callback_fn_t *tofn, void *baton, apr_time_t timeout);
functions.description: Like ap_mpm_register_poll_callback, but also specifies a timeout. Exactly one of cbfn or tofn will be called: cbfn if an fd becomes ready; tofn if the timeout expires. After the callback, all passed descriptors are removed from the pollset. Pool p may be cleared by the callbacks.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool. It may be cleared by cbfn or tofn when invoked; the MPM keeps no persistent data in it between registrations (explicit remark).
pfds must be a valid apr_array_header_t* array containing apr_pollfd_t entries (explicit).
cbfn and tofn must be valid function pointers; for each call, only one of them will be invoked, never both (explicit).
baton is user data passed to whichever callback executes; may be NULL (inferred).
timeout is in microseconds; if timeout <= 0, I/O wait is unlimited (explicit).
Return APR_SUCCESS on success; APR_ENOTIMPL if no async support; other errors may come from apr_pollset_add and must be handled (explicit).
On the first activity on any descriptor, all are removed from the pollset and a single callback is issued (explicit).

functions.name: ap_register_provider
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_register_provider(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *provider_group, const char *provider_name, const char *provider_version, const void *provider);
functions.description: Register a provider instance in the global provider pool under the specified group, name, and version. Typically called during module initialization so that other code can retrieve the provider later via ap_lookup_provider. The provider argument is an opaque pointer to the provider implementation; the function allocates any necessary registry storage from the given APR pool and returns APR_SUCCESS on success.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t* used for internal allocations; choose a pool with sufficient lifetime for the registration to remain valid (e.g., a process- or server-lifetime pool).
provider_group must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider_version must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider should point to a valid provider implementation and remain valid for as long as it may be looked up (opaque to this API).
The caller must check the returned apr_status_t and handle non-APR_SUCCESS error codes.

functions.name: ap_lookup_provider
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void *) ap_lookup_provider(const char *provider_group, const char *provider_name, const char *provider_version);
functions.description: Look up and return a previously registered provider from the global provider pool that matches the given group, name, and version. Returns the opaque provider pointer if found, or NULL if not found. Callers typically cast the result to the expected provider interface type before use.
requirements: provider_group must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider_name must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider_version must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
The caller must handle a NULL return value (provider not found).
The caller is responsible for casting the returned void* to the correct provider interface type before use.

functions.name: ap_list_provider_names
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_array_header_t *) ap_list_provider_names(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *provider_group, const char *provider_version);
functions.description: Return an APR array of ap_list_provider_names_t entries naming providers registered under the specified group and version. The array is allocated from the supplied pool and may be empty if no providers match.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t*; the returned array and its contents are allocated from this pool and remain valid while the pool lives.
provider_group must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
provider_version must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
The caller must handle the case where the returned array is empty (no matching providers).

functions.name: ap_list_provider_groups
functions.description: Return an APR array of ap_list_provider_groups_t entries listing all known provider groups and their versions. The array is allocated from the supplied pool and may be empty if no providers are registered.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t*; the returned array and its contents are allocated from this pool and remain valid while the pool lives.
The caller must handle the case where the returned array is empty.

functions.name: ap_regkey_const
functions.description: Returns a sentinel ap_regkey_t pointer corresponding to one of the predefined AP_REGKEY_* root-key constants (e.g., AP_REGKEY_CLASSES_ROOT). Intended to be used as the parentkey parameter for registry functions such as ap_regkey_open and ap_regkey_remove.
requirements: i should correspond to a defined AP_REGKEY_* constant index; from this header the valid indices are 0..6 (inferred from the AP_REGKEY_* macros).
The returned pointer represents a constant/root registry key handle suitable for use as a parentkey argument.
Do not attempt to modify or free/close the returned pointer as it represents a constant root key (inferred from "Used to recover AP_REGKEY_* constants").

functions.name: ap_regkey_open
functions.description: Opens (and optionally creates) a Windows registry key identified by keyname under the given parentkey. Returns a handle in newkey for subsequent operations (querying values, setting values, closing).
requirements: On Windows only.

newkey must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the opened key handle; the handle must be closed with ap_regkey_close when no longer needed (inferred from typical open/close pattern and the presence of ap_regkey_close).
parentkey must be a valid open registry key or one of the AP_REGKEY_* root constants.
keyname is the path of the subkey relative to parentkey.
flags is a bitwise OR of APR_READ, APR_WRITE, APR_CREATE, and/or APR_EXCL as documented.
If APR_CREATE is specified together with APR_EXCL and the key already exists, an error is returned.
pool must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the resulting key handle.

functions.name: ap_regkey_close
functions.description: Closes a registry key that was opened or created by ap_regkey_open, releasing any associated resources.
requirements: key must be a valid registry key previously returned by ap_regkey_open.
Do not pass AP_REGKEY_* root constants to this function (inferred: they are constants, not opened keys).

functions.name: ap_regkey_remove
functions.description: Removes (deletes) the specified registry key under the given parent. All values within the key are removed, but the operation is not recursive and will fail if the key contains subkeys.
requirements: On Windows only.
parent must be an open registry key or one of the AP_REGKEY_* root constants.
keyname is the path of the key relative to parent.
The removal is not recursive; the key must not contain subkeys for the operation to succeed (per remark).
pool must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_get
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_regkey_value_get(char **result,
                                             ap_regkey_t *key,
                                             const char *valuename,
                                             apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Retrieves a string value from the specified open registry key. Stores the resulting NUL-terminated string in memory from pool.
requirements: On Windows only.
result must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated string.
key must be a valid, open registry key with read access.
valuename is the name of the value to retrieve; pass "" for the default value.
pool must be a valid APR pool; the returned string’s storage is owned by pool.
Environment variable expansion is always performed for REG_EXPAND_SZ values; there is no option to disable this (per remark).

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_set
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_regkey_value_set(ap_regkey_t *key,
                                             const char *valuename,
                                             const char *value,
                                             apr_int32_t flags,
                                             apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Stores a string value into the specified open registry key. Optionally expands %name% environment variables when AP_REGKEY_EXPAND is set.
requirements: On Windows only.
key must be a valid, open registry key with write access.
valuename is the name of the value to set; pass "" for the default value.
value must point to a valid NUL-terminated string to be stored.
flags must be either 0 or AP_REGKEY_EXPAND; when AP_REGKEY_EXPAND is used, %foo% variables in value are expanded from the environment before storage.
pool must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_raw_get
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_regkey_value_raw_get(void **result,
                                                 apr_size_t *resultsize,
                                                 apr_int32_t *resulttype,
                                                 ap_regkey_t *key,
                                                 const char *valuename,
                                                 apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Retrieves a registry value as raw bytes from the specified open key, along with the byte count and the registry type code.
requirements: On Windows only.
result must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a buffer containing the raw value; storage is allocated from pool.
resultsize must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes returned.
resulttype must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the registry type of the value (inferred: a Windows REG_* type code).
key must be a valid, open registry key with read access.
valuename is the name of the value to retrieve; pass "" for the default value.
pool must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the result buffer.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_raw_set
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_regkey_value_raw_set(ap_regkey_t *key,
                                                 const char *valuename,
                                                 const void *value,
                                                 apr_size_t  valuesize,
                                                 apr_int32_t valuetype,
                                                 apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Stores a raw byte array as a registry value into the specified open key, specifying the registry type explicitly. Use this for non-string data or to control the exact registry type (e.g., REG_DWORD, REG_BINARY).
requirements: On Windows only.
key must be a valid, open registry key with write access.
valuename is the name of the value to set; pass "" for the default value.
value must point to a buffer of at least valuesize bytes; valuesize specifies the number of bytes to write.
valuetype must specify the registry type of the value (inferred: a Windows REG_* type code).
pool must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_array_get
functions.description: Retrieves a multi-string (REG_MULTI_SZ) registry value from the specified open key and returns it as an APR array of C strings allocated from pool.
requirements: On Windows only.
result must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the APR array of strings.
key must be a valid, open registry key with read access.
valuename is the name of the value to retrieve; pass "" for the default value.
pool must be a valid APR pool; the array and strings are allocated from this pool.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_array_set
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_regkey_value_array_set(ap_regkey_t *key,
                                                   const char *valuename,
                                                   int nelts,
                                                   const char * const * elts,
                                                   apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Stores an array of strings as a REG_MULTI_SZ registry value into the specified open key.
requirements: On Windows only.
key must be a valid, open registry key with write access.
valuename is the name of the value to set; pass "" for the default value.
nelts is the number of strings to store (note: the doc comments appear to swap nelts/elts; the function signature indicates nelts is the count).
elts must point to an array of nelts C string pointers; each string must be NUL-terminated.
pool must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations.

functions.name: ap_regkey_value_remove
functions.description: Removes (deletes) a named value from the specified open registry key.
requirements: On Windows only.
key must be a valid, open registry key with write access.
valuename is the name of the value to remove; pass "" for the default value.
pool must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_callback_fn_t
functions.description: Function type for callbacks invoked by slotmem providers over each slot. The callback receives a pointer to the slot’s memory, the user-supplied data, and a pool. Typically used via ap_slotmem_provider_t::doall to iterate all slots.
requirements: mem points to the current slot’s memory; it is valid only for the duration of the call (as provided by the provider).
pool must be a valid APR pool supplied by the caller of doall.
Return APR_SUCCESS on success; any non-success status may stop or affect iteration depending on provider (behavior unspecified).

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::doall
functions.description: Invoke the callback for all slots managed by the specified slotmem instance. Used to iterate over all allocated slots, typically for initialization, traversal, or inspection.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t obtained from create or attach.
func must be non-NULL and must conform to ap_slotmem_callback_fn_t.
pool must be a valid APR pool for any temporary allocations during iteration.
If the provider was created with AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE, callers must provide external synchronization when calling doall.
The callback must tolerate being called for each slot and return APR_SUCCESS to indicate success.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::create
functions.signature: apr_status_t (*create)(ap_slotmem_instance_t **inst, const char *name, apr_size_t item_size, unsigned int item_num, ap_slotmem_type_t type, apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Create a new slotmem region consisting of item_num slots of size item_size, potentially in shared memory, and return an instance handle in inst. The region may be persisted or require pre-grab semantics depending on type flags.
requirements: inst must be non-NULL and will receive the created instance on success.
name should be a non-NULL, provider-meaningful key used for debugging/sharing.
item_size must be greater than 0.
item_num must be greater than 0.
type is a bitmask of AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_* flags (e.g., PERSIST, NOTMPSAFE, PREGRAB, CLEARINUSE).
pool must be a valid APR pool used for allocations.
If AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE is set, external synchronization is required for multi-thread/process access.
If AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_PERSIST is set, the provider may persist data to the filesystem; semantics of persistence are provider-defined.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::attach
functions.signature: apr_status_t (*attach)(ap_slotmem_instance_t **inst, const char *name, apr_size_t *item_size, unsigned int *item_num, apr_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Attach to an existing slotmem region identified by name, returning an instance handle and reporting the slot size and slot count.
requirements: inst must be non-NULL and will receive the instance on success.
name must be a non-NULL identifier matching an existing slotmem region.
item_size must be a non-NULL pointer that will receive the slot size.
item_num must be a non-NULL pointer that will receive the number of slots.
pool must be a valid APR pool used for allocations.
The targeted region must already exist (e.g., previously created by create) or attach will fail.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::dptr
functions.description: Return a direct pointer to the memory of the specified slot within the instance.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
mem must be non-NULL and will receive the slot pointer on success.
item_id must be within the valid range [0, num_slots(s) - 1].
If the provider was created with AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE, callers must provide external synchronization when accessing the returned pointer.
The returned pointer is to the slot’s storage; the lifetime/validity and concurrency guarantees are provider-dependent.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::get
functions.signature: apr_status_t (*get)(ap_slotmem_instance_t *s, unsigned int item_id, unsigned char *dest, apr_size_t dest_len);
functions.description: Copy the data stored in the specified slot into the destination buffer.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
item_id must be within the valid range [0, num_slots(s) - 1].
dest must be a non-NULL buffer.
dest_len should be at least the slot size (slot_size(s)) to retrieve the full slot contents; otherwise provider behavior is unspecified (inferred from signature).
If the provider was created with AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE, callers must provide external synchronization for concurrent access.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::put
functions.signature: apr_status_t (*put)(ap_slotmem_instance_t *slot, unsigned int item_id, unsigned char *src, apr_size_t src_len);
functions.description: Write the provided data into the specified slot’s storage.
requirements: slot must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
item_id must be within the valid range [0, num_slots(slot) - 1].
src must be a non-NULL buffer containing the data to write.
src_len should be less than or equal to the slot size (slot_size(slot)); excess data cannot be stored (inferred from signature).
If the provider uses AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_PREGRAB semantics, item_id may need to be obtained via grab/fgrab before writing (inferred from type semantics).
If the provider was created with AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE, callers must provide external synchronization for concurrent writes.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::num_slots
functions.description: Return the total number of slots allocated in the slotmem instance.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::num_free_slots
functions.description: Return the number of free (not in-use) slots in the instance. Valid for AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_PREGRAB providers as well as those supporting get/release semantics.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
Meaningful only for providers that track in-use/free state; behavior is provider-defined otherwise (based on comment).

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::slot_size
functions.description: Return the size, in bytes, of each slot in the instance.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::grab
functions.description: Obtain a free slot and mark it as in-use, returning its slot id.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
item_id must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated slot id.
