There must be at least one free slot; otherwise an error status is returned (implied by purpose).
Primarily applicable to providers using pre-grab/in-use semantics (e.g., AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_PREGRAB).
If AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE is set, callers must synchronize concurrent grabs.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::release
functions.description: Release a previously grabbed slot, marking it as no longer in-use.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
item_id must be within the valid range [0, num_slots(s) - 1].
item_id should refer to a currently in-use slot; releasing an already-free slot is invalid (inferred from semantics).
If AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE is set, callers must synchronize concurrent releases.

functions.name: ap_slotmem_provider_t::fgrab
functions.description: Force-grab the specified slot id, marking it as in-use regardless of current state (provider-defined semantics). Useful to claim a known slot explicitly.
requirements: s must be a valid ap_slotmem_instance_t.
item_id must be within the valid range [0, num_slots(s) - 1].
Caller is responsible for ensuring this operation is appropriate for the provider and state; behavior if the slot is already in-use is provider-defined (inferred from comment).
If AP_SLOTMEM_TYPE_NOTMPSAFE is set, callers must synchronize concurrent operations.

functions.name: ap_get_server_revision
functions.description: Populate an ap_version_t with httpd’s numeric version components (major, minor, patch) and an optional add_string. Use to query the running server’s version.
requirements: version must be a valid, writable pointer

functions.name: ap_get_server_banner
functions.description: Return the server banner string suitable for network exposure (honors the ServerTokens directive).

functions.name: ap_get_server_description

functions.name: ap_add_version_component
functions.description: Append a custom component string to the server version/banner/description. Call during startup using the config pool.
requirements: pconf must be a valid pool
component must be a valid string (non-NULL)

functions.name: ap_get_server_built
functions.description: Return the string timestamp describing when the server was built.

functions.name: ap_context_document_root

requirements: r must be a valid request_rec pointer

functions.name: ap_context_prefix
functions.description: Return the URI prefix that maps to the request’s context_document_root.

functions.name: ap_set_context_info
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_set_context_info(request_rec *r, const char *prefix, const char *document_root);
functions.description: Set per-request context_prefix and context_document_root (without trailing slash). If either prefix or document_root is NULL, that property is not modified.

functions.name: ap_field_noparam

requirements: p must be a valid pool

functions.name: ap_getword

line must be a valid pointer to a C-string pointer

functions.name: ap_getword_white

functions.name: ap_getword_white_nc

functions.name: ap_getword_nulls_nc
functions.description: Like ap_getword_nulls() but takes a non-const char** line.

line must be a valid pointer to a mutable C-string pointer

functions.name: ap_getword_conf

functions.name: ap_getword_conf2

line must be a valid pointer to a C-string pointer

functions.name: ap_getword_conf2_nc

functions.name: ap_resolve_env

functions.name: ap_size_list_item

len must be a valid pointer to int

functions.description: Perform a weak ETag comparison for tok within a header field value list. Returns 1 if found, 0 otherwise.
requirements: p must be a valid pool

functions.name: ap_find_etag_strong
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_find_etag_strong(apr_pool_t *p, const char *line, const char *tok);
functions.description: Perform a strong ETag comparison for tok within a header field value list. Returns 1 if found, 0 otherwise.
requirements: p must be a valid pool

functions.name: ap_scan_http_token

functions.name: ap_scan_vchar_obstext

functions.name: ap_parse_token_list_strict

functions.name: ap_get_token

Callers should treat the returned const char* as an error and abort processing of the directive.

functions.name: ap_server_root_relative
functions.description: Return the canonical absolute path for fname relative to the ServerRoot. Absolute paths are returned unchanged.
requirements: p must be a valid pool to allocate the returned string.
fname must be a NUL-terminated path string.
Returned string is allocated from p and valid while p lives.

functions.name: ap_runtime_dir_relative
functions.description: Return a path for a runtime file relative to the configured runtime directory, or return fname unchanged if already absolute.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
fname must be a NUL-terminated path string.
Returned string is allocated from p.

functions.name: ap_state_dir_relative
functions.description: Return a path for persistent state files relative to the configured state directory, or return fname unchanged if absolute.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
fname must be a NUL-terminated path string.
Returned string is allocated from p.

functions.name: ap_add_module
functions.description: Add a module to the server’s module list. Returns NULL on success or an error string on failure. s is the module’s symbol name for logging.
requirements: m must point to a valid module struct to be added.
p must be a pool with lifetime at least as long as the module.
s should be the module’s symbol/name for logs.
Should only be used during (re)configuration when safe to mutate module lists.

functions.name: ap_remove_module
functions.description: Remove a module from the server. This invalidates per-dir and per-server configurations tied to the module’s slot; intended for use during restarts.
requirements: m must be a module currently loaded.
Call only in contexts where invalidating existing configurations is acceptable (e.g., restart), per documentation.

functions.name: ap_add_loaded_module
functions.description: Add a dynamically loaded module to both the chained modules list and the list of loaded modules. Returns NULL on success or an error string.
requirements: mod must be a valid module.
p must be a pool with lifetime matching the module.
s is the module’s symbol name for logging.

functions.name: ap_remove_loaded_module
functions.description: Remove a module from the chained and loaded modules lists.
requirements: mod must refer to a loaded module.
Intended for use during (re)configuration where removal is safe.

functions.name: ap_find_module_name
functions.description: Return the full name of the given module (e.g., "mod_alias.c").
requirements: m must be a valid module pointer.
Return may be NULL if name is unavailable (handle accordingly).

functions.name: ap_find_module_short_name
functions.description: Return the short name of the module identified by module_index, or NULL if not found.
requirements: module_index should refer to a loaded module.
Caller must handle NULL return if not found.

functions.name: ap_find_linked_module
functions.description: Find and return the module with the specified name; NULL if none is linked.
requirements: name must be the module’s name string (e.g., "mod_alias.c" or short form depending on build).
Caller must handle NULL return.

functions.name: ap_pcfg_openfile
functions.description: Open a configuration file and return an ap_configfile_t wrapper for reading via APR-like callbacks.
requirements: ret_cfg must be a non-NULL out-parameter pointer; on success *ret_cfg is set.
p must be a valid pool for allocations.
name must be a valid filename.
Returns APR status code; check for APR_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ap_pcfg_open_custom
functions.signature: ap_configfile_t *ap_pcfg_open_custom(apr_pool_t *p, const char *descr, void *param, apr_status_t (*getc_func)(char *ch, void *param), apr_status_t (*gets_func)(void *buf, apr_size_t bufsiz, void *param), apr_status_t (*close_func)(void *param));
functions.description: Create an ap_configfile_t with user-provided I/O callbacks and context for reading configuration-like streams.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
descr should describe the stream (used as name).
param is passed to callbacks; may be NULL if callbacks accept it.
getc_func, gets_func, and close_func must be valid function pointers implementing the expected semantics (APR-like return codes).
Returned handle is allocated from p.

functions.name: ap_cfg_getline
functions.description: Read one logical line from cfp, trim leading/trailing whitespace, increment line counter. Returns APR status; APR_ENOSPC if buffer too small.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least bufsize bytes.
bufsize must be > 0; if line exceeds bufsize, APR_ENOSPC is returned and buf may contain a partial line.
cfp must be an open ap_configfile_t.
Caller must handle non-APR_SUCCESS, including APR_ENOSPC.

functions.name: ap_cfg_getc
functions.description: Read a single character from cfp, incrementing line number on LF. Returns APR status.
requirements: ch must be a non-NULL pointer to store the read character.
cfp must be an open ap_configfile_t.
Caller must check return code for APR_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ap_cfg_closefile
functions.description: Close the ap_configfile_t by invoking its close handler and detach. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cfp must be a valid, open ap_configfile_t pointer.
Caller must interpret non-1 as failure.

functions.name: ap_pcfg_strerror
functions.description: Convert an APR status code (e.g., from ap_cfg_getline/ap_cfg_getc) to a human-readable string, possibly using cfp context. Returns NULL if rc == APR_SUCCESS.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for string allocation.
cfp may be NULL if not applicable; when provided, used for richer messages.
rc is the status code to describe.
Caller must handle NULL return meaning success.

functions.name: ap_soak_end_container
functions.description: Consume and discard all configuration lines up to the matching closing tag for the given opening directive (e.g., read through </foo>). Returns error string on failure or NULL on success. Uses a lower maximum line length when in .htaccess context (cmd->pool == cmd->temp_pool).
requirements: cmd must be a valid cmd_parms; cmd->pool and cmd->temp_pool determine context.
directive must be the opening directive name to match.
Caller must handle returned error string if non-NULL.

functions.name: ap_build_cont_config
functions.signature: const char *ap_build_cont_config(apr_pool_t *p, apr_pool_t *temp_pool, cmd_parms *parms, ap_directive_t **current, ap_directive_t **curr_parent, const char *orig_directive);
functions.description: Read nested configuration until the matching closing tag for orig_directive and build a configuration tree beneath current/curr_parent. Returns error string on failure or NULL on success. Uses lower max line length in .htaccess context when p == temp_pool.
requirements: p and temp_pool must be valid pools; p is for persistent allocations, temp_pool for temporaries.
parms must be a valid cmd_parms for invoking contained directives.
current and curr_parent must be non-NULL pointers to receive/update the built tree nodes.
orig_directive is the tag to close (e.g., "Directory").
Caller must handle non-NULL error return.

functions.name: ap_build_config
functions.description: Parse a configuration file into a directive tree. Returns error string on error or NULL on success. Uses lower max line length in .htaccess context when conf_pool == temp_pool.
requirements: parms must be initialized for the file to parse (sources set in parms->config_file/->directive as applicable).
conf_pool and temp_pool must be valid pools; conftree must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the root node.
Caller must check return for non-NULL error.

functions.name: ap_walk_config
functions.description: Walk a configuration tree and invoke directive handlers to populate the server’s internal structures. Returns error string on error, NULL otherwise.
requirements: conftree must be a valid configuration tree root (may be NULL to do nothing).
parms must be a valid cmd_parms for this pass.
section_vector is the per-section config vector to populate/merge; must be valid.
Caller must handle non-NULL error return.

functions.name: ap_dir_cfgmatch
functions.signature: ap_dir_match_t *ap_dir_cfgmatch(cmd_parms *cmd, int flags, const char *(*cb)(ap_dir_match_t *w, const char *fname), void *ctx);
functions.description: Create and return an ap_dir_match_t to iterate files matching wildcards for a directive context, invoking cb for each match. Returns a structure allocated from cmd->temp_pool. cb returns NULL on success or an error string per file.
requirements: cmd must be non-NULL and valid; allocation is from cmd->temp_pool.
flags control optional/recursive behavior per documentation; use defined flags as appropriate.
cb must be non-NULL and must follow the signature, returning NULL on success or an error string; caller must handle/report errors.
ctx is an opaque caller context passed to callbacks.

functions.name: ap_check_cmd_context
functions.description: Validate that a directive is used in an allowed context. forbidden is a bitmask of NOT_IN_* flags. Returns NULL if allowed, or an error string if the context is forbidden.
requirements: cmd must reflect the directive’s current context (directory/location/files/virtualhost/etc.).
forbidden must be a combination of the NOT_IN_* flags provided in this header.
Caller must treat non-NULL return as an error and stop processing the directive.

functions.name: ap_single_module_configure
functions.description: Run the specified module’s create_config hooks to initialize its per-server and per-directory configurations.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for allocations.
s must be a valid server_rec.
m must be a valid module pointer whose hooks will be invoked.
Call during server configuration before request processing.

functions.name: ap_setup_prelinked_modules
functions.description: Add all statically prelinked modules to the loaded module list. Returns NULL on success or an error string on failure.
requirements: process must be a valid process_rec for the running server.
Invoke during early server startup before dynamic module loading as needed.

functions.name: ap_show_directives
functions.description: Print to stdout a list of preloaded configuration directives, their help strings, owning modules, and allowed contexts (used for httpd -h).
requirements: Intended for command-line usage (e.g., httpd -h).
Output destination/format is implementation-defined; do not assume reentrancy.

functions.name: ap_exists_directive
functions.description: Return non-zero if a configuration directive of the given name has been registered by any module at the time of the call.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for temporary allocations.
name must be a NUL-terminated directive name string.

functions.name: ap_show_modules
functions.description: Print to stdout the names of preloaded modules (used for httpd -l).
requirements: Intended for command-line usage; output goes to standard output.

functions.name: ap_show_mpm
functions.description: Return the name of the active MPM (Multi-Processing Module) for reporting (e.g., mod_info).
requirements: Caller must handle non-NULL NUL-terminated string; ownership remains with server (do not free).

functions.name: ap_read_config
functions.description: Read all configuration files (starting at config_name), build the configuration tree, and initialize server structures. Returns the head of the server_rec list.
requirements: process must be valid.
temp_pool must be a valid temporary pool for reading/processing.
config_name is the top-level config file path/name.
conftree must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the root of the parsed configuration tree.

functions.name: ap_run_rewrite_args
functions.description: Run the rewrite_args hook for all loaded modules (MPMs may rewrite command line arguments).
requirements: process must be valid.
Modules should have registered hooks prior to invocation.

functions.name: ap_register_hooks
functions.description: Invoke the specified module’s register_hooks function so it can register its hooks with the core using the provided pool.
requirements: m must be a valid module whose register_hooks pointer may be called.
p must be a valid pool for any allocations during hook registration.

functions.name: ap_fixup_virtual_hosts
functions.description: Finalize and normalize the virtual host configuration for the server_rec chain anchored at main_server.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for allocations.
main_server must be the head of the server list.

functions.name: ap_reserve_module_slots
functions.description: Reserve a number of module slots for modules loaded by means other than EXEC_ON_READ directives; to be called in the pre_config stage by relevant modules.
requirements: count must be a non-negative integer.
Call during pre_config stage.

functions.name: ap_reserve_module_slots_directive
functions.description: Reserve module slots according to how often the given non-EXEC_ON_READ directive occurs in the config, by counting uses of the directive and calling ap_reserve_module_slots().
requirements: directive must be the name of a configuration directive to count.
Call during pre_config stage.

functions.name: ap_create_request_config
functions.description: Allocate and return a new configuration vector for request-scoped module configurations.
requirements: p must be a valid pool; the returned vector’s lifetime is tied to p.

functions.name: ap_create_per_dir_config
functions.description: Allocate and return a configuration vector for per-directory module configurations.
requirements: p must be a valid pool; the returned vector’s lifetime is tied to p.

functions.name: ap_merge_per_dir_configs
functions.description: Call each module’s merge_dir_config to merge two per-directory configuration vectors and return the merged result.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for allocations.
base and new_conf must be valid configuration vectors created for the same module layout (compatible module slots).

functions.name: ap_new_log_config
functions.description: Allocate a new ap_logconf and deep-copy fields from old if non-NULL.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
old may be NULL to create a fresh configuration.
Returned pointer is allocated from p.

functions.name: ap_merge_log_config
functions.signature: void ap_merge_log_config(const struct ap_logconf *old_conf, struct ap_logconf *new_conf);
functions.description: Merge old ap_logconf into new ap_logconf. Both must have the same lifetime.
requirements: old_conf and new_conf must be valid pointers.
Both configurations must have compatible structure; they should share the same lifetime (no allocations that outlive them).

functions.name: ap_create_conn_config
functions.description: Allocate and return a configuration vector for connection-scoped module configurations.
requirements: p must be a valid pool; the returned vector’s lifetime is tied to p.

functions.name: ap_parse_htaccess
functions.signature: int ap_parse_htaccess(ap_conf_vector_t **result, request_rec *r, int override, int override_opts, apr_table_t *override_list, const char *path, const char *access_name);
functions.description: Parse an .htaccess file located at path (with possible names from access_name) for the current request, respecting AllowOverride and related options. On success, stores a per-dir config vector in *result and returns a status code.
requirements: result must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the config vector.
r must be a valid request_rec.
override and override_opts must reflect the active AllowOverride settings.
override_list is the table of directives allowed with AllowOverrideList; may be NULL if not used.
path must be the directory path to search for the htaccess file.
access_name is the list of possible .htaccess filenames (implementation-defined, often a single name).
Returns an int status for the current request; callers must interpret per core semantics.

functions.name: ap_init_virtual_host
functions.signature: const char *ap_init_virtual_host(apr_pool_t *p, const char *hostname, server_rec *main_server, server_rec **ps);
functions.description: Initialize a virtual host for the given hostname under the main_server, allocating a new server_rec and returning it via ps. Returns NULL on success or an error string.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
hostname must be a valid host string.
main_server must be a valid server_rec for this configuration.
ps must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive the new server_rec.
Caller must handle non-NULL error string.

functions.name: ap_process_resource_config
functions.signature: const char *ap_process_resource_config(server_rec *s, const char *fname, ap_directive_t **conftree, apr_pool_t *p, apr_pool_t *ptemp);
functions.description: Process a single configuration resource file fname, building a directive tree in *conftree. Returns error string on failure or NULL on success.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec for context.
fname must be a valid file path or pattern (see also ap_process_fnmatch_configs).
conftree must be a non-NULL out-parameter.
p and ptemp must be valid pools; ptemp is for temporaries.
Caller must handle returned error string.

functions.name: ap_process_fnmatch_configs
functions.signature: const char *ap_process_fnmatch_configs(server_rec *s, const char *fname, ap_directive_t **conftree, apr_pool_t *p, apr_pool_t *ptemp, int optional);
functions.description: Process all files matching the pattern fname as configuration files, building/merging into *conftree. If optional is non-zero, a no-match is not an error. Returns error string or NULL.
requirements: s must be valid.
fname must be a pattern supported by apr_fnmatch.
conftree must be a non-NULL out-parameter.
p and ptemp must be valid pools.
optional controls whether no matches are treated as an error (0) or not (non-zero).

functions.name: ap_process_config_tree
functions.description: Execute/interpret the directives in conftree to configure server s. Returns OK (or other status) indicating success/failure.
requirements: s must be valid.
conftree may be NULL to indicate nothing to process.
p and ptemp must be valid pools.
Caller must handle non-OK returns as errors.

functions.name: ap_retained_data_create
functions.description: Allocate zero-initialized retained memory of given size under a unique key that survives module unload/load cycles.
requirements: key must be a unique identifier string for the retained data.
size is the number of bytes to allocate; must be > 0 to allocate meaningful storage.
Returns a pointer to the retained block; lifetime is managed by the core; do not free.

functions.name: ap_retained_data_get
functions.description: Retrieve previously created retained data by key, or NULL if not found.
requirements: key must be the exact key used with ap_retained_data_create.
Caller must handle NULL if not previously created.

functions.name: ap_invoke_handler
functions.description: Run the handler phase across modules until one handles the request. Returns the resulting HTTP status.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec with a selected handler/phase context.
Caller must handle the returned status code per HTTPd semantics.

functions.name: ap_find_command
functions.description: Search a command_rec table for a directive by name and return its definition, or NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be a NUL-terminated directive name.
cmds must point to a valid, NULL-terminated command table or similar iterable per core conventions.
Caller must handle NULL return.

functions.name: ap_find_command_in_modules
functions.description: Search the linked list of modules for a directive and return the command_rec defining it. *mod is updated to point to the module providing the directive. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: cmd_name must be a NUL-terminated directive name.
mod must be a non-NULL in/out pointer to the starting module; on return, set to the module containing the directive if found.
Caller must handle NULL return when directive is absent.

functions.name: ap_set_config_vectors
functions.signature: void *ap_set_config_vectors(server_rec *server, ap_conf_vector_t *section_vector, const char *section, module *mod, apr_pool_t *pconf);
functions.description: Ask a module to create per-server and per-section (dir/loc/file) configuration data if not already created, storing results in server->module_config and section_vector. Returns the (new) per-section config.
requirements: server must be valid.
section_vector must be a valid configuration vector for the current section.
section is the section name (e.g., "Directory"), used for context.
mod must be a valid module to initialize.
pconf must be a valid pool for configuration allocations.

functions.name: ap_open_htaccess
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_open_htaccess(request_rec *r, const char *dir_name, const char *access_name, ap_configfile_t **conffile, const char **full_name);
functions.description: Core internal function (use ap_run_open_htaccess via hook) to open an htaccess file for directory dir_name with candidate filename access_name. Returns APR_SUCCESS, APR_ENOENT/APR_ENOTDIR if none, AP_DECLINED to defer, or another error code on failure. Also returns the opened ap_configfile_t and the full file name.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
dir_name must be a valid directory path.
access_name must be the htaccess filename to look for.
conffile and full_name must be non-NULL out-parameters; on APR_SUCCESS, *conffile and *full_name are set.
Caller must check and handle APR status codes as documented.

functions.name: ap_pool_cleanup_set_null
functions.description: Generic pool cleanup callback that sets the pointer located at data to NULL. Always returns APR_SUCCESS.
requirements: data must point to a pointer variable (i.e., void **), whose contents will be set to NULL when the cleanup runs.
Register with apr_pool_cleanup_register as a cleanup for pointers that should be nulled on pool cleanup.

functions.name: ap_process_connection
functions.description: Protocol driver that runs all pre-connection and connection hooks for all protocol modules on the given connection. Typically invoked by the server once a connection is accepted; modules may inspect/setup filters and then process the connection using the appropriate protocol.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record (conn_rec*) for an active connection.
csd is the accepted I/O mechanism for the connection (commonly an apr_socket_t*), and must be valid for I/O as determined by the accepting module.
Should be called by the server framework; not intended to be called multiple times for the same live connection.

functions.name: ap_shutdown_conn
functions.description: Shuts down the connection for writing. Optionally flushes any pending outbound data before shutting down, then disables further writes on the connection.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record for an open connection.
flush is treated as a boolean flag: 0 = do not flush, non-zero = flush pending data before shutdown.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for success or the underlying error and handle failures accordingly.
After successful shutdown for writing, the caller must not attempt further write operations on this connection.

functions.name: ap_flush_conn
functions.description: Flushes all remaining data in the client send buffer for the connection and initiates a write-side shutdown. This is a convenience wrapper that calls ap_shutdown_conn(c, 1).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record for an open connection.
After calling, the connection is shut down for writing; callers must not perform further writes.

functions.name: ap_lingering_close
functions.description: Performs a lingering close on the connection: reads from the client until EOF or a timeout (MAX_SECS_TO_LINGER) to avoid TCP RSTs that might otherwise truncate the response on the client side.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record.
Should be called when closing a connection after response delivery to drain the client side input per lingering close semantics.

functions.name: ap_prep_lingering_close
functions.description: Prepares the connection for a lingering close. Exact actions and return semantics are not documented here; typically used internally to transition the connection to a state suitable for lingering close.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record.
Return value semantics are not documented in this header; callers must consult implementation or higher-level API for meaning.

functions.name: ap_start_lingering_close
functions.description: Starts the lingering close procedure on the connection. Exact steps and return semantics are not specified in this header.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record.
Return value semantics are not documented in this header; callers must consult implementation or higher-level API for meaning.

functions.name: ap_pre_connection
functions.description: Wrapper around ap_run_pre_connection: runs pre-connection hooks, marks the connection aborted on error, and ensures core basic connection setup is completed if not already. Returns the hook result.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized connection record.
csd must be the valid I/O mechanism for this connection (commonly an apr_socket_t*).
Caller must check the return value (OK/DECLINED/error code per hook conventions) and handle non-OK appropriately.

functions.name: ap_create_connection
functions.signature: conn_rec *ap_create_connection(apr_pool_t *p, server_rec *server, apr_socket_t *csd, long conn_id, void *sbh, apr_bucket_alloc_t *alloc, unsigned int outgoing);
functions.description: Creates a new server/incoming or client/outgoing (proxy) connection record with the provided resources and identifiers.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool used for allocating the connection record and its resources.
server must be a valid server_rec associated with this connection.
csd must be the accepted socket for the connection (incoming) or the socket to use (outgoing).
conn_id must be unique at the time of creation (not necessarily globally unique forever).
sbh must be a valid scoreboard handle for this connection, as provided by the server framework.
alloc must be a valid APR bucket allocator for all bucket/brigade allocations.
outgoing must be a boolean 0 or 1; if not 0/1, the function returns NULL.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.

functions.name: ap_create_secondary_connection
functions.description: Creates a new secondary connection associated with a given master connection, using the provided pool and bucket allocator. Useful for multiplexing or protocol layering that requires additional conn_rec instances tied to a master.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool for allocating the secondary connection.
master must be a valid, initialized master conn_rec to which this secondary connection belongs.
alloc must be a valid APR bucket allocator.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL before use.

functions.name: ap_bucket_eoc_make
functions.description: Converts the given bucket into an End Of Connection (EOC) bucket, signaling that the connection will be closed when this bucket is processed.
requirements: b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket instance suitable for reinitialization as an EOC bucket.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure) before inserting/using the bucket in a brigade.
Processing an EOC bucket indicates connection closure semantics; filters/consumers should not expect further data on the connection.

functions.name: ap_bucket_eoc_create
functions.description: Creates a new End Of Connection (EOC) bucket from the given bucket allocator freelist. Insertion of this bucket into a brigade indicates that the connection will be closed.
requirements: list must be a valid apr_bucket_alloc_t* allocator (freelist) from which the bucket can be allocated.
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure) before use.
Consumers encountering an EOC bucket should treat the connection as closing and not expect further data.

functions.name: ap_allow_options
functions.description: Returns the Options bitmask (OPT_*) in effect for the current request r. Use to test directory-level options within modules/handlers.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec for the current request lifecycle.

functions.name: ap_allow_overrides
functions.description: Returns the AllowOverride/AllowOverrideList bitmask in effect for the current request r. Useful to determine which .htaccess directives are permitted.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.

functions.name: ap_document_root
functions.description: Returns the server’s document root for request r. Warning in docs: not reliable when UserDir or similar rewrites are involved; kept for backward compatibility.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
Callers should not rely on this when Userdir or similar mappings apply (may not reflect the effective filesystem path).

functions.name: ap_get_useragent_host
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(const char *) ap_get_useragent_host(request_rec *req, int type, int *str_is_ip);
functions.description: Returns the remote user-agent’s hostname or IP associated with req->useragent_ip, according to lookup type (REMOTE_HOST/NAME/NOLOOKUP/DOUBLE_REV). Optionally sets *str_is_ip non-zero when an IP string is returned.
requirements: req must be a valid request_rec.
type must be one of REMOTE_HOST, REMOTE_NAME, REMOTE_NOLOOKUP, or REMOTE_DOUBLE_REV.
str_is_ip may be NULL; if non-NULL it will be set on output.
Return may be NULL if lookups fail (per the selected type).

functions.name: ap_get_remote_host
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(const char *) ap_get_remote_host(conn_rec *conn, void *dir_config, int type, int *str_is_ip);
functions.description: Returns the remote client’s hostname or IP based on the connection client_ip, honoring the provided per-dir config and lookup type. Optionally indicates if the returned string is an IP.
requirements: conn must be a valid connection record (conn_rec*).
dir_config should be the directory config vector from the request (may be NULL depending on usage).
type must be REMOTE_HOST, REMOTE_NAME, REMOTE_NOLOOKUP, or REMOTE_DOUBLE_REV.
str_is_ip may be NULL; if non-NULL it will be set on output.
Return may be NULL if lookups fail (per the selected type).

functions.name: ap_get_remote_logname
functions.description: Retrieves the remote user’s login name (ident), if determinable for request r; otherwise undefined/NULL.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
Return can be NULL if the remote logname cannot be determined.

functions.name: ap_construct_url
functions.description: Builds a fully qualified absolute URL from a path/URI and information in request r (scheme, host, port). The string is allocated from pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid apr_pool_t for result allocation.
uri must be a non-NULL path/URI string.
r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_server_name
functions.description: Returns the server name for request r (considering UseCanonicalName and host header processing).
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_server_name_for_url
functions.description: Returns the server name formatted for use in a URL for request r. If it is an IPv6 literal, it is returned in URL format with brackets, e.g. "[fe80::1]".
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_server_port
functions.description: Returns the effective server port for request r.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec pointer.

functions.name: ap_get_read_buf_size
functions.description: Returns the configured size of read buffers for the given request.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_limit_req_body
functions.description: Returns the configured limit on bytes allowed in the request message body for the given request.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_limit_xml_body
functions.description: Returns the configured limit on bytes allowed in an XML request body for the given request.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_custom_response
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_custom_response(request_rec *r, int status, const char *string);
functions.description: Installs a custom response for the given HTTP status on request r. The string may be a literal message, a filesystem path, or a URL.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
status must be a valid HTTP status code handled by httpd.
string must be a non-NULL pointer to a message, file path, or URL understood by httpd.

functions.name: ap_is_recursion_limit_exceeded
functions.description: Checks whether the request has exceeded the configured maximum for internal redirects or subrequest depth. Returns non-zero if exceeded.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_exists_config_define
functions.description: Checks whether a -D name was defined on the server’s command line or in the environment. Returns 1 if defined, 0 otherwise.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, non-empty string.

functions.name: ap_core_translate
functions.description: Core translate-name hook implementation: maps the request URI in r to a filename (filesystem path). Returns status code (typically HTTP status/OK).
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec with URI set.
Caller should handle the returned status (non-OK indicates an error in mapping).

functions.name: ap_auth_type
functions.description: Returns the authentication type (e.g., "Basic", "Digest") required for this request, if any.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
Return may be NULL if no auth type is set.

functions.name: ap_auth_name
functions.description: Returns the authentication realm name required for this request, if any.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
Return may be NULL if no auth realm is set.

functions.name: ap_satisfies
functions.description: Returns how authorization/Access control requirements must be met for request r: SATISFY_ANY, SATISFY_ALL, or SATISFY_NOSPEC.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_get_core_module_config
functions.description: Efficient accessor for core_module configuration in a configuration vector cv (equivalent to ap_get_module_config(cv, &core_module)).
requirements: cv must be a valid configuration vector (e.g., r->per_dir_config or s->module_config).
Returns module-specific data pointer, which may be NULL if not set.

functions.name: ap_set_core_module_config
functions.description: Efficient setter for core_module configuration in a configuration vector cv (equivalent to ap_set_module_config(cv, &core_module, val)).
requirements: cv must be a valid configuration vector to modify.
val is the value to store; may be NULL to clear depending on usage.

functions.name: ap_get_conn_socket
functions.description: Returns the APR socket associated with connection c from the core network filter. Preferred over accessing core connection config directly.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec.
Return may be NULL if no socket is associated (e.g., non-socket transports).

functions.name: ap_register_request_note
functions.description: Reserves and returns an index in core_request_config->notes for per-request custom data. Use with ap_get_request_note() to access the slot.
requirements: Must be called during initialization to register a notes slot (as documented).
Returned key is used later during request processing with ap_get_request_note().

functions.name: ap_get_request_note
functions.description: Returns a pointer-to-pointer handle to the note slot identified by note_num in the current request r. Initially each note element is NULL; caller can store a pointer that remains valid for the life of the request.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
note_num must be a valid index (from ap_register_request_note() or AP_NOTE_*).
Returns NULL if note_num is invalid.
Any structure stored by the caller must live at least as long as the request.

functions.name: ap_add_output_filters_by_type
functions.description: Applies configured output filters by content type for the given request.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.

functions.name: ap_core_reorder_directories
functions.description: Reorders per-dir configuration sections for the server during config processing. Used internally by http_config.c.
requirements: Must be called with a valid APR pool and server_rec.
Intended for internal/core use during configuration processing.

functions.name: ap_add_per_dir_conf
functions.description: Adds a per-directory configuration record to server s.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec.
dir_config must point to a valid per-dir config structure for the core.

functions.name: ap_add_per_url_conf
functions.description: Adds a per-URL configuration record to server s.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec.
url_config must be a valid per-URL config structure.

functions.name: ap_add_file_conf
functions.description: Adds a per-file configuration (within a directory/section) using pool p, updating core_dir_config conf with url_config.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool.
conf must be a valid core_dir_config pointer.
url_config must be a valid related config structure.

functions.name: ap_add_if_conf
functions.description: Adds an <If>/<ElseIf>/<Else> conditional per-dir configuration block; returns NULL on success or an error message string on failure.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool.
conf must be a valid core_dir_config pointer.
url_config must be a valid conditional section config structure.
Caller must check the returned const char* for an error message (non-NULL indicates an error).

functions.name: ap_limit_section
functions.signature: AP_CORE_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_limit_section(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Implements the <Limit> configuration section directive. Returns NULL on success or an error message on failure.
requirements: cmd must be a valid cmd_parms pointer from config parsing.
arg is the directive argument string.
Caller must check the return value: non-NULL indicates an error message.

functions.name: ap_get_server_protocol
functions.description: Returns the protocol string (e.g., "HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/2") configured or negotiated for server s.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec.
Return may be NULL if not set.

functions.name: ap_set_server_protocol
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_set_server_protocol(server_rec* s, const char* proto);
functions.description: Sets the server protocol string for server s to proto.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec.
proto should be a non-NULL protocol string understood by httpd/modules.

functions.name: insert_network_bucket
functions.description: Hook callback for inserting a network bucket into the core input filter’s brigade for a connection. Intended for MPMs or protocol modules that need special socket setup. Implementations should wrap the provided socket into an appropriate bucket and insert it into bb for the given connection c. Return AP_DECLINED if not handled, APR_SUCCESS on success, or an APR error code on failure.
requirements: c must be a valid, active conn_rec for which input is being set up.
bb must be a valid, non-NULL apr_bucket_brigade into which the network bucket will be inserted.
socket must be a valid apr_socket_t to be wrapped and inserted.
Return AP_DECLINED if the implementation does not handle this connection; return APR_SUCCESS on success; otherwise return an APR error status.
Implementations are typically registered via ap_hook_insert_network_bucket and will be invoked through ap_run_insert_network_bucket(c, bb, socket).

functions.name: get_mgmt_items
functions.description: Hook callback for modules to provide management/metrics items describing operational status. Implementations populate ht (keys are item names, values are ap_mgmt_item_t*) using pool p. The val parameter is a tree-structured selector (e.g., "*", "module.*", "module.foo.*", "module.foo.bar") indicating which items are requested.
requirements: p is a pool to allocate any returned items or auxiliary data; items stored in ht should remain valid for the caller’s use.
val specifies the requested item(s) using a tree-like path; implementations should honor the selector when possible.
ht must be a valid apr_hash_t into which results are inserted (keys are item names; values point to ap_mgmt_item_t structures).
Return an int status (conventionally nonzero for success/handled); exact semantics beyond population of ht are unspecified by this header.

functions.name: ap_register_errorlog_handler
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_register_errorlog_handler(apr_pool_t *p, char *tag, ap_errorlog_handler_fn_t *handler, int flags);
functions.description: Registers an external error log handler for %tag in the error log format with the given handler function.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool (configuration scope).
tag must be a single-character (format specifier) tag string.
handler must be a valid function pointer of type ap_errorlog_handler_fn_t.
flags are reserved; per docs should be set to 0.

functions.name: error_log
functions.description: Hook to log error messages using external handlers. Implementations receive context in info and the unformatted error message in errstr, and should emit the log entry accordingly. Handlers may be used by the core to route messages to alternative sinks.
requirements: info may reference server, connection, request and other context; any pointer within info may be NULL and must be checked before use.
errstr is the unformatted message to log and may be empty or non-NULL per caller behavior.
Allocating from the usual pools (info->pool, connection pool, or request pool) must be avoided to prevent leaks; use a transient subpool if allocation is necessary.

functions.name: ap_register_log_hooks
functions.description: Registers core logging hooks and providers during server startup using pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool (typically the process or config pool).

functions.name: ap_register_config_hooks
functions.description: Registers core configuration hooks during server startup using pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool (typically the process or config pool).

functions.name: ap_ident_lookup
functions.description: Optional function provided by mod_ident (when loaded) to perform an RFC 1413 ident lookup for a request. Returns an identifier string or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec.
The function may be absent if mod_ident is not loaded; callers must retrieve it with APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(ap_ident_lookup) and handle NULL.

functions.name: authz_some_auth_required
functions.description: Optional function provided by mod_authz_core (when loaded) that indicates whether any authorization is required for the given request. Returns non-zero if some auth is required, zero otherwise.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec.
The function may be absent if mod_authz_core is not loaded; retrieve with APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(authz_some_auth_required) and handle NULL.

functions.name: authn_ap_auth_type
functions.description: Optional function provided by mod_authn_* stack (when loaded) to retrieve the configured authentication type (e.g., Basic, Digest) for the request.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec.
The function may be absent if the providing module is not loaded; retrieve with APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(authn_ap_auth_type) and handle NULL.
Return value may be NULL if no auth type is configured.

functions.name: authn_ap_auth_name
functions.description: Optional function provided by mod_authn_* stack (when loaded) to retrieve the configured authentication realm (AuthName) for the request.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec.
The function may be absent if the providing module is not loaded; retrieve with APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(authn_ap_auth_name) and handle NULL.
Return value may be NULL if no auth name/realm is configured.

functions.name: access_compat_ap_satisfies
functions.description: Optional function provided by mod_access_compat (when loaded) that returns the satisfy policy (e.g., whether any or all requirements must be met) for the request, for compatibility with older access control directives.
requirements: r must point to a valid, initialized request_rec.
The function may be absent if mod_access_compat is not loaded; retrieve with APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(access_compat_ap_satisfies) and handle NULL.

functions.name: ap_state_query
functions.description: Queries the server state by query_code. Returns an integer value or AP_SQ_NOT_SUPPORTED for unknown codes. See AP_SQ_* constants for codes and return values.
requirements: query_code must be one of the AP_SQ_* codes (e.g., AP_SQ_MAIN_STATE, AP_SQ_RUN_MODE, AP_SQ_CONFIG_GEN).
Caller must interpret the returned value based on the query_code.

functions.name: ap_create_slave_connection
functions.description: Creates a slave (secondary) connection derived from primary connection c and returns its conn_rec.
requirements: c must be a valid primary conn_rec.
Caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned slave connection.

functions.name: get_pollfd_from_conn
functions.description: Hook callback to provide a pollable descriptor for connection input. Implementations populate pfd->desc_type and pfd->desc with a suitable descriptor for polling input on connection c and, if ptimeout is not NULL, set the effective timeout. For primary connections this is typically the socket; for secondary connections it may differ or be unavailable.
requirements: c must be a valid connection (primary or secondary).
pfd must be non-NULL and will be populated with a descriptor and descriptor type appropriate for polling connection input; APR_NO_DESC may be set if input is already closed.
If ptimeout is not NULL, set it to the timeout in effect for the provided descriptor.
Return APR_SUCCESS when pfd (and optionally ptimeout) are assigned; return APR_ENOTIMPL if not supported for this connection; otherwise return an appropriate APR error code.

functions.name: ap_get_pollfd_from_conn
functions.description: Populates pfd->desc_type and pfd->desc with a suitable descriptor for polling connection input, and optionally returns the timeout. For primary connections it's typically the socket; for secondary connections it may differ. May set APR_NO_DESC to indicate input already closed.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec.
pfd must be a valid pointer to an apr_pollfd_t to receive descriptor info.
ptimeout may be NULL; if non-NULL, receives the timeout in effect.
Returns APR_SUCCESS on success; caller must check status.

functions.name: ap_open_stderr_log
functions.description: Initialize Apache logging to write to stderr. Typically called during early server startup to ensure a valid logging sink is available.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool

functions.name: ap_replace_stderr_log
functions.description: Redirect stderr output to the given file. Used to replace stderr with a persistent error log file.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
file must point to a valid filename; if creation/open fails, a non-APR_SUCCESS status is returned

functions.name: ap_open_logs
functions.description: Open the server’s error logs and replace stderr with the main error log. Core-internal startup routine, not intended for module use.
requirements: pconf, plog, ptemp must be valid APR pools
s_main must be a valid main server_rec
Intended as an internal core function; modules should not call it

functions.name: ap_logs_child_init
functions.description: Child-process initialization for piped loggers in MPM children. Core-internal routine executed in child context.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
s must be a valid server_rec
Not intended for module use; internal core function

functions.name: ap_log_error
functions.signature: void ap_log_error(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const server_rec *s, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Log a message not tied to a specific request or connection to the error log. Implemented as a macro that gates by log level and calls ap_log_error_. Use APLOG_MARK for file/line/module and a printf-like fmt string.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and varargs must match
Do not include untrusted/raw network data in fmt; use "%s" with separate arguments instead
level should be an APLOG_* value
If a request_rec is available, prefer ap_log_rerror; if a conn_rec is available, prefer ap_log_cerror

functions.name: ap_log_error_
functions.signature: void ap_log_error_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const server_rec *s, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf,7,8)));
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_error. Emits a formatted log message for server context after any log-level checks performed by the macro wrapper.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string corresponding to arguments
file and line should indicate the call site (typically via APLOG_MARK)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Avoid embedding untrusted data in fmt; pass it as arguments and use "%s"

functions.name: ap_log_perror
functions.signature: void ap_log_perror(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, apr_pool_t *p, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Log a message not tied to request, connection, or virtual server. Implemented as a macro that may compile-time-elide messages above APLOG_MAX_LOGLEVEL and calls ap_log_perror_.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and varargs must match
Do not include untrusted/raw network data in fmt; use "%s" with separate arguments
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index

functions.name: ap_log_perror_
functions.signature: void ap_log_perror_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, apr_pool_t *p, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf,7,8)));
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_perror. Logs a formatted message associated with an APR pool context.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching arguments
file and line should come from the call site (APLOG_MARK)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Avoid embedding untrusted data in fmt; pass it as arguments

functions.name: ap_log_rerror
functions.signature: void ap_log_rerror(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const request_rec *r, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Log a message associated with a specific request. Implemented as a macro that gates by per-module/request log level and calls ap_log_rerror_.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and varargs must match
Do not include untrusted/raw network data in fmt; use "%s" with separate arguments
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index

functions.name: ap_log_rerror_
functions.signature: void ap_log_rerror_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const request_rec *r, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf,7,8)));
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_rerror. Emits a formatted log message tied to a request after macro-level filtering.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching arguments
file and line should reflect call site (APLOG_MARK)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Avoid embedding untrusted data in fmt

functions.name: ap_log_cerror
functions.signature: void ap_log_cerror(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const conn_rec *c, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Log a message associated with a specific connection. Implemented as a macro that gates by per-module/connection log level and calls ap_log_cerror_. Prefer ap_log_rerror if a request_rec exists.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and varargs must match
Do not include untrusted/raw network data in fmt; use "%s" with separate arguments
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index
Prefer ap_log_rerror when a request_rec is available

functions.name: ap_log_cerror_
functions.signature: void ap_log_cerror_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const conn_rec *c, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf,7,8)));
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_cerror. Emits a formatted log message tied to a connection after macro-level filtering.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching arguments
file and line should reflect call site (APLOG_MARK)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Avoid embedding untrusted data in fmt

functions.name: ap_log_cserror
functions.signature: void ap_log_cserror(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const conn_rec *c, const server_rec *s, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Log a message associated with a connection and a vhost other than c->base_server. Implemented as a macro that gates by per-module/conn+server log level and calls ap_log_cserror_. Useful before a request_rec exists (e.g., in mod_ssl).
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec
s must be the target server_rec (vhost)
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string and varargs must match
Do not include untrusted/raw network data in fmt; use "%s" with separate arguments
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index
Prefer ap_log_rerror when a request_rec is available

functions.name: ap_log_cserror_
functions.signature: void ap_log_cserror_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, apr_status_t status, const conn_rec *c, const server_rec *s, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf,8,9)));
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_cserror. Emits a formatted log message tied to a connection and explicit server (vhost) after macro-level filtering.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec
s must be a valid server_rec
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching arguments
file and line should reflect call site (APLOG_MARK)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Avoid embedding untrusted data in fmt

functions.name: ap_log_data
functions.signature: void ap_log_data(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const server_rec *s, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Log an arbitrary memory buffer (printable plus hex) not tied to a specific request/connection. Implemented as a macro that gates by log level and calls ap_log_data_.
requirements: label should be a printable description
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes (if len > 0)
len is the number of bytes to log
flags is a bitmask of AP_LOG_DATA_* values (e.g., AP_LOG_DATA_SHOW_OFFSET)
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index

functions.name: ap_log_data_
functions.signature: void ap_log_data_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const server_rec *s, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_data. Logs a buffer with printable and hex representation, optionally showing offsets.
requirements: label should be descriptive text
data must be valid for len bytes (if len > 0)
len specifies the buffer size to log
flags uses AP_LOG_DATA_* constants
file and line should reflect call site
level should be an APLOG_* value

functions.name: ap_log_rdata
functions.signature: void ap_log_rdata(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const request_rec *r, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Log a buffer associated with a specific request. Implemented as a macro that gates by per-module/request log level and calls ap_log_rdata_.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
data must be valid for len bytes (if len > 0)
label should describe the buffer
len is the number of bytes to log
flags is a bitmask of AP_LOG_DATA_* values
level should be an APLOG_* value
Use APLOG_MARK to supply file/line/module_index

functions.name: ap_log_rdata_
functions.signature: void ap_log_rdata_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const request_rec *r, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_rdata. Logs a printable+hex dump of a buffer in the context of a request.
requirements: r must be valid
data must be valid for len bytes
label should describe content
len specifies number of bytes to log
flags uses AP_LOG_DATA_* constants
file and line should reflect call site
level should be an APLOG_* value

functions.name: ap_log_cdata
functions.signature: void ap_log_cdata(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const conn_rec *c, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Log a buffer associated with a specific connection. Implemented as a macro that gates by per-module/connection log level and calls ap_log_cdata_.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec
data must be valid for len bytes (if len > 0)
label should describe the buffer
len is the number of bytes to log
flags is a bitmask of AP_LOG_DATA_* values
level should be an APLOG_* value

functions.name: ap_log_cdata_
functions.signature: void ap_log_cdata_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const conn_rec *c, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);

data must be valid for len bytes
label should describe content
len specifies number of bytes to log
flags uses AP_LOG_DATA_* constants

level should be an APLOG_* value

functions.name: ap_log_csdata
functions.signature: void ap_log_csdata(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const conn_rec *c, const server_rec *s, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);

label should describe the buffer

functions.signature: void ap_log_csdata_(const char *file, int line, int module_index, int level, const conn_rec *c, const server_rec *s, const char *label, const void *data, apr_size_t len, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Underlying implementation for ap_log_csdata. Logs a printable+hex dump of a buffer for a connection and specific server (vhost).

s must be valid
data must be valid for len bytes
label should describe content
len specifies number of bytes to log
flags uses AP_LOG_DATA_* constants

functions.name: ap_error_log2stderr
functions.description: Redirect (convert) the error log to stderr for the given server context.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec

functions.name: ap_log_command_line
functions.description: Log the command line used to start the server to the specified server’s error log.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
s must be a valid server_rec

functions.name: ap_log_mpm_common
functions.description: Log commonly useful MPM-related shared data at startup to the server’s error log.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec

functions.name: ap_log_pid
functions.description: Write the parent process’s current PID to a pidfile. If fname is not absolute it is relative to DefaultRuntimeDir.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
fname must be a writable path; if not absolute it is interpreted relative to DefaultRuntimeDir

functions.name: ap_remove_pid
functions.description: Remove (unlink) the pidfile at the given path. If not absolute, the path is relative to DefaultRuntimeDir.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
fname must reference the pidfile path; if not absolute it is interpreted relative to DefaultRuntimeDir

functions.name: ap_read_pid
functions.description: Read a PID from the specified pidfile into mypid. If filename is not absolute it is relative to DefaultRuntimeDir.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
filename must refer to an existing pidfile; if not absolute it is interpreted relative to DefaultRuntimeDir
mypid must be a non-NULL pointer; it is valid only when the function returns APR_SUCCESS

functions.name: ap_open_piped_log
functions.description: Start a piped log helper process running the specified program and return its piped_log handle. The program is invoked as APR_PROGRAM_ENV.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
program must be a valid executable/specification for APR to run

functions.name: ap_open_piped_log_ex
functions.signature: piped_log * ap_open_piped_log_ex(apr_pool_t *p, const char *program, apr_cmdtype_e cmdtype);
functions.description: Start a piped log helper process running program using the specified invocation method (e.g., APR_PROGRAM, APR_SHELLCMD_ENV) and return its piped_log handle.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool
program must be a valid executable/specification
cmdtype must be a valid apr_cmdtype_e specifying how to invoke program

functions.name: ap_close_piped_log
functions.description: Close the piped log and terminate the helper logging process.
requirements: pl must be a valid piped_log handle returned by ap_open_piped_log/_ex

functions.name: ap_piped_log_read_fd
functions.description: Return the APR file handle for the read end of the piped log’s pipe.
requirements: pl must be a valid piped_log handle

functions.name: ap_piped_log_write_fd
functions.description: Return the APR file handle for the write end of the piped log’s pipe.
requirements: pl must be a valid piped_log handle

functions.name: generate_log_id
functions.signature: int generate_log_id(const conn_rec *c, const request_rec *r, const char **id);
functions.description: Hook: generate a unique log identifier for a connection or request. Modules may implement this hook to set *id to a unique string. Returns OK or DECLINE.
requirements: c is the current connection (non-NULL for connection-level IDs)
r may be NULL; when non-NULL, may be used to influence/generate the ID
id must be a non-NULL pointer to a const char* location where the hook stores the generated ID when returning OK
Return value should be OK on success or DECLINE to let other hooks/default handling proceed

functions.name: ap_signal_server
functions.description: Optional APR function that sends a control signal to the server when the '-k' command-line option is used. Callers typically retrieve it via APR's optional function mechanism and, if available, invoke it to signal a running server process; the function stores an exit status in the provided integer pointer. Usage context is command-line control of the server lifecycle rather than per-request handling. Return value semantics are not documented here.
requirements: status must be a valid, non-null pointer to int where the function can store the resulting exit status.
pool must be a valid, initialized apr_pool_t* suitable for any allocations performed by the function.
This is an optional function; callers should obtain it via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(ap_signal_server) and must check for NULL before calling.
Intended to be used in the context of handling the '-k' command-line option to control the server; not typically called during normal request processing.

functions.name: ap_old_write_filter
functions.description: Output filter that emulates the legacy ap_r* write behavior by writing a brigade downstream. Intended for backward compatibility in modules relying on old write semantics.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter instance in the request/connection filter chain.
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade containing the data to forward.

functions.name: ap_old_write_filter
functions.description: Output filter that emulates the legacy ap_r* write behavior by writing a brigade downstream. Intended for backward compatibility in modules relying on old write semantics.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter instance in the request/connection filter chain.
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade containing the data to forward.

functions.name: ap_create_request
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new, empty request_rec associated with the given connection, setting reasonable defaults.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized conn_rec representing the current client connection.

functions.name: ap_read_request
functions.description: Read and parse an HTTP request from the connection and return a populated request_rec.
requirements: c must be a valid, connected conn_rec ready for input.
Must be called when a new request line is available on the connection (e.g., request loop).

functions.name: ap_assign_request_line
functions.signature: int ap_assign_request_line(request_rec *r, const char *method, const char *uri, const char *protocol);
functions.description: Assign the method, request URI, and protocol (first line components) to an existing request_rec. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
method, uri, and protocol should be valid null-terminated strings representing an HTTP method/URI/protocol.
Caller must check the return value and handle failure (0).

functions.name: ap_h1_tokenize_request_line
functions.signature: int ap_h1_tokenize_request_line(request_rec *r, const char *line, const char **pmethod, const char **puri, const char **pprotocol);
functions.description: Parse and validate an HTTP/1.x request line into method, URI, and protocol components. On success, outputs pointers to the components and returns 1.
requirements: r must be valid.
line must point to a full HTTP/1.x request-line (without CRLF).
pmethod, puri, pprotocol must be non-NULL if the corresponding output is expected.
Caller must check return code (1=success, 0=failure).

functions.name: ap_parse_request_line
functions.description: Parse and validate the request line from the input filter(s) into r’s method, uri, and protocol. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: r must be valid and associated with a connection/input filters ready to supply the request line.
Caller must check return value and handle failure.

functions.name: ap_check_request_header
functions.description: Validate the request headers and select the appropriate virtual host for the request. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec with headers read (e.g., after ap_get_mime_headers).
Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: ap_get_mime_headers
functions.description: Read and parse the MIME-encoded request headers into r->headers_in using the request’s input filters.
requirements: r must be valid and associated with input filters ready to read headers.
Should be called during request parsing before header-dependent processing.

functions.name: ap_get_mime_headers_core
functions.description: Optimized header reader that parses MIME headers using a caller-provided temporary bucket brigade.
requirements: r must be valid.
bb must be a valid, temporary apr_bucket_brigade for input processing.

functions.name: ap_post_read_request
functions.description: Run the post_read_request hook chain and validate the request. Returns OK or HTTP error status.
requirements: r must be valid and populated with request line and headers.
Caller must handle non-OK return values (HTTP_...).

functions.name: ap_finalize_request_protocol
functions.description: Finalize protocol handling after sending the response (e.g., send terminating protocol information).
requirements: r must be the current request whose response has completed sending.

functions.name: ap_send_error_response
functions.description: Generate and send an error response to the client. If recursive_error is non-zero, indicates an error occurred while handling an ErrorDocument, so the original error is reported with a brief note about the ErrorDocument issue.
requirements: r must be valid and contain the error status to report.
recursive_error indicates nested error handling; caller should set appropriately.

functions.name: ap_set_content_length
functions.description: Set the Content-Length for the current request’s outgoing response.
requirements: r must be valid.
length should be the exact number of bytes to be sent in the response body when known.

functions.name: ap_set_keepalive
functions.description: Determine and set keepalive for the request/connection based on headers and server config. Returns 1 if keepalive can be set, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r must be valid and have request/response headers available as needed.
Caller must check return value to know if keepalive is enabled.

functions.name: ap_rationalize_mtime
functions.description: Return a rational last-modified time: mtime unless it lies in the future, in which case the current time is returned.
requirements: r must be valid.
mtime is the candidate last-modified time to rationalize.

functions.name: ap_make_content_type
functions.description: Construct the content-type header value to send to the client, optionally adding a default charset when appropriate. Returns NULL if type is NULL or empty.
requirements: r must be valid.
type is the base content type string; may be NULL or empty to indicate no content-type.
Behavior respects server settings about charset addition.

functions.name: ap_setup_make_content_type
functions.description: Precompile metadata structures used by ap_make_content_type() for faster content-type processing.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool used for allocations.

functions.name: ap_make_etag
functions.description: Construct an entity tag (ETag) for the resource associated with the request. If a filesystem-backed resource, file characteristics are included. Optionally force a weak ETag.
requirements: r must be valid and associated with the resource/metadata used for ETag generation.
force_weak non-zero forces a weak ETag if needed.

functions.name: ap_make_etag_ex
functions.description: Construct an ETag using parameters provided in an etag_rec (e.g., vary list, finfo, pathname, fd).
requirements: r must be valid.
er must point to a properly filled etag_rec structure.

functions.name: ap_set_etag
functions.description: Compute and set the ETag header in the outgoing response based on the current request/resource.
requirements: r must be valid and reference the resource metadata needed for ETag calculation.

functions.name: ap_set_etag_fd
functions.description: Compute and set the ETag header using the provided file descriptor and current request context, with the option to force a strong ETag.
requirements: r must be valid.
fd should reference the file being served when generating the ETag.

functions.name: ap_set_last_modified
functions.description: Set the Last-Modified header in the outgoing response based on the file/resource being sent.
requirements: r must be valid and have access to the resource’s modification time.

functions.name: ap_condition_if_match
functions.description: Evaluate the If-Match precondition against the given response headers. Returns AP_CONDITION_NONE if header missing, AP_CONDITION_NOMATCH if not matched, or AP_CONDITION_STRONG for a strong match.
requirements: r must be valid.
headers must be the response headers to test against (e.g., contain ETag).

functions.name: ap_condition_if_unmodified_since
functions.description: Evaluate the If-Unmodified-Since precondition against the given response headers. Returns AP_CONDITION_* indicating match strength or absence.
requirements: r must be valid.
headers should include Last-Modified and/or validators as needed.

functions.name: ap_condition_if_none_match
functions.description: Evaluate the If-None-Match precondition against the given response headers. Returns AP_CONDITION_* indicating match strength, no match, or absence.
requirements: r must be valid.
headers should include ETag as needed.

functions.name: ap_condition_if_modified_since
functions.description: Evaluate the If-Modified-Since precondition against the given response headers. Returns AP_CONDITION_* indicating match strength, no match, or absence.
requirements: r must be valid.
headers should include Last-Modified as needed.

functions.name: ap_condition_if_range
functions.description: Evaluate the If-Range precondition (combined with Range header). Returns AP_CONDITION_NONE if If-Range or Range missing, AP_CONDITION_NOMATCH if validator mismatch, AP_CONDITION_STRONG for a strong match (weak matches not permitted).
requirements: r must be valid.
headers must be the response headers (ETag or Last-Modified) used for validation.
The request must include a Range header to be meaningful.

functions.name: ap_meets_conditions
functions.description: Implement conditional GET processing per HTTP/1.1 by inspecting request headers and resource validators. Returns OK if the response meets the conditions, otherwise another status code (e.g., HTTP_NOT_MODIFIED, HTTP_PRECONDITION_FAILED).
requirements: r must be valid and contain response header/validator context (ETag/Last-Modified).
Caller must handle non-OK return statuses accordingly.

functions.name: ap_send_fd
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_send_fd(apr_file_t *fd, request_rec *r, apr_off_t offset, apr_size_t length, apr_size_t *nbytes);
functions.description: Send a portion of a file to the client, using sendfile if supported. Writes from fd starting at offset for length bytes and returns the actual bytes sent in nbytes.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file handle readable by the server.
r must be valid.
If nbytes is non-NULL, it will be set to the number of bytes actually sent.
Caller should ensure appropriate timeout is registered before calling.

functions.name: ap_send_mmap
functions.signature: apr_size_t ap_send_mmap(apr_mmap_t *mm, request_rec *r, apr_size_t offset, apr_size_t length);
functions.description: Send a region of an MMAP’ed file to the client starting at offset for length bytes. Returns the number of bytes sent.
requirements: Available only when APR_HAS_MMAP is true at build time.
mm must be a valid apr_mmap_t of the file content.
r must be valid.
Caller should ensure appropriate timeout is registered before calling.

functions.name: ap_method_register
functions.description: Register a new (extension) HTTP method name and return the bitmask offset associated with it.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for allocations.
methname must be a non-NULL, valid HTTP method token string.

functions.name: ap_method_registry_init
functions.description: Initialize the global method registry and allocate memory for it using the provided pool.
requirements: p must be a valid pool lasting at least as long as the registry is needed (typically process lifetime).

functions.name: ap_make_method_list
functions.description: Create a new method list with space preallocated for nelts extension methods.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
nelts should be non-negative.

functions.name: ap_copy_method_list
