functions.description: Copy all methods from src into dest.
requirements: dest and src must be valid, initialized ap_method_list_t instances.

functions.name: ap_method_in_list
functions.description: Return 1 if the given method name exists in the method list, 0 otherwise.
requirements: l must be a valid method list.
method must be a valid, null-terminated method name.

functions.name: ap_method_list_add
functions.description: Add the given HTTP method name to the list if not already present.
requirements: l must be a valid method list.
method must be a valid method token.

functions.name: ap_method_list_remove
functions.description: Remove the given HTTP method name from the list.
requirements: l must be a valid method list.
method must be a valid, null-terminated string.

functions.name: ap_clear_method_list
functions.description: Reset a method list to be completely empty.
requirements: l must be a valid method list.

functions.name: ap_set_content_type
functions.description: Set r->content_type for the request. Required for AddOutputFilterByType to work properly.
requirements: r must be valid.
ct must be a valid content type string.
Should be called to set r->content_type rather than assigning directly.

functions.name: ap_set_content_type_ex
functions.signature: void ap_set_content_type_ex(request_rec *r, const char *ct, int trusted);
functions.description: Set r->content_type for the request and optionally mark it as from a trusted source (e.g., server config vs application output).
requirements: r must be valid.
ct must be a valid content type string.
trusted non-zero indicates a trusted source.

functions.name: ap_set_accept_ranges
functions.description: Set the Accept-Ranges header in the response to advertise support for range requests.
requirements: r must be valid.

functions.name: ap_rputc
functions.description: Write a single character to the client for the current request. Returns number of bytes sent.
requirements: r must be valid and have an output filter chain ready.
Caller should ensure a timeout is registered before calling.

functions.name: ap_rwrite
functions.signature: int ap_rwrite(const void *buf, int nbyte, request_rec *r);
functions.description: Write nbyte bytes from buf to the client for the current request. Returns number of bytes sent.
requirements: buf must point to at least nbyte bytes of data.
nbyte must be >= 0.
r must be valid and writable.
Caller should ensure a timeout is registered before calling.

functions.name: ap_rvputs
functions.description: Write a variable number of strings to the client for the current request. Variadic list must be terminated per AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL semantics.
requirements: r must be valid and writable.
The variadic argument list must be properly terminated as required by the sentinel convention.

functions.name: ap_vrprintf
functions.signature: int ap_vrprintf(request_rec *r, const char *fmt, va_list vlist);
functions.description: Formatted output to the client using a printf-style format string and an existing va_list. Returns number of bytes sent.
requirements: r must be valid and writable.
fmt must be a valid format string compatible with the arguments in vlist.

functions.name: ap_rprintf
functions.description: Formatted output to the client using a printf-style format string and variadic arguments. Returns number of bytes sent.
requirements: r must be valid and writable.
fmt must be a valid format string for the provided arguments.

functions.name: ap_rflush
functions.description: Flush all pending output for the current request to the client. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: r must be valid and writable.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: ap_index_of_response
functions.description: Return the index into the custom_responses array for the given HTTP status code.
requirements: status must be a valid HTTP status code integer.

functions.name: ap_get_status_line
functions.description: Return the reason phrase (Status-Line without HTTP-Version) for a given status code. Returns "500 Internal Server Error" for invalid or unknown codes.
requirements: status is an HTTP status code integer.

functions.name: ap_get_status_line_ex
functions.description: Return the reason phrase for a status code. Invalid codes return "500 Internal Server Error"; unknown codes return a generated string like "xxx Status xxx" allocated from pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for allocations when status is unknown.
status is an HTTP status code integer.

functions.name: ap_setup_client_block
functions.description: Prepare to read the request body according to the specified policy regarding Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding. Returns OK or an HTTP error.
requirements: r must be valid.
read_policy must be one of REQUEST_NO_BODY, REQUEST_CHUNKED_ERROR, or REQUEST_CHUNKED_DECHUNK as defined by the server.
Caller must handle non-OK return values.

functions.name: ap_should_client_block
functions.description: Determine if the client has sent a request body; if HTTP/1.1, may send 100-Continue. Returns 0 if no body, 1 otherwise. Must not be called more than once.
requirements: r must be valid.
Must never be called more than once per request (as documented).
Call only when ready to read the request body since it may send 100-Continue.

functions.name: ap_get_client_block
functions.description: Read the next block of request body data into buffer up to bufsiz bytes. Returns number of bytes read, 0 on EOF, or -1 on error.
requirements: r must be valid and prepared for body reading (via ap_setup_client_block and ap_should_client_block).
buffer must point to a writable region of at least bufsiz bytes.
Caller must loop until 0 (EOF) or error and handle -1 appropriately.

functions.name: ap_map_http_request_error
functions.description: Map specific APR status codes from reading the request/filter stack to HTTP error codes, or fall back to the provided default status. Returns AP_FILTER_ERROR if the filter already handled the error.
requirements: rv is an APR status code from request input operations.
status is the default HTTP status code to use if rv is not recognized.
Caller must handle AP_FILTER_ERROR specially (pass-through).

functions.name: ap_discard_request_body
functions.description: If the request has a message body, read and discard it to avoid misinterpreting it as the next request on a persistent connection. Returns OK on success or an error status if the request is malformed.
requirements: r must be valid.
Should be used by handlers that do not consume request bodies.

functions.name: ap_note_auth_failure
functions.description: Setup the response headers (e.g., WWW-Authenticate) so the client knows how to authenticate on next request after an authentication failure.
requirements: r must be valid and represent a request that failed authentication.

functions.name: ap_note_basic_auth_failure
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ap_note_auth_failure. Historically set up Basic auth challenge headers.
requirements: r must be valid.
Prefer ap_note_auth_failure in new code.

functions.name: ap_note_digest_auth_failure
functions.description: Deprecated: Use ap_note_auth_failure. Historically set up Digest auth challenge headers.
requirements: r must be valid.
Prefer ap_note_auth_failure in new code.

functions.name: ap_get_basic_auth_pw
functions.description: Deprecated. Retrieve the Basic authentication password from request headers and set r->user as a side effect. Must be followed by immediate authentication decision or immediate error response to avoid incorrect authentication (CVE-2017-3167).
requirements: r must be valid.
pw must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the password on success.
Caller MUST either authenticate immediately after the call or stop the request with an error response (as documented).
Caller must handle return values: OK (0) on success; HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED, or DECLINED for other cases.

functions.name: ap_get_basic_auth_components
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_get_basic_auth_components(const request_rec *r, const char **username, const char **password);
functions.description: Parse Basic authentication credentials from the request headers without side effects. On success, returns APR_SUCCESS and outputs username and/or password when non-NULL.
requirements: r must be valid.
username and/or password may be NULL if not needed; non-NULL outputs are set only on success.
Caller must handle APR_EINVAL when header missing or not Basic; outputs remain unchanged on failure.

functions.name: ap_parse_uri
functions.description: Parse the provided URI into request_rec components, with side effects: sets r->args (after '?'), r->uri (without args), and r->hostname if not already set based on scheme://host:port.
requirements: r must be valid.
uri must be a valid, null-terminated URI string.

functions.name: ap_getline
functions.signature: int ap_getline(char *s, int n, request_rec *r, int flags);
functions.description: Read the next input line for the request into buffer s up to n bytes. Returns length on success, n if line exceeds buffer, or -1 on error.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer of size at least n.
n must be > 0.
r must be valid with input filters ready.
flags is a bitmask of AP_GETLINE_* options (e.g., AP_GETLINE_FOLD, AP_GETLINE_CRLF, AP_GETLINE_NOSPC_EOL, AP_GETLINE_NONBLOCK).
Caller must handle the special return n meaning line too long.

functions.name: ap_fgetline
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_fgetline(char **s, apr_size_t n, apr_size_t *read, ap_filter_t *f, int flags, apr_bucket_brigade *bb, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Read the next line from input filter f into buffer *s (allocating from p if *s == NULL), up to n bytes. Returns APR_SUCCESS, APR_ENOSPC if the line is too long, or other APR errors.
requirements: s must be non-NULL; if *s is NULL a buffer will be allocated from p.
n is the maximum bytes to read into the buffer.
read must be a valid pointer to receive the line length.
f must be a valid input filter.
flags is a bitmask of AP_GETLINE_* options.
bb must be a working brigade for reading buckets.
p must be a valid pool for allocations when needed.

functions.name: ap_rgetline
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_rgetline(char **s, apr_size_t n, apr_size_t *read, request_rec *r, int flags, apr_bucket_brigade *bb);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around ap_fgetline() reading from r->proto_input_filters. Reads a line into *s up to n bytes.
requirements: s must be non-NULL; allocation behavior matches ap_fgetline.
n is the maximum bytes to read.
read must be a valid pointer to receive number of bytes read.
r must be valid with proto_input_filters set.
flags is a bitmask of AP_GETLINE_* options.
bb must be a working brigade.

functions.name: ap_method_number_of
functions.description: Return the internal method number associated with the given HTTP method name, or M_INVALID if not recognized.
requirements: method must be a valid, null-terminated method name string.

functions.name: ap_method_name_of
functions.description: Return the method name associated with an internal method number, or NULL if not recognized. May allocate from pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid pool for temporary allocations.
methnum is an internal method number.

functions.name: ap_get_protocol_upgrades
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_get_protocol_upgrades(conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, server_rec *s, int report_all, const apr_array_header_t **pupgrades);
functions.description: Determine protocols that the connection/request may upgrade to (besides the current protocol). If report_all is 0, only more preferable protocols are included; otherwise all available alternatives. Returns the array via pupgrades, possibly NULL if none.
requirements: c must be valid.
r may be NULL or a valid request.
s may be NULL or valid; if NULL, it will be inferred as documented.
pupgrades must be non-NULL to receive results; may be set to NULL when none are available.

functions.name: ap_select_protocol
functions.signature: const char *ap_select_protocol(conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, server_rec *s, const apr_array_header_t *choices);
functions.description: Select a protocol for the connection/request from the provided choices (often the client’s proposals). May return the current protocol or NULL if no protocol can be agreed upon. Passing NULL for choices removes restrictions on selection.
requirements: c must be valid.
r may be NULL or valid.
s must be valid for selection context.
choices may be NULL to indicate unrestricted selection or a valid array of protocol identifiers.

functions.name: ap_switch_protocol
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_switch_protocol(conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, server_rec *s, const char *protocol);
functions.description: Perform the actual protocol switch to the given protocol previously selected for the same connection/request pair. Returns APR_SUCCESS to continue processing, APR_EOF to stop processing, APR_EINVAL if protocol already in place, APR_NOTIMPL if no module performed the switch, or other errors as appropriate.
requirements: c must be valid.
r may be NULL for connection-level or valid for request-triggered switch.
s must be the selected server/virtual host.
protocol must be a valid identifier that was previously selected for this connection/request.

functions.name: ap_get_protocol
functions.description: Return the protocol identifier currently in use on the connection. Defaults to "http/1.1" unless a switch has been reported via the protocol_get hook.
requirements: c must be valid.

functions.name: ap_is_allowed_protocol
functions.signature: int ap_is_allowed_protocol(conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, server_rec *s, const char *protocol);
functions.description: Check whether the given protocol is allowed for the specified connection/request/server context. Returns non-zero if allowed.
requirements: c must be valid.
r may be NULL or valid.
s may be NULL (then derived from r or c) or valid.
protocol must be a non-NULL protocol identifier string.

functions.name: ap_bucket_error_make
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_error_make(apr_bucket *b, int error, const char *buf, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Convert an existing bucket into an HTTP error bucket carrying status code and optional error string.
requirements: b must be a valid, modifiable apr_bucket.
error is an HTTP status code to embed.
buf may be NULL or a text message; allocated from p as needed.
p must be a valid pool for allocations.

functions.name: ap_bucket_error_create
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_error_create(int error, const char *buf, apr_pool_t *p, apr_bucket_alloc_t *list);
functions.description: Create a new bucket referencing an HTTP error with the given status code and optional string.
requirements: error is an HTTP status code.
buf may be NULL or a message; will be allocated from p as needed.
p must be a valid pool.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_request_make
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_request_make(apr_bucket *b, const char *method, const char *uri, const char *protocol, apr_table_t *headers, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Convert an existing bucket into a request bucket, copying all parameters into pool p.
requirements: b must be a valid, modifiable apr_bucket.
method, uri, protocol must be valid strings.
headers must be a valid apr_table_t of request headers.
p must be a valid pool; data is copied to p.

functions.name: ap_bucket_request_maken
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_request_maken(apr_bucket *b, const char *method, const char *uri, const char *protocol, apr_table_t *headers, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Convert an existing bucket into a request bucket, using the provided parameters without copying.
requirements: b must be a valid, modifiable apr_bucket.
method, uri, protocol pointers must remain valid for the bucket’s lifetime.
headers must remain valid for the bucket’s lifetime.
p must be a valid pool (stored for lifetime management, not for copying).

functions.name: ap_bucket_request_create
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_request_create(const char *method, const char *uri, const char *protocol, apr_table_t *headers, apr_pool_t *p, apr_bucket_alloc_t *list);
functions.description: Create a new request bucket, copying all parameters to the given pool p.
requirements: method, uri, protocol must be valid strings.
headers must be a valid apr_table_t.
p must be a valid pool for copies.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_request_createn
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_request_createn(const char *method, const char *uri, const char *protocol, apr_table_t *headers, apr_pool_t *p, apr_bucket_alloc_t *list);
functions.description: Create a new request bucket using the provided parameters without copying.
requirements: method, uri, protocol pointers and headers table must outlive the bucket.
p must be a valid pool (stored).
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_request_clone
functions.description: Clone an existing request bucket into another pool/allocator to manage a separate lifetime. Returns the new bucket or NULL on failure.
requirements: source must be a valid request bucket.
p must be a valid pool for cloned data if copying is required.
list must be a valid bucket allocator for the clone.

functions.name: ap_bucket_response_make
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_response_make(apr_bucket *b, int status, const char *reason, apr_table_t *headers, apr_table_t *notes, apr_pool_t *p);
functions.description: Convert an existing bucket into a response bucket containing status, optional reason phrase, headers, and internal notes.
requirements: b must be a valid, modifiable apr_bucket.
status must be an HTTP status code integer.
reason may be NULL.
headers and notes must be valid apr_table_t structures.
p must be a valid pool.

functions.name: ap_bucket_response_create
functions.signature: apr_bucket *ap_bucket_response_create(int status, const char *reason, apr_table_t *headers, apr_table_t *notes, apr_pool_t *p, apr_bucket_alloc_t *list);
functions.description: Create a new response bucket with the given status/reason, headers, and internal notes.
requirements: status must be an HTTP status code.
reason may be NULL.
headers and notes must be valid tables.
p must be a valid pool.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_response_clone
functions.description: Clone a response bucket into another pool/allocator for an independent lifetime.
requirements: source must be a valid response bucket.
p must be a valid pool for cloned data if needed.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_headers_make
functions.description: Convert an existing bucket into a headers bucket referring to a table of HTTP headers.
requirements: b must be a valid, modifiable apr_bucket.
headers must be a valid apr_table_t.
p must be a valid pool.

functions.name: ap_bucket_headers_create
functions.description: Create a new headers bucket referencing the given header table.
requirements: headers must be a valid apr_table_t.
p must be a valid pool.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_bucket_headers_clone
functions.description: Clone a headers bucket into another pool/allocator for separate lifetime management.
requirements: source must be a valid headers bucket.
p must be a valid pool.
list must be a valid bucket allocator.

functions.name: ap_byterange_filter
functions.description: Output filter that processes Range requests and emits the appropriate byte ranges (possibly multipart/byteranges) to the client.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter in the chain.
b must be a valid brigade of response buckets to filter.

functions.name: ap_http_header_filter
functions.description: Output filter that generates and sends HTTP headers for the response prior to the body.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter.
b must be a valid brigade; headers and any pre-body buckets are expected.

functions.name: ap_content_length_filter
functions.description: Output filter that sets or verifies the Content-Length of the response by buffering/counting the outgoing body as needed.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter.
b must be a valid brigade of body buckets.

functions.name: ap_set_sub_req_protocol
functions.description: Initialize protocol-related fields for a subrequest rnew based on the parent request r.
requirements: rnew must be a valid, newly created subrequest.
r must be a valid parent request.

functions.name: ap_finalize_sub_req_protocol
functions.description: Finalize protocol/accounting for a subrequest, indicating that no more content will be produced by it.
requirements: sub_r must be a valid subrequest whose content generation is complete.

functions.name: ap_set_std_response_headers
functions.description: Populate standard response headers (e.g., Date and Server) in r->headers_out, respecting precedence of existing values (such as from proxied requests).
requirements: r must be valid.

functions.name: ap_send_interim_response
functions.description: Send an interim HTTP 1xx response immediately. If send_headers is non-zero, send and then clear r->headers_out.
requirements: r must be valid and in a state where sending an interim response is appropriate (before final response).
send_headers controls whether current response headers are sent/cleared.

functions.name: ap_h1_append_header
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_h1_append_header(apr_bucket_brigade *b, apr_pool_t *pool, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Append a single HTTP/1.1 formatted header line (name: value\r\n) to the brigade.
requirements: b must be a valid brigade to append to.
pool must be a valid pool for any allocations.
name and value must be valid, null-terminated strings without CR/LF.

functions.name: ap_h1_append_headers
functions.description: Append a set of HTTP/1.1 headers from the given table to the brigade, using r for pool and logging context.
requirements: b must be a valid brigade.
r must be valid.
headers must be a valid apr_table_t of header fields.

functions.name: ap_h1_terminate_header
functions.description: Append the HTTP/1.1 header terminator (an empty CRLF) to the brigade.
requirements: b must be a valid brigade to append to.

functions.name: ap_h1_add_end_chunk
functions.description: Insert or append the terminating chunk for Transfer-Encoding: chunked, optionally with trailers, before the EOS bucket or at the end if eos is NULL.
requirements: b must be a valid brigade representing the chunked response body.
eos may be NULL or an EOS bucket before which to insert the last chunk.
r must be valid.
trailers may be NULL or a table of trailers to include.

functions.name: ap_process_request_internal
functions.description: Internal handler used by ap_process_request, subrequest mechanisms, and redirects to pre-process a request record and drive the internal phases up to handler invocation as appropriate. Returns the request status code.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec for the current request or subrequest

functions.name: ap_sub_req_lookup_uri
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(request_rec *) ap_sub_req_lookup_uri(const char *new_uri, const request_rec *r, ap_filter_t *next_filter);
functions.description: Create a subrequest from the given URI relative to the current request. The returned subrequest can be inspected to discover how the server would handle that URI. The subrequest is not automatically run; use ap_run_sub_req() to execute it.
requirements: r must be the current (main or sub) request
new_uri points to a valid NUL-terminated URI string
next_filter may be NULL to default to the main request’s first filter
The returned subrequest’s memory is allocated from a pool associated with r; destroy with ap_destroy_sub_req() when done unless handed off via ap_internal_fast_redirect()

functions.name: ap_sub_req_lookup_file
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(request_rec *) ap_sub_req_lookup_file(const char *new_file, const request_rec *r, ap_filter_t *next_filter);
functions.description: Create a subrequest that maps the given filesystem path as if requested, without running it. Useful to inspect how a file would be served.
requirements: r must be the current request
new_file points to a valid NUL-terminated filesystem path
next_filter may be NULL to default to the main request’s first filter
Destroy the returned subrequest with ap_destroy_sub_req() when finished (unless merged via ap_internal_fast_redirect())

functions.name: ap_sub_req_lookup_dirent
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(request_rec *) ap_sub_req_lookup_dirent(const apr_finfo_t *finfo, const request_rec *r, int subtype, ap_filter_t *next_filter);
functions.description: Create a subrequest from an apr_dir_read result (apr_finfo_t) for a directory entry. Allows inspection of how that entry would be handled.
requirements: r must be the current request
finfo must describe an entry in the same directory as the current request
finfo must at minimum include the name; APR_FINFO_MIN|APR_FINFO_NAME is the minimum recommended query when using apr_dir_read results
subtype must be one of AP_SUBREQ_NO_ARGS or AP_SUBREQ_MERGE_ARGS
next_filter may be NULL to default to the main request’s first filter
Destroy the returned subrequest with ap_destroy_sub_req() when finished (unless merged via ap_internal_fast_redirect())

functions.name: ap_sub_req_method_uri
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(request_rec *) ap_sub_req_method_uri(const char *method, const char *new_uri, const request_rec *r, ap_filter_t *next_filter);
functions.description: Create a subrequest for the given URI but using the specified HTTP method (e.g., "GET", "POST"). The subrequest can be inspected before optionally running it.
requirements: r must be the current request
method must point to a valid NUL-terminated method name string
new_uri points to a valid NUL-terminated URI
next_filter may be NULL to default to the main request’s first filter
Destroy the returned subrequest with ap_destroy_sub_req() when finished (unless merged via ap_internal_fast_redirect())

functions.name: ap_sub_req_output_filter
functions.description: An output filter that strips EOS buckets from subrequests. Must be the last filter in a subrequest’s filter stack to prevent premature end-of-stream signaling.
requirements: f must be a valid filter context for a subrequest
bb must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade
This filter must be inserted at the end of the subrequest’s filter stack

functions.name: ap_run_sub_req
functions.description: Execute the handler pipeline for the given subrequest and return its status code.
requirements: r must be a subrequest created by an ap_sub_req_* API
Subrequest must be properly initialized (as created) before running

functions.name: ap_destroy_sub_req
functions.description: Free resources associated with a subrequest. Copy out any data you need before destroying, as its pool and allocations will be reclaimed.
requirements: r must be a subrequest created by ap_sub_req_*
Do not call this if the subrequest’s pool has been merged into another request (e.g., after ap_internal_fast_redirect())

functions.name: ap_internal_redirect
functions.description: Internally redirect the current request to a different URI. Typically called by a handler which then returns OK to stop further processing of the original target.
requirements: r must be the current request
new_uri must be a valid NUL-terminated URI string
Should be followed by returning OK from the handler to complete the redirect

functions.name: ap_internal_redirect_handler
functions.description: Like ap_internal_redirect(), but preserves the content type across the internal redirect (useful for actions/CGI set via AddHandler).
requirements: r must be the current request
new_uri must be a valid NUL-terminated URI string
Typically used when the original content type must be preserved across the redirect

functions.name: ap_internal_fast_redirect
functions.description: Redirect the current request to a prepared subrequest, merging the subrequest’s pool into the main request. The subrequest is adopted as the main one.
requirements: sub_req must be a valid subrequest created from r
Do not destroy sub_req after calling; its pool is merged and it will be destroyed with the main request
Callers must be careful with lifetimes of any allocations that were in sub_req’s pool (now merged)

functions.name: ap_some_auth_required
functions.description: Deprecated. Previously indicated if authentication was required for the current request. Behavior changed in 2.4.x; API no longer usable. See ap_some_authn_required().
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Do not rely on this API in new code; use ap_some_authn_required() instead

functions.name: ap_clear_auth_internal
functions.description: Clear the internal flag controlling when access control hooks are run for internal requests.

functions.name: ap_setup_auth_internal
functions.description: Configure whether access control hooks run for all internal requests with distinct URIs or only when configurations differ from the initial request. Defaults to per-URI unless all access control hooks and providers are registered with AP_AUTH_INTERNAL_PER_CONF.
requirements: ptemp must be a valid APR pool for temporary allocations

functions.name: ap_register_auth_provider
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_register_auth_provider(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *provider_group, const char *provider_name, const char *provider_version, const void *provider, int type);
functions.description: Register an authentication or authorization provider in the global provider pool under a group/name/version, with an internal request processing mode. Returns APR status.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool for any provider storage
provider_group, provider_name, and provider_version should be valid NUL-terminated strings identifying the provider
provider points to the provider’s opaque vtable/structure expected by the group
type must be AP_AUTH_INTERNAL_PER_URI or AP_AUTH_INTERNAL_PER_CONF
Check the returned apr_status_t for success (APR_SUCCESS) or failure

functions.name: authn_ap_list_provider_names
functions.description: Optional function (from mod_authn_core) that returns an APR array of strings listing all registered authentication provider names.
requirements: ptemp must be a valid APR pool used for temporary allocations
Function availability depends on the module exporting this optional function being loaded/resolved

functions.name: authz_ap_list_provider_names
functions.description: Optional function (from mod_authz_core) that returns an APR array of strings listing all registered authorization provider names.
requirements: ptemp must be a valid APR pool used for temporary allocations
Function availability depends on the module exporting this optional function being loaded/resolved

functions.name: ap_is_initial_req
functions.description: Return nonzero if r is the main (initial) request, zero if it is a subrequest or internal redirect.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec

functions.name: ap_update_mtime
functions.description: Set r->mtime to dependency_mtime if it is later than the current r->mtime. Used to track the most recent modification time among dependencies.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
dependency_mtime is an APR time value (microseconds)

functions.name: ap_allow_methods
functions.description: Add one or more HTTP methods (by name) to the list permitted to access the resource. Typically called by the content handler before sending the response headers; may be called earlier if authoritative. Methods are added to existing ones unless reset is nonzero. The Allow header is generated from this list when needed.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
reset determines replacement (nonzero) vs merge (zero) with existing allowed methods
Variadic args: a NULL-terminated list of const char* method names; the final argument must be NULL

functions.name: ap_allow_standard_methods
functions.description: Add one or more standard methods (by numeric identifiers from the M_* constants defined in httpd.h) to the list permitted to access the resource. Similar to ap_allow_methods but uses method IDs.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
reset determines replacement (nonzero) vs merge (zero) with existing allowed methods
Variadic args: a list of int method IDs from the M_* series terminated by -1 (e.g., M_GET, M_POST, -1)

functions.name: ap_process_request
functions.description: Process a top-level client request synchronously, generating and writing the response to the client.
requirements: r must be a valid, fully initialized top-level request_rec

functions.name: ap_process_request_after_handler
functions.description: Perform post-processing steps after a handler has finished with a request. Commonly used after a request was suspended.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec whose handler phase has completed or been resumed

functions.name: ap_process_async_request
functions.description: Process a top-level request allowing response data to remain buffered in the core output filter for later, asynchronous completion.
requirements: r must be a valid, fully initialized top-level request_rec

functions.name: ap_die
functions.description: Terminate processing of the current request with the specified reason/type, sending the appropriate error response to the client.
requirements: r must be the current request_rec
type must be a valid reason code understood by the server’s error handling

functions.name: ap_check_pipeline
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_check_pipeline(conn_rec *c, apr_bucket_brigade *bb, unsigned int max_blank_lines);
functions.description: Check whether a connection is still established and has data available, optionally consuming up to max_blank_lines blank lines. Returns APR_SUCCESS if established with data, APR_EAGAIN if established and empty, APR_NOTFOUND if too many blank lines, or another APR_E* on errors.
requirements: c must be a valid connection record
bb must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade for input filtering
max_blank_lines is the maximum number of blank lines to consume; zero means treat blank lines as data (single read)
Callers must handle the returned apr_status_t accordingly

functions.name: ap_location_walk
functions.description: Perform the server’s internal per-location (Location directive) walk for the request. Details are not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Specific semantics and return codes are not documented in this header; consult core implementation for details

functions.name: ap_directory_walk
functions.description: Perform the server’s internal per-directory walk for the request, applying directory-based configuration. Details are not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Specific semantics and return codes are not documented in this header; consult core implementation for details

functions.name: ap_file_walk
functions.description: Perform the server’s internal per-file walk for the request. Details are not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Specific semantics and return codes are not documented in this header; consult core implementation for details

functions.name: ap_if_walk
functions.description: Evaluate per-condition (If directive) sections for the request. Details are not documented here.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Specific semantics and return codes are not documented in this header; consult core implementation for details

functions.name: ap_bucket_eor_make
functions.description: Transform an existing bucket into an End Of REQUEST (EOR) bucket associated with r. When the bucket is destroyed, the associated request can be destroyed after output completion.
requirements: b must be a valid apr_bucket
r must be the request to destroy when the EOR bucket is destroyed
Returns NULL if allocation failed; callers must check the return value

functions.name: ap_bucket_eor_create
functions.description: Create a new End Of REQUEST (EOR) bucket from the given bucket allocator and bind it to r, so that r can be destroyed once output is fully sent.
requirements: list must be a valid apr_bucket_alloc_t allocator (freelist)
r must be the request to destroy when the EOR bucket is destroyed
Returns NULL if allocation failed; callers must check the return value

functions.name: ap_bucket_eor_request
functions.description: Return the request_rec associated with an EOR bucket.
requirements: b must be an EOR bucket (AP_BUCKET_IS_EOR(b) should be true)

functions.name: ap_some_authn_required
functions.description: Determine whether any authentication is required for the current request. If used inside access_checker/access_checker_ex hooks or authz providers, the caller must avoid loops because this function invokes these hooks.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec
Callers using this within access control or authz hooks must ensure they do not create recursion/looping

functions.name: ssl_conn_is_ssl
functions.description: Hook: modules managing SSL can report whether a given connection is using their SSL. Callers run this hook to query providers; an implementation returns OK if the connection is SSL for that module, DECLINED otherwise.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized conn_rec* for the current connection.
Callers should interpret a return value of OK as 'SSL in use' for that provider, and DECLINED as 'not SSL' (for that provider).
Multiple modules may register; callers should be prepared to aggregate results per the hook runner’s policy.

functions.name: ap_ssl_conn_is_ssl
functions.description: Returns nonzero iff the connection is encrypted with SSL/TLS. Convenience API that answers the SSL state of a connection.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized conn_rec*.
Callers must treat any nonzero return as 'SSL enabled', zero as 'not SSL'.

functions.name: ssl_bind_outgoing
functions.signature: int ssl_bind_outgoing(conn_rec *c, struct ap_conf_vector_t *dir_conf, int enable_ssl);
functions.description: Hook: declare a connection as outgoing and apply configuration to it; can also enable SSL on the connection. Called after connection creation and before pre-connection hooks; may be called multiple times (e.g., on reuse in different request contexts). All registered hooks run until one returns a value other than DECLINED. If enable_ssl != 0, a hook that sets up SSL should return OK to prevent subsequent hooks from doing the same.
requirements: c must be a valid, outgoing conn_rec*.
dir_conf may vary across calls on the same connection and must be a valid ap_conf_vector_t* when provided.
enable_ssl nonzero requests SSL setup; a hook that enables SSL must return OK to stop further SSL setup by other hooks.
Callers should expect this hook may be invoked multiple times during a connection’s lifetime; hook implementations must be idempotent or handle repeated calls.

functions.name: ap_ssl_bind_outgoing
functions.signature: int ap_ssl_bind_outgoing(conn_rec *c, struct ap_conf_vector_t *dir_conf, int require_ssl);
functions.description: Marks the connection as outgoing and invokes the ssl_bind_outgoing hook. May be called several times on an outgoing connection with varying dir_conf values. require_ssl must not change for the same connection. Returns OK iff SSL was required and is enabled; otherwise DECLINED.
requirements: c must be a valid, outgoing conn_rec*.
dir_conf must be a valid configuration vector appropriate to the current request context; it may vary across calls.
require_ssl must be consistent across all calls for the same connection (it is not allowed to change).
Callers must handle the return value: OK indicates SSL was required and is enabled; DECLINED indicates otherwise.

functions.name: ap_ssl_has_outgoing_handlers
functions.description: Returns nonzero iff handlers/hooks for outgoing SSL connections are registered. Useful to decide if SSL binding for outgoing connections is supported.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any point after module registration when hook availability is relevant.

functions.name: ssl_var_lookup
functions.signature: const char *ssl_var_lookup(apr_pool_t *p, server_rec *s, conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, const char *name);
functions.description: Hook: lookup an SSL-related variable in the context of a server, connection, and/or request. Some variables are only available with a connection or request. The returned string, if not NULL, is allocated from pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid apr_pool_t* and is required.
name must be a non-NULL C string naming the variable.
s, c, and r may be NULL; availability depends on the variable.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is allocated from p and valid for the lifetime of p.

functions.name: ap_ssl_var_lookup
functions.signature: const char *ap_ssl_var_lookup(apr_pool_t *p, server_rec *s, conn_rec *c, request_rec *r, const char *name);
functions.description: Looks up an SSL-related variable for the provided server/connection/request context, or a global value if s, c, and r are all NULL. The returned string, if not NULL, is allocated from pool p.
requirements: p must be a valid apr_pool_t* and is required.
name must be a non-NULL C string naming the variable.
s, c, and r may be NULL; variable availability depends on context.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is allocated from p and valid for the lifetime of p.

functions.name: ssl_add_cert_files
functions.description: Hook: providers register certificate and private key files for a server. Certificate files should contain the certificate chain (server certificate first, excluding the trust anchor) in PEM; each must be accompanied by a PEM private key file.
requirements: s must be the target server_rec*.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t* for any allocations.
cert_files must be a valid apr_array_header_t* of const char* file paths to PEM certificate chains.
key_files must be a valid apr_array_header_t* of const char* file paths to PEM private keys.
Each added certificate must have a corresponding private key file.
Return value: OK if files were added; DECLINED if not; other values indicate error.

functions.name: ap_ssl_add_cert_files
functions.description: Collects certificate/key file paths from all registered providers, including global and optional hooks provided by SSL modules. Populates the provided arrays with PEM certificate chains and corresponding private key files.
requirements: s must be the target server_rec*.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
cert_files must be a valid, initialized apr_array_header_t* accepting const char* entries.
key_files must be a valid, initialized apr_array_header_t* accepting const char* entries.
The caller must handle the returned apr_status_t; APR_SUCCESS indicates files were collected successfully.

functions.name: ssl_add_fallback_cert_files
functions.description: Hook: providers register 'fallback' certificate and key files used when no real certificates are configured. These are commonly self-signed, temporary certificates; modules using them are encouraged to respond with HTTP 503.
requirements: s must be the target server_rec*.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
cert_files must be a valid apr_array_header_t* of const char* PEM certificate chain file paths.
key_files must be a valid apr_array_header_t* of const char* PEM private key file paths.
Each fallback certificate should have an accompanying private key.
Return value: OK if files were added; DECLINED if not; other values indicate error.

functions.name: ap_ssl_add_fallback_cert_files
functions.description: Collects 'fallback' certificate/key file paths from all registered providers (global and optional). Intended for temporary use until a trusted certificate is available; modules using fallbacks are encouraged to answer with HTTP 503.
requirements: s must be the target server_rec*.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
cert_files must be a valid, initialized apr_array_header_t* accepting const char* entries.
key_files must be a valid, initialized apr_array_header_t* accepting const char* entries.
The caller must handle the returned apr_status_t.

functions.name: ssl_answer_challenge
functions.signature: int ssl_answer_challenge(conn_rec *c, const char *server_name, const char **pcert_pem, const char **pkey_pem);
functions.description: Hook: allow modules to provide a certificate and key for TLS connections that are performing a challenge (e.g., ACME tls-alpn-01) and do not relate to a configured vhost. Implementations return OK and set pcert_pem/pkey_pem when they can answer the challenge.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec*.
server_name should be the SNI or relevant server name for the challenge.
pcert_pem and pkey_pem must be valid, non-NULL output pointers to receive PEM strings.
If a certificate PEM is provided, it must be accompanied by a private key PEM; pkey_pem may be set to NULL only if the private key is embedded in the certificate PEM string.
Returned certificate/key PEMs replace any other certificates selected on the connection.

functions.name: ap_ssl_answer_challenge
functions.signature: int ap_ssl_answer_challenge(conn_rec *c, const char *server_name, const char **pcert_pem, const char **pkey_pem);
functions.description: Determines whether the connection is a challenge (e.g., ACME tls-alpn-01) requiring a specific certificate, and if so, obtains a certificate and key to present in the handshake. ALPN protocol negotiation via protocol_propose/protocol_switch must have run before this call.
requirements: c must be a valid conn_rec*.
server_name should be the relevant SNI/server name.
pcert_pem and pkey_pem must be valid, non-NULL output pointers to receive PEM strings.
If a certificate PEM is provided, it must be accompanied by a private key PEM; pkey_pem may be NULL only if the private key is contained in the certificate PEM string.
ALPN negotiation (protocol_propose and protocol_switch hooks) must have completed before calling.
A certificate provided this way replaces any other certificates selected for the connection.
Return value is nonzero iff a challenge is present and a specific certificate is provided.

functions.name: ap_setup_ssl_optional_fns
functions.description: Installs optional functions to bridge old-style SSL module functions with the newer ap_is_ssl() and related queries, shadowing older optionals so that legacy modules get correct results. Should run in core’s very early POST_CONFIG hook.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
Should be invoked during the server’s very early POST_CONFIG hook phase.
Must run after providers register their optionals (during register_hooks) and before consumers retrieve them (often post-config or later).

functions.name: ssl_ocsp_prime_hook
functions.signature: int ssl_ocsp_prime_hook(server_rec *s, apr_pool_t *p, const char *id, apr_size_t id_len, const char *pem);
functions.description: Hook: providers of OCSP stapling register here to accept certificates for which they will later provide OCSP responses. Implementations return OK if they will provide stapling data for the given certificate.
requirements: s must be the server being configured.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
id must be an opaque byte sequence uniquely identifying the certificate within the server instance; id_len is its length.
pem must contain PEM data of the certificate first, followed by the PEM of the issuer certificate (at least).
The memory referenced by id and pem is only valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: ap_ssl_ocsp_prime
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_ssl_ocsp_prime(server_rec *s, apr_pool_t *p, const char *id, apr_size_t id_len, const char *pem);
functions.description: Registers a certificate for provisioning OCSP stapling responses. Callers must supply an instance-unique identifier for the certificate and the certificate PEM followed by chain certs (at least the issuer). A certificate can be primed multiple times but must use the exact same identifier bytes each time.
requirements: s must be the server being configured.
p must be a valid apr_pool_t*.
id must be an opaque, globally unique (per Apache instance) identifier for the certificate; id_len specifies its length.
If primed multiple times for the same cert, the id bytes must be identical each time.
pem must contain PEM of the certificate first, followed by chain certificates (at least the issuer).
The memory referenced by id and pem is only valid for the duration of the call.
Return APR_SUCCESS iff OCSP responses will be provided; APR_ENOENT if no provider was found or accepted responsibility; other apr_status_t values indicate different errors.

functions.name: ssl_ocsp_get_resp_hook
functions.signature: int ssl_ocsp_get_resp_hook(server_rec *s, conn_rec *c, const char *id, apr_size_t id_len, ap_ssl_ocsp_copy_resp *cb, void *userdata);
functions.description: Hook: request OCSP response DER data for a previously primed certificate. Implementations invoke cb with the DER bytes (or possibly NULL,0 if not available) and return OK when response data has been provided; otherwise DECLINED.
requirements: s must be the (SNI-selected) server of the connection.
c must be the active connection.
id must be the same identifier (byte-wise) used during priming; id_len specifies its length.
cb must be a valid callback pointer; implementations may invoke it during the call. Any data passed to cb is only valid for the duration of the call; the caller must copy it.
userdata is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback.
Return OK iff response data has been provided; otherwise DECLINED.

functions.name: ap_ssl_ocsp_get_resp
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_ssl_ocsp_get_resp(server_rec *s, conn_rec *c, const char *id, apr_size_t id_len, ap_ssl_ocsp_copy_resp *cb, void *userdata);
functions.description: Retrieves OCSP response DER data for a previously primed certificate. If APR_SUCCESS is returned, cb has been called with the response data. Otherwise another apr_status_t is returned; SSL handshakes should generally proceed without stapling if unavailable. Response data and the id pointer are only valid during the call.
requirements: s must be the (SNI-selected) server for the connection.
c must be a valid connection.
id must be byte-wise identical to the identifier used in ap_ssl_ocsp_prime; id_len specifies its length. The memory pointed to by id is only valid for the duration of the call.
cb must be a valid callback pointer and may be invoked during the call. The DER data provided to cb is only valid for the duration of the call; the caller must copy it for further use.
userdata is passed through to the callback.
Return APR_SUCCESS iff response data has been provided; other apr_status_t values indicate non-availability or error.

functions.name: ap_init_vhost_config
functions.description: Initialize the virtual host configuration subsystem before any server configuration is read. Typically called during server startup to prepare internal data structures that will be populated during config parsing.
requirements: p must be a valid, live APR pool for any allocations performed by the initializer.
Call this before any configuration files are parsed (i.e., early in server initialization).
Threading/ordering requirements beyond “before config is read” are unknown from this header.

functions.name: ap_fini_vhost_config
functions.description: Finalize virtual host configuration after configuration has been parsed by compiling the lookup tables used for run‑time vhost resolution. Should be invoked once the full vhost list is known.
requirements: Call only after all configuration (including all <VirtualHost> blocks) has been read.
p must be a valid APR pool for any allocations during the finalization step.
main_server must be a valid pointer to the head of the server_rec list (the main server that anchors the virtual hosts).
Assumes the vhost list linked off main_server is fully constructed; partial/ongoing modification during this call is not supported (not stated, but implied by finalize/compile step).

functions.name: ap_parse_vhost_addrs
functions.signature: const char * ap_parse_vhost_addrs(apr_pool_t *p, const char *hostname, server_rec *s)
functions.description: Parse and register the address/port specifications provided on a <VirtualHost> directive line, associating them with the given server_rec. Returns an error message on failure or NULL on success. Usage: called during configuration processing for each <VirtualHost ...> block.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool for any temporary/permanent allocations made during parsing.
hostname should be a non-NULL string containing the raw <VirtualHost> argument(s) (e.g., IPs/hostnames with optional ports).
s must be a valid, initialized server_rec corresponding to the <VirtualHost> being configured.
Return value: NULL indicates success; a non-NULL const char* points to a human-readable error message (behavior inferred from Apache config handler conventions).
Exact accepted address formats beyond “addresses in <VirtualHost>” are not specified in this header.

functions.name: ap_set_name_virtual_host
functions.signature: const char * ap_set_name_virtual_host(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg)
functions.description: Process the NameVirtualHost directive during configuration. The argument must be of the form "<address>[:port]". Returns NULL on success or a const char* error message on failure (standard Apache directive handler convention). The dummy parameter is unused.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the active cmd_parms for the configuration pass.
arg must be a non-NULL string of the form "<address>[:port]".
dummy is not used by the function and may be NULL.
Return value semantics follow Apache directive handlers: NULL for success; non-NULL error string for failure (inferred from naming and comment).
Should be called only during configuration parsing, not at runtime.

functions.name: ap_vhost_iterate_given_conn
functions.description: Iterate over each name-based virtual host applicable to the given connection and invoke the provided callback for each. Iteration stops early if the callback returns non-zero; the function’s return value is the last callback return value.
requirements: conn must be a valid, active connection record whose vhost candidates have been determined (e.g., after initial vhost selection by IP).
func_cb must be a valid function pointer of type int(*)(void*, conn_rec*, server_rec*). It should return 0 to continue iteration and non-zero to stop.
baton is an opaque user pointer passed through to each callback invocation and may be NULL.
Callbacks must not modify or free data structures owned by the server in a way that invalidates subsequent iterations (not stated explicitly; general callback safety applies).

functions.name: ap_update_vhost_given_ip
functions.description: Select the best-fit virtual host for the connection using only the local/remote IP and port information. Establishes the baseline vhost prior to evaluating the Host header for name-based vhosts.
requirements: conn must be a valid, initialized connection record.
Call when the connection is established and before or independent of request headers; this step alone may be insufficient for final vhost selection (per comment).

functions.name: ap_update_vhost_from_headers
functions.description: Refine vhost selection using request headers (e.g., the Host header) after they have been read. May update r->server to a better name-based vhost match.
requirements: r must be a valid request record.
Call only after request headers have been read.
r->server may be modified by this function; callers must be prepared for server context to change.

functions.name: ap_update_vhost_from_headers_ex
functions.description: Like ap_update_vhost_from_headers, but returns a status code and can enforce that the requested hostname matches a configured name-based vhost. Returns HTTP_OK on success; if require_match is non-zero and no explicit match is found, returns an HTTP error status.
requirements: r must be a valid request record with headers already read.
If require_match is non-zero, the function will return an HTTP error status if the requested hostname does not match any ServerName/ServerAlias or VirtualHost address-spec within the selected chain.
Call after initial IP-based vhost selection (i.e., after ap_update_vhost_given_ip has identified the matching chain) and after headers are available.

functions.name: ap_matches_request_vhost
functions.signature: int ap_matches_request_vhost(request_rec *r, const char *host, apr_port_t port)
functions.description: Test whether the provided host:port matches any of the aliases of r->server for this request. Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r must be a valid request record.
host should be a non-NULL hostname to test; empty or NULL inputs are not specified in this header.
port must be a valid TCP/UDP port number in the range 0–65535 (based on apr_port_t semantics; precise constraints not stated here).

functions.name: ap_authn_cache_store
functions.signature: void ap_authn_cache_store(request_rec *r, const char *module, const char *user, const char *realm, const char *data)
functions.description: Optional function (exported via APR optional function mechanism) for authentication providers to store/look up results in mod_authn_cache. Call this to cache the value retrieved or computed during authentication for a given module, user, and realm (realm may be NULL for Basic auth). Returns void and performs caching as a side effect; availability depends on mod_authn_cache being loaded and the optional symbol being retrieved at runtime.
requirements: This is an APR optional function; callers must retrieve it at runtime (e.g., via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN("ap_authn_cache_store")) and verify the returned pointer is non-NULL before calling.
r must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an active request_rec for the current request.
user should be a valid NUL-terminated C string identifying the user (exact constraints not documented).
realm may be NULL for Basic authentication; otherwise, if provided, it should be a valid NUL-terminated C string representing the authn realm.
module should identify the calling module (format unspecified; must be a valid NUL-terminated C string).
data is the value looked up by the authn provider to cache; it should be a valid NUL-terminated C string and valid for the duration of the call.
Function returns void; callers should not expect error codes and must rely on logging or downstream behavior to detect failures (not documented).

functions.name: ap_http_filter
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_http_filter(ap_filter_t *f, apr_bucket_brigade *b, ap_input_mode_t mode, apr_read_type_e block, apr_off_t readbytes);
functions.description: Core HTTP input filter. Reads request data from the connection into the provided bucket brigade according to the requested input mode, blocking behavior, and maximum bytes. Intended for internal mod_core use within the input filter chain.
requirements: f must be a valid, initialized ap_filter_t* that is part of the active connection/request input filter chain.
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* owned by the caller to receive input data.
mode must be a valid ap_input_mode_t (e.g., AP_MODE_READBYTES/AP_MODE_SPECULATIVE/etc.).
block must be a valid apr_read_type_e (APR_BLOCK_READ or APR_NONBLOCK_READ).
readbytes should be >= 0; when mode is AP_MODE_READBYTES this typically limits the amount of data read.
Should be invoked by the server’s filter framework, not called directly by modules unless integrating with the core filter stack.

functions.name: ap_h1_request_in_filter
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_h1_request_in_filter(ap_filter_t *f, apr_bucket_brigade *bb, ap_input_mode_t mode, apr_read_type_e block, apr_off_t readbytes);
functions.description: HTTP/1.x request header parsing input filter. Processes/normalizes incoming request header bytes for HTTP/1.x and passes them upstream. Internal to mod_core’s input processing.
requirements: f must be a valid, active input filter (ap_filter_t*).
bb must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* to receive filtered data.
mode must be a valid ap_input_mode_t.
block must be APR_BLOCK_READ or APR_NONBLOCK_READ.
readbytes should be >= 0 when applicable.
Typically installed and invoked by the server’s filter framework for HTTP/1.x requests; not intended for direct use by modules.

functions.name: ap_h1_body_in_filter
functions.signature: apr_status_t ap_h1_body_in_filter(ap_filter_t *f, apr_bucket_brigade *b, ap_input_mode_t mode, apr_read_type_e block, apr_off_t readbytes);
functions.description: HTTP/1.x request body input filter. Reads and decodes the request body (handling content-length, chunked encoding, etc.) and delivers data into the brigade per the requested mode/block semantics.
requirements: f must be a valid, active input filter (ap_filter_t*).
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* for output data.
mode must be a valid ap_input_mode_t.
block must be APR_BLOCK_READ or APR_NONBLOCK_READ.
readbytes should be >= 0 when applicable.
Intended to be invoked by Apache’s input filter stack; typically not called directly by third-party modules.

functions.name: ap_h1_response_out_filter
functions.description: HTTP/1.1 response formatting output filter. Formats response headers/status for HTTP/1.1 on output and passes buckets down the filter chain.
requirements: f must be a valid, active output filter (ap_filter_t*).
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* containing response data/metadata to be formatted and forwarded.
Should be installed and called by the server’s output filter framework; not typically invoked directly by modules.

functions.name: ap_http_chunk_filter
functions.description: HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer-encoding output filter. Encodes the outgoing response body using chunked transfer-coding when appropriate and forwards the resulting buckets.
requirements: f must be a valid, active output filter (ap_filter_t*).
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* containing the body data to encode/forward.
Generally applied when response uses chunked transfer-coding; typically installed/called by the server’s filter framework.

functions.name: ap_http_outerror_filter
functions.description: Output filter that processes error buckets on the output chain. Ensures proper handling/formatting of error conditions during response generation.
requirements: f must be a valid, active output filter (ap_filter_t*).
b must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* possibly containing error buckets to be handled.
Invoked by the server’s output filter pipeline; not generally called directly by modules.

functions.name: ap_response_code_string
functions.description: Returns a textual string for an HTTP response code/index associated with the given request. Exact mapping/semantics of error_index are not documented here; likely maps to HTTP status codes or table indices. Details are unknown in this header.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current request.
error_index should be a valid index/code expected by the core (exact valid range/values are unknown from this header).
Caller should not assume the returned string’s lifetime beyond typical request scope unless documented elsewhere (unknown here).

functions.name: ap_basic_http_header
functions.description: Adds/sends the minimal part of an HTTP response header for the current request into the provided brigade. Intended for special cases; most modules should rely on the server’s default header generation to preserve HTTP/1.1 correctness.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current request.
bb must be a valid, initialized apr_bucket_brigade* that the caller will pass down the output chain.
Use with caution: modules should prefer the default header generation path; incorrect use can break HTTP/1.1 compliance (per the warning in the header comments).

functions.name: ap_send_http_trace
functions.description: Generates and sends an appropriate response to an HTTP TRACE request. Returns DONE or an HTTP status code if it handles the TRACE, or DECLINED if the request method is not TRACE.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* representing the current request.
Caller must inspect the return value: DONE or an HTTP error status indicates the request has been handled; DECLINED indicates it was not a TRACE request and normal processing should continue.

functions.name: ap_send_http_options
functions.description: Generates and sends an appropriate response to an HTTP OPTIONS request for the current request/URI/server context.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current request.
Caller should handle/propagate the returned HTTP status code as appropriate.

functions.name: ap_init_rng
functions.description: Initializes the server’s RNG at startup using the provided pool for allocation/cleanup. Should be called during server initialization.
requirements: p must be a valid, long-lived APR pool (typically a process or server pool) available at startup.
Call during startup/initialization before RNG is used elsewhere.

functions.name: ap_random_parent_after_fork
functions.description: Updates the RNG state in the parent process after a fork to maintain randomness and avoid state reuse.
requirements: Call in the parent process after a fork event (not in the child).
Should be invoked after any fork that occurs during the server’s lifetime to reseed/update RNG as required.

functions.name: ap_h1_set_keepalive
functions.description: Determines and sets the keep-alive status for the given HTTP/1.x request based on the response being sent. Returns 1 if keep-alive can be enabled, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current request.
resp must be a valid ap_bucket_response* representing the response that will be sent.
Caller should check the return value to decide whether to keep the connection alive.

functions.name: ap_request_insert_filter
functions.description: Adds the mod_request keep-body input filter to the given request’s filter chain so that the request body can be preserved/kept for later consumption. This function is declared as an APR optional function; callers must retrieve it at runtime (e.g., via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN) and verify availability. Typical usage is early in request processing, before the request body is read, to enable buffering/retention (filters commonly identified in this module by names like KEEP_BODY_FILTER/KEPT_BODY_FILTER). Exact buffering semantics and limits depend on mod_request’s configuration (e.g., per-directory keep_body). Unknown: precise timing guarantees and whether multiple insertions are idempotent.
requirements: The function is optional; retrieve it via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(ap_request_insert_filter) and verify the returned pointer is non-NULL before calling.
The request_rec pointer r must be a valid, live request context associated with the current request; r must not be NULL.
Call before the request body is consumed if the intent is to keep/preserve the body (inferred from filter insertion behavior).
mod_request must be loaded/available so that the optional function is registered (inferred from being an APR optional function).
Thread-safety and reentrancy constraints follow httpd request processing conventions; do not call after the request has been finalized (inferred).

functions.name: ap_request_remove_filter
functions.description: Removes the mod_request keep-body input filter from the given request’s filter chain, disabling further body preservation for that request. This is an APR optional function; callers must retrieve it dynamically (e.g., via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN) and check availability. Use during request processing when the keep-body functionality is no longer needed or to revert earlier insertion. Unknown: whether removal is a no-op if the filter was not present and whether multiple removals are safe/idempotent.
requirements: The function is optional; retrieve it via APR_RETRIEVE_OPTIONAL_FN(ap_request_remove_filter) and verify the returned pointer is non-NULL before calling.
The request_rec pointer r must be a valid, live request context associated with the current request; r must not be NULL.
Call during the lifetime of the request and before request teardown to modify the active filter chain (inferred from filter manipulation semantics).
mod_request must be loaded/available so that the optional function is registered (inferred).

functions.name: ap_reclaim_child_processes
functions.description: Reclaim (wait for) MPM child processes and other registered children to exit. Optionally sends SIGTERM each loop when terminate != 0. Invokes the provided callback for each dead child. Intended for use by the parent process during shutdown/restart.
requirements: Must be called by the parent process that spawned the children.
terminate must be 0 or 1, per documentation.
mpm_callback, if non-NULL, must point to a function of type ap_reclaim_callback_fn_t and must be safe to call for each reaped child.
Children considered include those in the scoreboard and those registered via ap_register_extra_mpm_process().

functions.name: ap_relieve_child_processes
functions.description: Reaps (relieves) any exited MPM children and other registered processes without force-signalling. Invokes the provided callback for each dead child.
requirements: Should be called by the parent process.
mpm_callback, if non-NULL, must be a valid ap_reclaim_callback_fn_t and safe to call.
Operates on children listed in the scoreboard and those registered via ap_register_extra_mpm_process().

functions.name: ap_register_extra_mpm_process
functions.description: Registers an MPM child process that is not tracked in the scoreboard so it can be reclaimed by ap_reclaim_child_processes()/ap_relieve_child_processes().
requirements: pid must be a valid process id of a current extra MPM child.
gen must be the generation of that MPM child.
Call ap_unregister_extra_mpm_process() if the process terminates before reclamation.

functions.name: ap_unregister_extra_mpm_process
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered extra MPM child process. Returns 1 if found/removed, 0 otherwise, and optionally returns its generation via old_gen.
requirements: pid must be the process ID previously registered via ap_register_extra_mpm_process().
old_gen may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid pointer to receive the generation.

functions.name: ap_mpm_safe_kill
functions.description: Safely sends a signal to a child process only if it belongs to the current process group. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success or an error per kill(3); APR_EINVAL for invalid pid (<1) or if the pid is not in the current process group.
requirements: pid must be >= 1.
sig must be a valid signal number for the platform.
Only succeeds if the target pid is in the current process group; otherwise returns APR_EINVAL.

functions.name: ap_process_child_status
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(int) ap_process_child_status(apr_proc_t *pid, apr_exit_why_e why, int status);
functions.description: Logs and processes the termination status of a child process that exited without being signaled by the parent. Returns 0 on success or APEXIT_CHILDFATAL if the MPM should terminate.
requirements: pid must reference the child process whose status is being processed.
why must be a valid apr_exit_why_e explaining how the process exited.
status must be the status code returned by ap_wait_or_timeout or wait APIs.

functions.name: ap_fatal_signal_setup
functions.description: Installs fatal signal handlers in the parent process so that crashes produce useful diagnostics and cleanup. Returns APR status.
requirements: s must be a valid server_rec.
in_pconf must be a valid pool for any required allocations.
Should be called during server startup (parent context).

functions.name: ap_fatal_signal_child_setup
functions.description: Configures fatal signal handling appropriate for child processes. Returns APR status.
requirements: Must be called in a child process context.
s must be a valid server_rec.

functions.name: ap_mpm_end_gen_helper
functions.description: Pool cleanup function used by the end-generation hook implementation to perform generation-end tasks. Intended to be registered as a pool cleanup.
requirements: Argument is ignored; callers typically register this with a pool cleanup mechanism and pass a placeholder pointer.
Must be called by APR pool cleanup machinery.

functions.name: ap_wait_or_timeout
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_wait_or_timeout(apr_exit_why_e *status, int *exitcode, apr_proc_t *ret, apr_pool_t *p, server_rec *s);
functions.description: Runs the monitor hook periodically, waits for terminated child processes, and if none are found sleeps for one second. Fills out status, exitcode, and ret for a dead child if any.
requirements: status, exitcode, and ret must be valid pointers to receive output.
p must be a valid APR pool for any temporary allocations.
s must be a valid server_rec.
Caller should inspect output parameters to determine whether a process exited.

functions.name: ap_sock_disable_nagle
functions.description: Disables Nagle’s algorithm (TCP_NODELAY) on the given socket to reduce latency for persistent connections. On platforms without TCP_NODELAY, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: s must be a valid, open APR socket.
Effective only when TCP_NODELAY is available; otherwise expands to a no-op.

functions.name: ap_uname2id
functions.description: Converts a username string to its numeric user ID (uid).
requirements: Available only when HAVE_GETPWNAM is defined on the platform.
name must be a non-NULL, valid username present in the system user database.

functions.name: ap_gname2id
functions.description: Converts a group name string to its numeric group ID (gid).
requirements: Available only when HAVE_GETGRNAM is defined on the platform.
name must be a non-NULL, valid group name present in the system group database.

functions.name: initgroups
functions.description: Fallback implementation declaration for initgroups(3): initializes the supplementary group access list for a user and adds basegid.
requirements: Declared only when HAVE_INITGROUPS is not defined.
name must be non-NULL.
basegid is added to the group list. Return value 0 indicates success per documentation.

functions.name: ap_mpm_pod_open
functions.description: Creates and opens a pipe-of-death (POD) used by the parent to signal children to shut down gracefully.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool for allocations.
pod must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated ap_pod_t*.
Intended for use by the parent process.

functions.name: ap_mpm_pod_check
functions.description: Checks the POD to determine if the current process has been signaled to shut down.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t* previously opened with ap_mpm_pod_open or ap_mpm_podx_open.

functions.name: ap_mpm_pod_close
functions.description: Closes the pipe-of-death and releases associated resources.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t* previously opened.
After closing, the pod should not be used.

functions.name: ap_mpm_pod_signal
functions.description: Writes to the POD to signal that one child process should exit.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t* opened by ap_mpm_pod_open.
Caller should be the parent or a controller responsible for signaling children.

functions.name: ap_mpm_pod_killpg
functions.description: Signals via the POD that a process group of children (num children) should exit.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t*.
num must be a non-negative integer indicating how many child processes to signal.

functions.name: ap_mpm_podx_open
functions.description: Opens the extended POD capable of conveying restart type (normal or graceful).
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool.
pod must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created ap_pod_t*.

functions.name: ap_mpm_podx_check
functions.description: Checks the extended POD and returns a code indicating whether to restart normally, restart gracefully, or not restart.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t* created by ap_mpm_podx_open.
Return values correspond to ap_podx_restart_t semantics: AP_MPM_PODX_NORESTART, AP_MPM_PODX_RESTART, AP_MPM_PODX_GRACEFUL.

functions.name: ap_mpm_podx_close
functions.description: Closes the extended pipe-of-death.
requirements: pod must be a valid ap_pod_t* previously opened by ap_mpm_podx_open.

functions.name: ap_mpm_podx_signal
functions.description: Signals via the extended POD that one child should exit, specifying the restart type (none, restart, or graceful).
requirements: pod must be a valid extended POD.
graceful must be one of ap_podx_restart_t values.

functions.name: ap_mpm_podx_killpg
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_mpm_podx_killpg(ap_pod_t *pod, int num, ap_podx_restart_t graceful);
functions.description: Signals via the extended POD that num children should exit, indicating the restart type.
requirements: pod must be a valid extended POD.
num must be a non-negative integer.
graceful must be a valid ap_podx_restart_t value.

functions.name: ap_check_mpm
functions.description: Verifies that exactly one MPM is loaded. Returns NULL if the configuration is valid; otherwise returns an error string.
requirements: Call after modules are loaded/selected to validate MPM configuration.
Caller must handle a non-NULL returned error string as configuration error.

functions.name: ap_mpm_set_max_requests

functions.name: ap_mpm_set_graceful_shutdown
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(const char *) ap_mpm_set_graceful_shutdown(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);

functions.name: ap_mpm_set_max_mem_free

functions.name: monitor
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; modules may implement this to be called periodically by some MPMs in the parent process. Purpose: periodic monitoring/housekeeping in the parent. Expected usage: register a callback matching this signature using the hook API (e.g., ap_hook_monitor); it may be invoked at intervals depending on the MPM. Notes: This hook is not portable across all platforms/MPMs; return OK or DECLINED (errors are ignored).
requirements: Must be safe to run in the parent process context (not all MPMs call it).
