functions.name: drop_privileges
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; modules may implement this to manage system security (e.g., dropping privileges). Purpose: participate in privilege dropping in the child process. Expected usage: register a callback matching this signature using the hook API. Notes: Specific semantics are not documented here; behavior is MPM/module-specific.
requirements: Must be safe to run in a child process context.
Return value conventions are not documented; typical hook practice is to return OK/DECLINED, but exact requirements are unknown due to missing docs.

functions.name: mpm_query
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; implementers (typically the MPM) answer MPM capability/setting queries. Purpose: provide information about the active MPM. Expected usage: handlers set *result and/or *rv based on query_code. Notes: Comment specifies the overall ap_mpm_query contract.
requirements: For unimplemented query codes, the MPM should return OK and set *rv to APR_ENOTIMPL (per comment: "OK+APR_ENOTIMPL").
Modules that only handle some query codes should return DECLINED for others (per comment).
Caller must provide non-NULL pointers for result and rv when expecting outputs; otherwise behavior is MPM-specific (not documented here).

functions.name: mpm_register_timed_callback
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; registers a callback to be invoked after a specified time t. Purpose: schedule a timed callback within the MPM. Expected usage: pass the delay/when (t), the callback function pointer, and an opaque baton passed back on invocation. Notes: Precise timing semantics and lifetime of registration are MPM-specific and not documented here.
requirements: cbfn must be a valid function pointer of type ap_mpm_callback_fn_t (declared in ap_mpm.h).
baton is an opaque pointer that must remain valid until the callback is invoked or unregistered (exact lifecycle unspecified).

functions.name: mpm_register_poll_callback
functions.signature: apr_status_t mpm_register_poll_callback(apr_pool_t *p, const apr_array_header_t *pds, ap_mpm_callback_fn_t *cbfn, void *baton)
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; registers a callback associated with polling a set of descriptors. Purpose: integrate a module’s callback with the MPM’s poll loop. Expected usage: provide a pool for allocation, an array of poll descriptors (pds), the callback, and a baton. Notes: Details of descriptor type and invocation conditions are MPM-specific and not documented here.

functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; like mpm_register_poll_callback, but also registers a timeout callback and timeout value. Purpose: integrate callbacks into the MPM poll loop with a timeout action. Expected usage: supply poll descriptors, a normal callback (cbfn), a timeout callback (tofn), a baton, and timeout. Notes: Exact semantics (edge cases, one-shot vs repeating) are MPM-specific and not documented here.

pds must describe valid poll descriptors acceptable to the MPM.
cbfn and tofn must be valid function pointers of type ap_mpm_callback_fn_t.
baton should remain valid while either callback may be invoked.
timeout must be a valid apr_time_t; interpretation is MPM-specific (not documented).

functions.name: mpm_resume_suspended
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; request the MPM to resume a previously suspended connection. Purpose: resume handling of a connection that was disassociated from a thread. Expected usage: modules call the run function for this hook to ask the MPM to resume c. Notes: Applicable only to MPMs that support connection suspension; not all MPMs implement it.
requirements: c must be a valid pointer to a connection that is currently suspended by the MPM; otherwise behavior is MPM-defined/unknown.

functions.name: mpm_get_name
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; returns the active MPM’s name (e.g., "prefork", "event"). Purpose: identify the current MPM. Expected usage: modules obtain a string identifier for conditional behavior. Notes: The string is managed by the MPM and should be treated as read-only.
requirements: No arguments; caller should not modify the returned string.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: output_pending
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; determine whether the write completion phase should continue. Purpose: let MPM/modules decide if more output work is pending. Expected usage: invoked with current connection; returns OK to continue, DECLINED to end gracefully, or a positive error to begin lingering close.
requirements: c must be a valid connection_rec pointer.
Return OK if write completion should continue, DECLINED if it should end gracefully, or a positive error value to indicate lingering should begin (per comment).

functions.name: input_pending
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; determine if input filters have pending data that can be read without blocking. Purpose: non-blocking read readiness hint. Expected usage: return OK if a read can proceed without blocking, DECLINED if it would block.
requirements: c must be a valid connection_rec pointer.
Return OK only when data can be read without blocking; return DECLINED when a read would block (per comment).

functions.name: suspend_connection
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; notification that connection handling is suspending (disassociating from the current thread). Purpose: inform modules that the active connection (and possibly current request) is being suspended. Expected usage: modules may save state or adjust resources. Notes: Not implemented by Prefork/Worker MPMs; called on the thread that was processing the connection; not called at end of connection processing; may not be called for I/O-only resuspension with no non-MPM code executed.
requirements: c must be a valid connection_rec pointer.
r may be NULL if there is no active request (per comment).
Implementations must not assume this is called by all MPMs; Prefork/Worker do not call it (per comment).
Must not assume it is called at the end of connection processing; it only signals suspension (per comment).

functions.name: resume_connection
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; notification that connection handling is resuming (associating with a thread). Purpose: inform modules that processing of a previously-suspended connection is resuming. Expected usage: modules may restore state/resources. Notes: Not implemented by Prefork/Worker; called on the thread that will resume processing; not called at the beginning of connection processing; may not be called for I/O-only resumption with no non-MPM code executed.
requirements: c must be a valid connection_rec pointer.
r may be NULL if there is no active request (per comment).
Implementations must not assume this is called by all MPMs; Prefork/Worker do not call it (per comment).
Must not assume it is called at the beginning of connection processing; it only signals resumption for a previously suspended connection (per comment).

functions.name: child_stopping
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; notification that the child is stopping and no new requests/tasks should be started. Purpose: allow modules to prepare for shutdown; if graceful, already-started work should proceed normally. Expected usage: use pchild for any temporary allocations; check graceful to distinguish graceful vs immediate shutdown.
requirements: pchild must be a valid child pool pointer.
graceful is non-zero iff this is a graceful shutdown (per comment).
Implementations should stop initiating new work and, if graceful != 0, allow already-started work to continue (per comment).

functions.name: child_stopped
functions.description: Hook callback signature declared via AP_DECLARE_HOOK; notification that the child has stopped processing requests completely and running threads should be shut down. Purpose: allow modules to tear down per-child threads/resources. Expected usage: ideally ensure no more threads are running when this completes; global resource deallocation should be done via pool destroy callbacks after this. Notes: graceful indicates graceful shutdown.
requirements: pchild must be a valid child pool pointer.
graceful is non-zero iff this is a graceful shutdown (per comment).
Implementations should ensure threads in the child are shut down by the time the hook completes (per comment).
Global resource deallocation should be handled via memory pool destroy callbacks after this (per comment).

functions.name: mpm_common_pre_config
functions.description: Performs internal pre-configuration for MPM-related settings. Intended to be called only from core's pre-config hook.
requirements: pconf must be a valid APR pool.
Should only be called from the core’s pre-configuration hook, not by external modules.

functions.name: ap_create_scoreboard
functions.description: Create the Apache runtime scoreboard (shared or local) using the given APR pool and scoreboard sharing mode. Typical usage: called early by the MPM to set up scoreboard storage before workers start.
requirements: p must be a valid, live APR pool used for allocation.
t must be a valid ap_scoreboard_e value (SB_NOT_SHARED or SB_SHARED).

functions.name: ap_cleanup_scoreboard

Return value is an apr_status_t; callers should handle APR error codes.

functions.description: Report whether a scoreboard image exists (has been created and is accessible). Intended for modules/MPMs to gate scoreboard operations.

functions.name: ap_increment_counts

functions.name: ap_reopen_scoreboard

functions.description: Initialize the in-memory scoreboard structures, optionally with a pointer to shared memory that backs the scoreboard.
requirements: shared_score must point to valid, appropriately sized shared memory (when using SB_SHARED), or may be null/ignored depending on build/MPM; exact requirement is not documented in this header.
Must be called after scoreboard allocation/creation and before worker processes/threads start updating entries.

functions.name: ap_calc_scoreboard_size
functions.description: Compute the size in bytes required for the scoreboard shared memory (or backing storage) for the current server limits/configuration.
requirements: Server limit and thread limit configuration must be finalized prior to calling to get an accurate size.

functions.name: ap_create_sb_handle
functions.signature: void ap_create_sb_handle(ap_sb_handle_t **new_sbh, apr_pool_t *p, int child_num, int thread_num);
functions.description: Create a scoreboard handle that refers to a specific child/thread slot. The handle is used to update worker status and counters.

requirements: sbh must be a valid scoreboard handle.

functions.description: Locate a child process index given an APR process descriptor. Typically returns the child slot number or -1 if not found.
requirements: pid must be a valid pointer to an apr_proc_t representing a running/known child process.

functions.name: ap_update_child_status
functions.description: Update the worker status in the scoreboard for the given handle using one of the SERVER_* status codes. Optionally associates request context.
requirements: sbh must be valid.
status must be one of the SERVER_* constants defined in this header (e.g., SERVER_READY, SERVER_BUSY_READ, etc.).

functions.signature: int ap_update_child_status_from_indexes(int child_num, int thread_num, int status, request_rec *r);

functions.description: Update a worker's status using a connection object (conn_rec) for context.
requirements: sbh must be valid.

functions.name: ap_update_child_status_from_server

functions.description: Mark the start or stop of timing for processing a request in the scoreboard. The status argument selects start or stop.

functions.name: ap_set_time_process_request

functions.description: Explicitly set the begin and end timestamps for processing a request in the scoreboard.
requirements: sbh must be valid.
timebeg and timeend are absolute apr_time_t timestamps; exact expected ordering is not documented here.

functions.name: ap_update_global_status
functions.description: Update aggregate/global scoreboard metrics (e.g., counts across processes/threads). Intended to be called by the MPM or status-updating code.
requirements: Must be called after the scoreboard has been created/initialized.

functions.name: ap_get_scoreboard_worker
functions.description: Return a pointer to the worker_score structure for the given scoreboard handle.
requirements: sbh must be valid.
Returned pointer refers to a scoreboard entry; lifetime and mutability depend on scoreboard sharing mode.

functions.name: ap_get_scoreboard_worker_from_indexes
functions.description: Deprecated: Return a pointer to the worker_score for a given child/thread index pair. Prefer ap_copy_scoreboard_worker instead.

functions.description: Copy the contents of a worker_score entry for the given child/thread into the caller-provided dest structure.
requirements: dest must be a non-null pointer to writable memory sized as worker_score.

functions.description: Return a pointer to the process_score entry for the specified child process slot index.

requirements: Scoreboard must have been created/initialized before calling.
Returned pointer refers to internal scoreboard storage.

functions.name: ap_set_scoreboard
functions.description: Configuration directive handler to set the scoreboard filename or mode. Called by the Apache config parser during directive processing.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer provided by the config parser.
dummy is module-specific and typically unused here.

requirements: cmd must be valid.
dummy is module-specific and typically unused.

functions.name: ap_set_reqtail

functions.name: ap_hook_pre_mpm
functions.signature: void ap_hook_pre_mpm(ap_HOOK_pre_mpm_t *pf, const char * const *aszPre, const char * const *aszSucc, int nOrder)
functions.description: Registers a module callback to the pre_mpm hook, which runs after the scoreboard is created and before the MPM starts. The registered callback must have the signature: int callback(apr_pool_t *p, ap_scoreboard_e sb_type). Typical usage is inside a module’s register_hooks() to arrange execution order relative to other modules. The callback should return OK or DECLINE on success; any other value is treated as an error by the hook runner.
requirements: pf must be a valid pointer to a function with signature: int (apr_pool_t *p, ap_scoreboard_e sb_type).
The callback’s return value is expected to be OK or DECLINE on success; any other value indicates an error (per the hook’s documentation).

aszPre and aszSucc, if provided, specify ordering constraints relative to other module names; if provided they should follow Apache’s convention of NULL-terminated arrays of const char* module names. They may be NULL if no ordering is needed.
nOrder should be one of the standard Apache hook order constants (e.g., APR_HOOK_FIRST, APR_HOOK_MIDDLE, APR_HOOK_LAST).
Should be called during module hook registration (e.g., in the module’s register_hooks function) before the server starts processing requests.

functions.name: ap_add_node
functions.description: Adds a directive node into the Apache HTTP Server configuration tree and returns the node that was added. The function links the provided node (toadd) either as a child (when child is non-zero) or at the same level as current (when child is zero). If the node is added as a first child, the value pointed to by parent may be updated to reflect the new current node. Typical usage is during configuration parsing to build the tree of directives and their nested blocks. Implementation details and exact linkage behavior (e.g., updating next/first_child/last) are not documented here; only the general intent is known from the header comments.
requirements: parent: a pointer to a variable holding the current parent ap_directive_t*. It may be modified by the function when adding a first child (per header comment). The header does not state whether NULL is allowed.
current: the current node at the level where insertion occurs. The header does not define whether NULL is permitted; behavior when NULL is passed is unspecified.
toadd: must be a valid, initialized ap_directive_t* representing the node to insert into the tree. Passing NULL would be invalid/meaningless.
child: treated as a boolean flag; non-zero indicates the node is to be added as a child node. Exact accepted range beyond 0/non-zero is not specified.

Return value: the function returns the added node; no error reporting mechanism is documented (no errno or status code), so callers should assume a non-NULL return on success. Error handling behavior is otherwise unspecified.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; callers should assume tree construction is not thread-safe unless externally serialized.

functions.name: ap_cookie_write
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_cookie_write(request_rec * r, const char *name, const char *val, const char *attrs, long maxage, ...) AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL;
functions.description: Write an RFC2109-compliant Set-Cookie header. Adds a cookie with the given name and value and optional attributes to one or more apr_table_t destinations provided via varargs. If attrs is NULL, DEFAULT_ATTRS is used. If maxage is non-zero, a Max-Age attribute is included. Intended for use within an Apache module handling a request.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* representing the current HTTP request.
name must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string; cookie name should be sane (see ap_cookie_check_string).
val must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string (may be empty if a blank value is desired).
attrs may be NULL to use DEFAULT_ATTRS; if non-NULL it must be a valid NUL-terminated string of cookie attributes.
maxage controls inclusion of Max-Age; non-zero adds a Max-Age attribute. No specific range constraints are documented beyond type long.
The variadic arguments must be zero or more apr_table_t* followed by a terminating NULL sentinel (AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL).
Each apr_table_t* provided via varargs must be a valid, initialized table suitable for receiving Set-Cookie headers.

functions.name: ap_cookie_write2
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_cookie_write2(request_rec * r, const char *name2, const char *val, const char *attrs2, long maxage, ...) AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL;
functions.description: Write an RFC2965-compliant Set-Cookie2 header. Adds a cookie with the given name and value and optional attributes to one or more apr_table_t destinations provided via varargs. If attrs2 is NULL, DEFAULT_ATTRS is used. If maxage is non-zero, a Max-Age attribute is included. Intended for use within an Apache module handling a request.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current HTTP request.
name2 must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string; cookie name should be sane (see ap_cookie_check_string).
val must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string.
attrs2 may be NULL to use DEFAULT_ATTRS; if non-NULL it must be a valid NUL-terminated string of cookie attributes.
maxage non-zero adds Max-Age; no further constraints documented.
The variadic arguments must be zero or more apr_table_t* followed by a terminating NULL sentinel (AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL).
Each apr_table_t* provided via varargs must be a valid, initialized table suitable for receiving Set-Cookie2 headers.

functions.name: ap_cookie_remove
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_cookie_remove(request_rec * r, const char *name, const char *attrs, ...) AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL;
functions.description: Remove (expire) an RFC2109 cookie by adding an appropriate Set-Cookie header. If attrs is NULL, CLEAR_ATTRS is used. The cookie header is added to one or more apr_table_t destinations provided via varargs.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current HTTP request.
name must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string identifying the cookie to remove.
attrs may be NULL to use CLEAR_ATTRS; if non-NULL it must be a valid NUL-terminated string of cookie attributes.
The variadic arguments must be zero or more apr_table_t* followed by a terminating NULL sentinel (AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL).
Each apr_table_t* provided via varargs must be a valid, initialized table suitable for receiving Set-Cookie headers.

functions.name: ap_cookie_remove2
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_cookie_remove2(request_rec * r, const char *name2, const char *attrs2, ...) AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL;
functions.description: Remove (expire) an RFC2965 cookie by adding an appropriate Set-Cookie2 header. If attrs2 is NULL, CLEAR_ATTRS is used. The cookie header is added to one or more apr_table_t destinations provided via varargs.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current HTTP request.
name2 must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string identifying the cookie to remove.
attrs2 may be NULL to use CLEAR_ATTRS; if non-NULL it must be a valid NUL-terminated string of cookie attributes.
The variadic arguments must be zero or more apr_table_t* followed by a terminating NULL sentinel (AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL).
Each apr_table_t* provided via varargs must be a valid, initialized table suitable for receiving Set-Cookie2 headers.

functions.name: ap_cookie_read
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_cookie_read(request_rec * r, const char *name, const char **val, int remove);
functions.description: Read a cookie with the given name from the incoming request. Scans both Cookie and Cookie2 headers. On success, stores a pointer to the cookie value in *val. If the cookie is duplicated, returns APR_EGENERAL. If found and remove is non-zero, the cookie is removed from the headers to prevent forwarding to backends.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec* for the current HTTP request.
name must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string specifying the cookie name to look up.
val must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting value pointer on success.
remove is an integer flag; if non-zero, the function will remove the cookie from the request headers upon successful read.
Caller should handle APR_EGENERAL specifically to detect duplicate cookies; other apr_status_t values may indicate not found or errors (exact set not documented).

functions.name: ap_cookie_check_string
functions.description: Sanity-check a string (typically a cookie name). Verifies that it exists, is not empty, and does not contain the special characters '=', ';', or '&'. Use this before creating or processing cookie names.
requirements: string must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string (must exist and not be NULL).
Empty strings are considered invalid by this check.
The string must not contain '=', ';', or '&' to pass the check.
Caller should examine the returned apr_status_t to determine validity (APR_SUCCESS on pass; specific error codes not documented).

functions.name: ap_init_ebcdic
functions.description: Initializes global character-set translation handlers for EBCDIC builds, allocating any needed resources from the provided APR pool. Intended to prepare the server’s translation tables so later protocol conversions can occur. On non-EBCDIC systems this function does not exist and should be compiled out (guard with #if APR_CHARSET_EBCDIC).
requirements: Only available when APR_CHARSET_EBCDIC is true (must be compiled under that guard).
pool must be a valid, live apr_pool_t* from which allocations are permitted.
Should be invoked before using protocol conversion helpers (inferred from purpose).
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for success/failure (inferred from return type).

functions.name: ap_xlate_proto_to_ascii
functions.description: Converts protocol data in-place from the server’s implementation character set (e.g., EBCDIC) to ASCII for transmission. On non-EBCDIC systems this is compiled to an empty macro (no-op).
requirements: buffer points to writable memory containing at least len bytes.
len is the number of bytes to translate; if 0, no bytes are translated (inferred from common semantics).
Only meaningful when APR_CHARSET_EBCDIC is true; otherwise expands to a no-op macro.
Buffer contents are modified in place; pass mutable storage, not string literals (inferred from signature).

functions.name: ap_xlate_proto_from_ascii
functions.description: Converts protocol data in-place from ASCII to the server’s implementation character set (e.g., EBCDIC) after receipt. On non-EBCDIC systems this is compiled to an empty macro (no-op).
requirements: buffer points to writable memory containing at least len bytes.
len is the number of bytes to translate; if 0, no bytes are translated (inferred from common semantics).
Only meaningful when APR_CHARSET_EBCDIC is true; otherwise expands to a no-op macro.
Buffer contents are modified in place; pass mutable storage, not string literals (inferred from signature).

functions.name: ap_rvputs_proto_in_ascii
functions.description: Converts the given variable list of strings from the implementation character set to ASCII and writes them to the client for the specified request. The argument list must be terminated by a NULL pointer. On non-EBCDIC systems this is replaced by a direct call to ap_rvputs.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to an initialized request_rec associated with an active request.
The variadic arguments are char* string pointers terminated by a final NULL pointer, with no count parameter.
Only meaningful as a distinct function when APR_CHARSET_EBCDIC is true; otherwise maps to ap_rvputs.
Return value is an int; exact success/byte-count semantics follow ap_rvputs (not specified here; unknown details).

functions.name: ap_fcgi_header_to_array
functions.description: Packs an ap_fcgi_header struct into its wire-format 8-byte FastCGI record header array. Use when serializing a header to send over the FastCGI protocol.
requirements: h must point to a valid, initialized ap_fcgi_header structure.
a must point to a writable buffer of at least AP_FCGI_HEADER_LEN (8) bytes.
The caller is responsible for ensuring field values in h (e.g., version, type, lengths) are set to valid FastCGI values before packing.

functions.name: ap_fcgi_header_from_array
functions.description: Unpacks an 8-byte FastCGI record header array into an ap_fcgi_header structure. Use when parsing received FastCGI headers.
requirements: h must point to a writable ap_fcgi_header structure.
a must point to a readable buffer of at least AP_FCGI_HEADER_LEN (8) bytes containing a FastCGI header.
The buffer a should contain data in FastCGI header wire format (version, type, requestId, contentLength, paddingLength, reserved).

functions.name: ap_fcgi_header_fields_from_array
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(void) ap_fcgi_header_fields_from_array(unsigned char *version,
                                                  unsigned char *type,
                                                  apr_uint16_t *request_id,
                                                  apr_uint16_t *content_len,
                                                  unsigned char *padding_len,
                                                  unsigned char a[]);
functions.description: Unpacks an 8-byte FastCGI header array directly into individual output fields without using an intermediate ap_fcgi_header struct. Useful for lightweight parsing.
requirements: version, type, request_id, content_len, and padding_len must be valid writable pointers.
a must point to a readable buffer of at least AP_FCGI_HEADER_LEN (8) bytes containing a FastCGI header.
The caller must manage endianness as implied by FastCGI (request_id and content_len are two-byte fields in network/wire order; the function handles decoding).

functions.name: ap_fcgi_begin_request_body_to_array
functions.description: Packs an ap_fcgi_begin_request_body structure into its 8-byte wire-format array for inclusion in an AP_FCGI_BEGIN_REQUEST record.
requirements: h must point to a valid, initialized ap_fcgi_begin_request_body structure (role bytes, flags set as needed).
a must point to a writable buffer of at least AP_FCGI_HEADER_LEN (8) bytes.
Flags and role fields should contain valid FastCGI values (e.g., AP_FCGI_RESPONDER, AP_FCGI_KEEP_CONN) before packing.

functions.name: ap_fcgi_fill_in_header
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(void) ap_fcgi_fill_in_header(ap_fcgi_header *header,
                                        unsigned char type,
                                        apr_uint16_t request_id,
                                        apr_uint16_t content_len,
                                        unsigned char padding_len);
functions.description: Initializes an ap_fcgi_header with the required FastCGI header fields for a record of the given type and lengths. Use prior to packing or sending a record header.
requirements: header must point to a writable ap_fcgi_header structure.
type must be a valid FastCGI record type (e.g., AP_FCGI_BEGIN_REQUEST, AP_FCGI_PARAMS, etc.).
content_len must be <= AP_FCGI_MAX_CONTENT_LEN (65535).
padding_len is the amount of padding bytes following content and should fit in an unsigned char (0–255).
request_id is a 16-bit identifier for the FastCGI request; choose appropriately for your connection/session.

functions.name: ap_fcgi_fill_in_request_body
functions.description: Initializes an ap_fcgi_begin_request_body with the provided role and flags for an AP_FCGI_BEGIN_REQUEST record.
requirements: brb must point to a writable ap_fcgi_begin_request_body structure.
role should be one of AP_FCGI_RESPONDER, AP_FCGI_AUTHORIZER, or AP_FCGI_FILTER.
flags should be 0 or a bitwise combination of defined flags such as AP_FCGI_KEEP_CONN.

functions.name: ap_fcgi_encoded_env_len
functions.description: Computes the number of bytes required to encode the next portion of the environment variable table into FastCGI name-value format, not exceeding maxlen (capped internally at AP_FCGI_MAX_CONTENT_LEN). Advances starting_elem to point to the next element for the following record.
requirements: env must be a valid apr_table_t containing environment variables to encode.
maxlen is the maximum allowed buffer size for this portion; effective limit is capped at AP_FCGI_MAX_CONTENT_LEN (65535).

starting_elem must be a valid pointer to an index into the table’s array; on input it specifies the next element to consider, and on output it is updated to the next element to process on the next record.
If the function returns 0 and starting_elem has reached the end of the table array, all variables have been encoded; otherwise, the next env var cannot fit within the specified limit.

functions.name: ap_fcgi_encode_env
functions.signature:
AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_fcgi_encode_env(request_rec *r,
                                            apr_table_t *env,
                                            void *buffer,
                                            apr_size_t buflen,
                                            int *starting_elem);
functions.description: Encodes the next portion of the environment table into FastCGI name-value format into the provided buffer. Use a buffer length previously computed by ap_fcgi_encoded_env_len. Returns APR_SUCCESS if encoded, or APR_ENOSPC if it does not fit.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec used for logging purposes.
env must be a valid apr_table_t containing environment variables to encode.
buffer must point to a writable buffer of size buflen bytes; buflen should be the value returned by ap_fcgi_encoded_env_len for the same segment.
starting_elem must be a valid pointer to an index; on input it specifies the next element to encode for this record, and on output it is updated to the next element to process on the next record.
Do not use the output starting_elem from ap_fcgi_encoded_env_len as the input starting_elem to ap_fcgi_encode_env when building the same FastCGI record (per note).
Caller must check the return value: APR_SUCCESS indicates data was encoded; APR_ENOSPC indicates the section could not be encoded in the provided buffer.

functions.name: ap_acquire_brigade
functions.description: Acquire a reusable apr_bucket_brigade allocated from the connection’s pool/allocator and return it cleaned up (emptied). Intended to reduce allocations by reusing brigades per-connection.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized conn_rec pointer for the active connection.
Returned brigade belongs to the connection pool/allocator; caller should cleanup/destroy after use per APR brigade rules (e.g., apr_brigade_cleanup/destroy when done).

functions.name: ap_release_brigade
functions.description: Release and cleanup a brigade previously acquired on the connection’s pool/allocator. Allows pooling/reuse of brigades per-connection.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized conn_rec pointer corresponding to the brigade’s allocation.
bb must be a brigade created on the connection pool/allocator (e.g., obtained via ap_acquire_brigade).
After return, bb should not be used unless reacquired (contents are cleaned up).

functions.name: ap_get_brigade
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_get_brigade(ap_filter_t *filter, apr_bucket_brigade *bucket, ap_input_mode_t mode, apr_read_type_e block, apr_off_t readbytes);
functions.description: Invoke the next input filter to populate the provided brigade according to the specified input mode, blocking behavior, and byte limit. Returns APR status; if the bottom-most filter doesn’t read from the network, AP_NOBODY_READ is returned. The brigade will be empty when there is no more data.
requirements: filter must point to the next input filter in the chain (non-NULL, initialized).
bucket must be a valid, empty apr_bucket_brigade when passed in.
mode must be a valid ap_input_mode_t value (e.g., AP_MODE_READBYTES, AP_MODE_GETLINE, etc.).
block must be APR_BLOCK_READ or APR_NONBLOCK_READ.
readbytes specifies the maximum bytes to read for AP_MODE_READBYTES (other modes may ignore or interpret it differently as per filter semantics).
Caller retains ownership of the brigade and is responsible for managing returned buckets per APR rules.

functions.name: ap_pass_brigade
functions.description: Pass the current bucket brigade to the next output filter in the chain. Returns APR status; AP_NOBODY_WROTE if the bottom-most filter doesn’t write to the network. Caller retains ownership of the brigade; on return its contents are undefined and must be cleaned up/destroyed.
requirements: filter must be a valid pointer to the next output filter in the chain.
bucket must be a valid brigade; after the call, its contents are undefined and the caller must call apr_brigade_cleanup or apr_brigade_destroy.
Caller must not assume any particular state of buckets in bucket after return (they may be moved/consumed downstream).

functions.name: ap_pass_brigade_fchk
functions.description: Wrapper around ap_pass_brigade that checks for filter errors and maps them to HTTP status codes. Returns OK on success, AP_FILTER_ERROR on filter error, or HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on other errors. Optional printf-style fmt message describes the error context.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec when called during request processing.
bucket must be a valid brigade; on return its contents are undefined and the caller must cleanup/destroy it.
If fmt is NULL, a default message "ap_pass_brigade returned" is used; otherwise fmt and varargs must be a valid printf-style format/arguments.

functions.name: ap_register_input_filter
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(ap_filter_rec_t *) ap_register_input_filter(const char *name, ap_in_filter_func filter_func, ap_init_filter_func filter_init, ap_filter_type ftype);
functions.description: Register an input filter by name with its callback, optional init function, and filter type. After registration, the filter can be installed in chains via ap_add_input_filter* by name or handle.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, unique filter name for lookup.
filter_func must be a valid ap_in_filter_func callback.
filter_init may be NULL or a valid init callback; if non-NULL it may be called before request handlers when the filter is active.
ftype must be a valid ap_filter_type (typically AP_FTYPE_CONTENT_SET or AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION for inputs).
Must be called during module initialization/registration phase (typical Apache pattern).

functions.name: ap_register_output_filter
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(ap_filter_rec_t *) ap_register_output_filter(const char *name, ap_out_filter_func filter_func, ap_init_filter_func filter_init, ap_filter_type ftype);
functions.description: Deprecated: Register an output filter by name. Prefer ap_register_output_filter_protocol to specify protocol flags. After registration the filter can be installed in output chains by name or handle.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and unique.
filter_func must be a valid ap_out_filter_func.
filter_init may be NULL or a valid init callback; called (if provided) before request handlers for request/subrequest filters; never for connection filters (ftype >= AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION).
ftype must be a valid ap_filter_type (typically AP_FTYPE_CONTENT_SET or AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION).
Should be called during module initialization/registration.

functions.name: ap_register_output_filter_protocol
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(ap_filter_rec_t *) ap_register_output_filter_protocol(const char *name, ap_out_filter_func filter_func, ap_init_filter_func filter_init, ap_filter_type ftype, unsigned int proto_flags);
functions.description: Register an output filter by name, with its callback, optional init function, filter type, and protocol flags (AP_FILTER_PROTO_*). Enables mod_filter provider use and precise protocol characteristics.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and unique.
filter_func must be a valid ap_out_filter_func.
filter_init may be NULL or valid; never called for connection filters (ftype >= AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION) per comments on ap_filter_rec_t.
ftype must be a valid ap_filter_type (typically AP_FTYPE_CONTENT_SET or AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION).
proto_flags is a logical OR of AP_FILTER_PROTO_* bits matching the filter’s behavior.
Should be called during module initialization/registration.

functions.name: ap_add_input_filter
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(ap_filter_t *) ap_add_input_filter(const char *name, void *ctx, request_rec *r, conn_rec *c);
functions.description: Add a named input filter to the specified request/connection filter chain, with an optional context pointer. Filters are ordered FIFO within their type; this inserts after existing filters of the same type and before filters from other requests.
requirements: name must refer to a previously registered input filter.
ctx is an opaque per-filter installation context and may be NULL.
r may be NULL for connection-level filters; pass the request when associated with a request.
c must be the target connection for the filter (non-NULL).
Filters are appended in FIFO order among same-type filters; callers should be aware of ordering semantics.

functions.name: ap_add_input_filter_handle
functions.description: Add an input filter to a request/connection chain using a previously obtained filter handle instead of a name.
requirements: f must be a valid filter handle obtained from registration (ap_register_input_filter) or lookup (ap_get_input_filter_handle).
ctx may be NULL or a valid context pointer for this installation.
r may be NULL for connection-level filters; otherwise pass the relevant request.
c must be a valid connection pointer.

functions.name: ap_get_input_filter_handle
functions.description: Lookup and return the registered input filter handle by name for use with ap_add_input_filter_handle.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and match a registered input filter name.
Returns NULL if the name is not registered; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: ap_add_output_filter
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(ap_filter_t *) ap_add_output_filter(const char *name, void *ctx, request_rec *r, conn_rec *c);
functions.description: Add a named output filter to a request/connection filter chain with a per-installation context. Filters are inserted FIFO within their type. If adding a connection-level output filter (ftype >= AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION) during a request, pass r to ensure proper chain modification; f->r will still be initialized to NULL.
requirements: name must refer to a previously registered output filter.
ctx may be NULL or a valid context pointer.
r may be NULL for connection-level filters added outside request processing; when adding a connection-level output filter during a request, r must be provided.
c must be a valid connection pointer.
Ordering is FIFO among same-type filters; be aware of existing chain composition (request vs sub-request filters).

functions.name: ap_add_output_filter_handle
functions.description: Add an output filter to a request/connection filter chain using a registered filter handle. Honors the same ordering and request/connection semantics as ap_add_output_filter.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter handle.
ctx may be NULL or valid per-install context.
If adding a connection-level output filter (ftype >= AP_FTYPE_CONNECTION) during request processing, r must be passed to update chains correctly; the resulting filter’s f->r remains NULL.
c must be a valid connection pointer.

functions.name: ap_get_output_filter_handle
functions.description: Lookup and return a registered output filter handle by name for use with ap_add_output_filter_handle or as a provider under mod_filter.
requirements: name must be non-NULL; it must match a previously registered output filter or NULL is returned.
Caller must handle NULL when the filter is not found.

functions.name: ap_remove_input_filter
functions.description: Remove an input filter from its associated request or connection filter stack.
requirements: f must be a valid filter previously added to a chain.
After removal, f should not be used for further filter operations.

functions.name: ap_remove_output_filter
functions.description: Remove an output filter from its associated request or connection filter stack.
requirements: f must be a valid filter previously added to a chain.
After removal, f should not be used for further filter operations.

functions.name: ap_remove_input_filter_byhandle
functions.description: Search the given filter stack and remove the first matching input filter by handle (name). Returns APR_SUCCESS on removal or error (per header comment).
requirements: next must be a pointer to the head (or current position) of an input filter stack.
handle must be the filter handle/name to remove (non-NULL).
Caller must handle the APR status return to determine success or error.

functions.name: ap_remove_output_filter_byhandle
functions.description: Search the given filter stack and remove the first matching output filter by handle (name). Returns APR_SUCCESS on removal or error (per header comment).
requirements: next must be a pointer to the head (or current position) of an output filter stack.
handle must be the filter handle/name to remove (non-NULL).
Caller must check the APR status return for success or error.

functions.name: ap_save_brigade
functions.description: Prepare a brigade to be set aside for later use by the filter, concatenating with any previously set-aside brigade. If *save_to is NULL, a brigade is created and a cleanup is registered to clear the pointer on pool destruction. The input brigade is always emptied on return.
requirements: f must be the current filter (valid ap_filter_t*).
save_to must be a valid pointer to a brigade pointer; may point to NULL to create one.
b must be a valid pointer to a brigade pointer; on return, the brigade referenced is emptied.
p must be a pool whose lifetime should cover the set-aside data; data in the brigade is ensured to live at least as long as p.
Caller must later destroy/cleanup any set-aside brigades or rely on pool cleanup.

functions.name: ap_filter_prepare_brigade
functions.description: Prepare the filter to allow brigades to be set aside. Typically allocates state so input filters can set aside data, or can be used from an output filter via ap_filter_setaside_brigade. Returns OK if a brigade was created, DECLINED otherwise.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer.
Caller should check for OK vs DECLINED to know whether setaside is prepared.

functions.name: ap_filter_setaside_brigade
functions.description: Set aside a brigade within the filter, creating dedicated storage if necessary for the brigade’s lifetime. The passed brigade is always emptied on return. Intended for deferring downstream writes/reads.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer previously prepared (typically via ap_filter_prepare_brigade).
bb must be a valid brigade; on return, bb is emptied and must not assume original buckets remain.
All buckets in bb will be made to live at least as long as the filter’s dedicated storage (implementation-specific).

functions.name: ap_filter_reinstate_brigade
functions.description: Reinstate previously set-aside data into the provided brigade, determining how much to flush based on flush buckets, in-memory size limits, and pipeline backpressure. If bb is empty, the function reinstates without further checks. Returns APR_SUCCESS and may set flush_upto to the bucket that should be flushed up to.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer with previously set-aside data.
bb must be a valid brigade to restore data into; may be empty to trigger immediate reinstatement.
flush_upto may be NULL or a pointer to receive the bucket up to which flushing should occur.
Caller should use flush_upto (if non-NULL) to decide what to pass downstream and may combine with AP_BUCKET_IS_WC logic if applicable.

functions.name: ap_filter_adopt_brigade
functions.description: Adopt a brigade as-is into the filter’s internal storage without setaside or copying; the passed brigade is always emptied on return. Intended for fast hand-off when buckets already match the connection’s allocator.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer.
bb must be a brigade whose buckets are allocated on f->c->pool and f->c->bucket_alloc (per remark).
After the call, bb is empty and should not be assumed to hold previous buckets.

functions.name: ap_filter_should_yield
functions.description: Determine whether downstream filters still have buffered, unsent brigades. Returns non-zero if downstream has pending output, which suggests that passing more data might block; filters can use this to decide to set aside data and yield.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer.
Safe to call from a handler as per note.
Caller interprets non-zero as pending downstream data and may decide to defer/queue output accordingly.

functions.name: ap_filter_output_pending
functions.description: Check whether any output filters on the connection have unwritten data, and if so attempt a single write to each. Returns DECLINED if none remain, OK if some remain, or a positive integer if any attempt to write failed.
requirements: c must be a valid connection pointer.
Caller must interpret return values: DECLINED (no pending), OK (some pending), positive integer (write attempt failed).

functions.name: ap_filter_input_pending
functions.description: Determine whether there is pending data in the input filters (already read from the socket but not yet returned to the application). Returns DECLINED if none, OK if some remain.
requirements: c must be a valid connection pointer.
Caller must interpret return values: DECLINED (no pending), OK (pending data).

functions.name: ap_filter_flush
functions.description: Flush function suitable for apr_brigade_* buffering callbacks. If the brigade buffer overflows, this function calls ap_pass_brigade to flush the brigade down the filter stack. Not related to FLUSH buckets themselves.
requirements: bb must be a valid brigade to flush.
ctx must be a pointer to the target ap_filter_t to pass the brigade to.
Intended for use as the flush callback parameter to APR brigade write APIs (e.g., apr_brigade_write).

functions.name: ap_fflush
functions.description: Explicitly flush the current brigade down the filter stack via the specified filter.
requirements: f must be a valid filter pointer to pass data to.
bb must be a valid brigade; caller retains ownership and must cleanup/destroy as appropriate after flushing.

functions.name: ap_fputstrs
functions.description: Write an unspecified number of NUL-terminated strings to the current filter, buffering into the provided brigade and using ap_filter_flush as needed. Varargs list must be terminated appropriately (sentinel as per macro attribute).
requirements: f must be a valid output filter pointer.
bb must be a valid brigade for buffering output.
Varargs must be properly terminated per AP_FN_ATTR_SENTINEL convention (implementation expects a sentinel; typically NULL).
Caller should handle APR status returns and may need to cleanup the brigade after use.

functions.name: ap_fprintf
functions.description: Format and write data to the current filter using printf-style formatting, buffering into the provided brigade and flushing via ap_filter_flush as needed.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter pointer.
bb must be a valid brigade for buffering output.
fmt and varargs must form a valid printf-style format/arguments tuple.

functions.name: ap_filter_protocol
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_filter_protocol(ap_filter_t* f, unsigned int proto_flags);
functions.description: Set protocol flags (AP_FILTER_PROTO_* bits) for an output content filter (AP_FTYPE_RESOURCE or AP_FTYPE_CONTENT_SET only) to describe behavioral properties such as content changes, length changes, byterange compatibility, caching, proxying, and transform semantics.
requirements: f must be a valid output filter pointer of type AP_FTYPE_RESOURCE or AP_FTYPE_CONTENT_SET; only works for these types.
proto_flags must be a logical OR of AP_FILTER_PROTO_* bits that accurately describe the filter’s behavior.

functions.name: ap_bucket_wc_make
functions.description: Convert the given bucket into a Write Completion (WC) bucket, a special kind of FLUSH bucket (APR_BUCKET_IS_FLUSH is true) with ->data pointing to ap_bucket_wc_data. WC buckets signal write completion boundaries to cooperating filters.
requirements: b must be a valid apr_bucket pointer; typically a FLUSH-capable bucket.
Returns the modified bucket or NULL if allocation failed; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: ap_bucket_wc_create
functions.description: Create and return a Write Completion (WC) bucket from the given bucket allocator freelist. WC buckets are FLUSH buckets marked with ap_bucket_wc_data for filters that care about write completion semantics.
requirements: list must be a valid apr_bucket_alloc_t* from which to allocate the bucket.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: uldap_connection_open
functions.description: Opens and (if needed) binds an LDAP connection using the parameters stored in the provided util_ldap_connection_t. If already connected (ldc->ldap != NULL), it will not reconnect; if already bound, it will not rebind. Returns an LDAP SDK status code (LDAP_SUCCESS on success). Intended to be called after acquiring or creating a connection structure for a request.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to the current Apache request_rec.
ldc must be a valid, initialized util_ldap_connection_t with host/port and optional binddn/bindpw configured.
Do not expect a new network connection if ldc->ldap is already non-NULL; the function is a no-op for the connect/bind steps already completed.
Caller should check the integer return value for LDAP_SUCCESS and handle error codes appropriately.

functions.name: uldap_connection_close
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired LDAP connection, unbinding and clearing ldc->ldap as needed, and unlocks it for reuse by other threads. Used when the caller has finished using a connection obtained via uldap_connection_find/open.
requirements: ldc must be a valid util_ldap_connection_t previously obtained/found and currently held by the caller.
After calling, the connection instance may be reused by the connection pool; the caller must not use ldc->ldap until reopened.
Should be called to release the lock acquired by uldap_connection_find once the caller is finished with the connection.

functions.name: uldap_connection_unbind
functions.description: Unbinds and disconnects an LDAP connection to bring it back to a known state (typically used during error handling). The parameter is expected to point to a util_ldap_connection_t.
requirements: param must be a pointer that actually refers to a util_ldap_connection_t instance.
Call this during error conditions to reset the connection; afterwards, a subsequent open/bind will be required before reuse.
Caller must check the apr_status_t return and handle failures.

functions.name: uldap_connection_find
functions.signature: util_ldap_connection_t * uldap_connection_find(request_rec *r, const char *host, int port, const char *binddn, const char *bindpw, deref_options deref, int secure);
functions.description: Searches the module’s connection list for a matching LDAP connection (host/port/bind/opts). If found or created, returns a util_ldap_connection_t and acquires a lock on it to prevent concurrent use by other threads. The caller must close it when done to release the lock.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec for the current request.
host must be a non-NULL hostname string (optionally a space-separated list).
port should be a valid LDAP port number.
binddn and bindpw may be NULL if anonymous or external bind is intended; if provided, they must match the intended bind identity for the session.
deref must be one of the deref_options enumeration values.
secure controls SSL/TLS usage; pass an appropriate mode per the module’s expectations.
On success, the returned connection is locked for exclusive use; the caller must call uldap_connection_close to release it when finished.
The returned pointer must be checked for NULL before use.

functions.name: uldap_cache_comparedn
functions.signature: int uldap_cache_comparedn(request_rec *r, util_ldap_connection_t *ldc, const char *url, const char *dn, const char *reqdn, int compare_dn_on_server);
functions.description: Determines whether two distinguished names (DNs) refer to the same entry, optionally using the LDAP server for canonical comparison. Uses an internal cache keyed by the provided URL to optimize repeat comparisons. Returns an LDAP-style status/int indicator (LDAP_SUCCESS on match, or other code).
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
ldc must be a valid, open/bound LDAP connection if compare_dn_on_server is nonzero.
url must be a non-NULL string identifying the LDAP backend/cache context.
dn and reqdn must be non-NULL, properly formatted DN strings.
compare_dn_on_server controls whether to perform a server-side canonical comparison; server-side is more accurate but requires a functional connection.
Caller must check the integer result and handle negative/LDAP error codes.

functions.name: uldap_cache_compare
functions.signature: int uldap_cache_compare(request_rec *r, util_ldap_connection_t *ldc, const char *url, const char *dn, const char *attrib, const char *value);
functions.description: Performs an LDAP compare operation (attribute equals value) on the specified DN, using an internal cache keyed by URL to avoid redundant operations. Typically used to test group membership or presence of an attribute/value on an entry. Returns an int status (LDAP_SUCCESS on true, or an LDAP/error code).
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
ldc must be a valid LDAP connection suitable for the URL provided.
url must be a non-NULL cache key identifying the LDAP server/context.
dn must be a non-NULL DN string of the target entry.
attrib must be a non-NULL attribute type string.
value must be a non-NULL attribute value string.
Caller must interpret the return code (success vs. not present vs. error).

functions.name: uldap_cache_check_subgroups
functions.signature: int uldap_cache_check_subgroups(request_rec *r, util_ldap_connection_t *ldc, const char *url, const char *dn, const char *attrib, const char *value, char **subgroupAttrs, apr_array_header_t *subgroupclasses, int cur_subgroup_depth, int max_subgroup_depth);
functions.description: Checks whether a user (identified by an attribute/value) is a member of a given group DN or any of its nested subgroups. Uses subgroup attribute names and group objectClass filters to traverse subgroup relationships. Employs caching keyed by URL. Returns an int status indicating membership or an LDAP/error code.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
ldc must be a valid LDAP connection for the target directory.
url must be a non-NULL cache/LDAP context identifier.
dn must be a non-NULL DN of the starting group object.
attrib must be a non-NULL attribute name that identifies users within group entries (for example, member, uniqueMember).
value must be a non-NULL attribute value corresponding to the user to test (for example, the user DN).
subgroupAttrs must point to a NULL-terminated array of attribute names that reference subgroup DNs.
subgroupclasses must be a valid apr_array_header_t* containing objectClass values that identify group objects.
cur_subgroup_depth should be >= 0 and represent the current recursion depth.
max_subgroup_depth should be >= 0 and limits recursion; the function should not recurse deeper than this value.
Caller must check the integer return code and handle membership/nomatch/error appropriately.

functions.name: uldap_cache_checkuserid
functions.signature: int uldap_cache_checkuserid(request_rec *r, util_ldap_connection_t *ldc, const char *url, const char *basedn, int scope, char **attrs, const char *filter, const char *bindpw, const char **binddn, const char ***retvals);
functions.description: Searches for exactly one user entry matching the provided LDAP filter under basedn, and attempts to bind as that user with the provided password. If the bind succeeds, returns success and provides the found DN and selected attribute values via out-parameters. Results are cached per URL. Note: documentation states the filter must return exactly one user.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
ldc must be a valid LDAP connection suitable for the provided URL.
url must be a non-NULL string indicating the LDAP server/cache context.
basedn must be a non-NULL base DN for the search.
scope must be a valid LDAP search scope constant (e.g., LDAP_SCOPE_BASE/ONELEVEL/SUBTREE).
attrs may be NULL or point to a NULL-terminated list of attribute names to fetch; behavior for NULL vs. empty may depend on the LDAP library.
filter must be a non-NULL LDAP filter string that should match exactly one entry for success.
bindpw must be the password corresponding to the found user entry; must not be NULL when a user bind is required.
binddn must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the DN string of the matched user; ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unknown from this header and should be treated as read-only.
retvals must be a non-NULL pointer to receive attribute values; structure/ownership of returned arrays is unknown from this header and should be treated as read-only.
Caller must check the integer result for success vs. LDAP/no such object/invalid credentials and handle errors.

functions.name: uldap_cache_getuserdn
functions.signature: int uldap_cache_getuserdn(request_rec *r, util_ldap_connection_t *ldc, const char *url, const char *basedn, int scope, char **attrs, const char *filter, const char **binddn, const char ***retvals);
functions.description: Searches the directory for exactly one user entry matching the filter under basedn and returns the user’s DN and any requested attribute values via out-parameters, using a cache keyed by URL. Unlike the checkuserid variant, this does not take a password and is focused on lookup rather than credential verification.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
ldc must be a valid LDAP connection for the specified URL.
url must be a non-NULL LDAP/cache context identifier.
basedn must be a non-NULL base DN for the search.
scope must be a valid LDAP search scope constant.
attrs may be NULL or a NULL-terminated list of attributes to fetch.
filter must be a non-NULL LDAP filter that should match exactly one entry for success.
binddn must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the DN string; ownership/lifetime is unspecified in this header (treat as read-only).
retvals must be a non-NULL pointer to receive attribute values; ownership/lifetime is unspecified (treat as read-only).
Caller must check the integer return value and handle not-found/multiple matches/error cases.

functions.name: uldap_ssl_supported
functions.description: Indicates whether mod_ldap has SSL/TLS support available in the current build/configuration. Returns a nonzero value if SSL is supported, zero otherwise.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec.
Caller should interpret nonzero as SSL supported and zero as not supported.

functions.name: util_ldap_cache_init
functions.description: Initializes the LDAP cache structures (shared memory and in-process/in-thread cache as applicable) using the provided APR pool and module state. Returns an APR status code indicating success or failure.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool used for allocations during initialization.
st must point to a util_ldap_state_t structure to be initialized; fields like cache sizes/TTLs should be set appropriately before calling.
Caller must check and handle the returned apr_status_t; cache may still be set up for in-process operation even if shared memory initialization fails (per comments).

functions.name: util_ald_cache_display
functions.description: Returns a formatted, human-readable summary string of cache statistics for the LDAP cache managed by the module. The string is allocated from a request-appropriate pool (per signature, obtained via request_rec). Note: header comment mentions apr_pool_t *pool, but the actual signature takes request_rec *r; the implementation likely allocates from r->pool.
requirements: r must be a valid request_rec with an associated APR pool for allocation.
st must be a valid, initialized util_ldap_state_t representing the current LDAP module state.
The returned char* points to memory allocated from the request pool and is valid for the lifetime of that pool.

functions.name: ap_md5
functions.description: Computes the MD5 checksum of a null-terminated input string and returns a pool-allocated textual representation of the digest. Intended for generating an MD5 hash for ASCII/UTF-8 strings using an APR memory pool for allocation. The returned string is typically the 32-character hexadecimal MD5 plus a NUL terminator (inferred from common Apache/APR usage; exact format not documented here).
requirements: Parameter a must be a valid, live apr_pool_t*; the returned string’s lifetime is tied to this pool.
Parameter string must point to a valid null-terminated string; it must be readable for its full length.
Caller must not free the returned pointer manually; it is managed by the APR pool.
Function behavior on allocation failure or invalid inputs is not documented here; callers should not assume a non-NULL return in out-of-memory conditions (inferred).

functions.name: ap_md5_binary
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(char *) ap_md5_binary(apr_pool_t *a, const unsigned char *buf, int len);
functions.description: Computes the MD5 checksum of a binary buffer of length len and returns a pool-allocated textual representation of the digest. Use when hashing arbitrary binary data rather than a C string. The returned string is typically the 32-character hexadecimal MD5 plus a NUL terminator (inferred; exact format not documented here).
requirements: Parameter a must be a valid, live apr_pool_t*; the returned string’s lifetime is tied to this pool.
Parameter buf must point to a readable memory region of at least len bytes.
Parameter len must be non-negative and must accurately reflect the size of buf to be hashed.
Caller must not free the returned pointer manually; it is managed by the APR pool.
Function behavior on allocation failure or invalid inputs is not documented here; callers should not assume a non-NULL return in out-of-memory conditions (inferred).

functions.name: ap_parse_mutex
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_parse_mutex(const char *arg, apr_pool_t *pool, apr_lockmech_e *mutexmech, const char **mutexfile);
functions.description: Parses a Mutex configuration string and extracts the APR lock mechanism and an optional lock file path. Intended for use when processing Apache’s Mutex directive or module-specific mutex settings. On success, writes the selected mechanism to mutexmech and, if applicable, the resolved lock file path to mutexfile.
requirements: arg must be a valid mutex configuration string in Apache syntax (e.g., "default", "none", or a mechanism spec like "flock:/path/to/file", "fcntl:/path/to/file", "pthread", "sysvsem", "posixsem", or "sem").
pool must be a valid, initialized apr_pool_t used for any allocations during parsing.
mutexmech must be a non-NULL output pointer to receive the parsed apr_lockmech_e.
mutexfile must be a non-NULL output pointer; it will be set to a file path if a file-backed mechanism is selected, or possibly NULL otherwise.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t and handle non-APR_SUCCESS codes.

functions.name: ap_set_mutex
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE_NONSTD(const char *) ap_set_mutex(cmd_parms *cmd, void *dummy, const char *arg);
functions.description: Module-internal command handler for the Mutex directive. Parses and applies a single Mutex configuration argument within Apache’s configuration processing. Returns an error message string on failure or NULL on success.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer provided by the Apache configuration framework.
arg should be a single Mutex argument string as it appears in configuration; on error this function returns a non-NULL const char* message.
Caller (the config framework) must treat a non-NULL return as a configuration error and surface it appropriately.
Intended to be invoked by Apache’s directive processing; not for general-purpose calling.

functions.name: ap_mutex_init
functions.description: Initializes the Apache mutex infrastructure early in server startup. Prepares internal state so that registered mutex types and subsequent mutex creation operate correctly.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool whose lifetime covers the initialization phase.
Should be called during server initialization before creating or using registered mutexes; exact hook timing is internal/private (usage outside core is discouraged).

functions.name: ap_mutex_register
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_mutex_register(apr_pool_t *pconf, const char *type, const char *default_dir, apr_lockmech_e default_mech, apr_int32_t options);
functions.description: Registers a module-defined mutex type with the core so it can be configured via the Mutex directive. Must be called in the pre_config hook. Allows specifying optional defaults for lock file directory and preferred mechanism, and options to allow or default to "none".
requirements: Must be called in the pre_config hook; if not, Mutex directives referencing this type will be rejected.
type must be a unique mutex type name across all registered types (used as basename for any associated lock file).
If the mutex type supports multiple instances, uniqueness is per instance via instance IDs at creation time; registration requires only a unique type name.
default_dir may be NULL to use built-in defaults; if provided, it is used as the default lock file directory for this type.
default_mech should normally be APR_LOCK_DEFAULT to respect built-in defaults; a specific apr_lockmech_e can be provided.
options is a bitwise-or of AP_MUTEX_* flags (AP_MUTEX_ALLOW_NONE, AP_MUTEX_DEFAULT_NONE).
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t and handle failure.

functions.name: ap_global_mutex_create
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_global_mutex_create(apr_global_mutex_t **mutex, const char **name, const char *type, const char *instance_id, server_rec *server, apr_pool_t *pool, apr_int32_t options);
functions.description: Creates a registered, process-shared (APR global) mutex of the specified type. Handles lock files, permissions, and error logging internally. Returns the created APR global mutex and optionally the generated filename when file-backed.
requirements: type must have been previously registered with ap_mutex_register().
mutex must be a non-NULL output pointer; on success it receives the created apr_global_mutex_t*.

If this mutex type is disabled (e.g., via configuration allowing "none"), *mutex will be set to NULL; this is allowed only if AP_MUTEX_ALLOW_NONE was passed to ap_mutex_register() for this type. Callers must be prepared for a NULL mutex in that case.
name may be NULL if the caller does not need the generated filename; otherwise it receives the filename for file-based mechanisms or NULL if none.
instance_id must be a unique string if the mutex type is multi-instance; otherwise pass NULL.
server must be the main server_rec for logging and context.
pool specifies the mutex lifetime; it must remain valid as long as the mutex is needed.
options is a bitwise-or of AP_MUTEX_* flags; currently none are defined for this function.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t and handle failure.

functions.name: ap_proc_mutex_create
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_proc_mutex_create(apr_proc_mutex_t **mutex, const char **name, const char *type, const char *instance_id, server_rec *server, apr_pool_t *pool, apr_int32_t options);
functions.description: Creates a registered APR process mutex (proc mutex) of the specified type. As with global mutex creation, lock files, permissions, and error logging are handled internally. Optionally returns the generated filename when a file-backed mechanism is used.
requirements: type must have been previously registered with ap_mutex_register().
mutex must be a non-NULL output pointer; on success it receives the created apr_proc_mutex_t*.

If this mutex type is disabled (e.g., via configuration allowing "none"), *mutex will be set to NULL; this is allowed only if AP_MUTEX_ALLOW_NONE was passed to ap_mutex_register() for this type. Callers must be prepared for a NULL mutex in that case.
name may be NULL if the caller does not need the generated filename; otherwise it receives the filename for file-based mechanisms or NULL if none.
instance_id must be a unique string if the mutex type is multi-instance; otherwise pass NULL.
server must be the main server_rec for logging and context.
pool specifies the mutex lifetime; it must remain valid as long as the mutex is needed.
options is a bitwise-or of AP_MUTEX_* flags; currently none are defined for this function.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t and handle failure.

functions.name: ap_dump_mutexes
functions.description: Writes information about available/registered mutex mechanisms and configuration to the given output file. Useful for diagnostics or generating human-readable listings of mutex support.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool for any transient allocations.
s must be a valid server_rec providing server context.
out must be a valid, open apr_file_t suitable for writing; caller is responsible for flushing/closing as needed.

functions.name: ap_create_environment
functions.description: Create a NULL-terminated environment vector from an Apache APR table of key-value pairs, suitable for use with exec-family calls. Allocates the array and strings from the given APR pool. Typical use: pass the returned char** as the environment to a subprocess/CGI.
requirements: p must be a valid, live apr_pool_t; returned memory is allocated from this pool and must not be freed manually.
t should be a valid apr_table_t containing string keys and values; non-string/NULL entries may produce undefined results (exact validation is not documented).
The returned array is suitable for exec-style calls and is expected to be NULL-terminated (standard pattern; explicit format not further documented).

functions.name: ap_find_path_info
functions.description: Compare a URI and a path-info string to find how much of the path-info matches the URI, returning the length of the path-info portion. Useful when mapping filesystem paths to URIs that may carry additional PATH_INFO.
requirements: uri must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
path_info must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: ap_add_cgi_vars
functions.description: Populate the request’s subprocess environment table with CGI variables required by HTTP/1.1. Intended for CGI/CGI-like script execution before invoking the script.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec for the current request.
r must have an allocated subprocess_env table (standard for initialized requests); this function will add/overwrite entries there.

functions.name: ap_add_common_vars
functions.description: Add common CGI environment variables (beyond those specifically required by HTTP/1.1) to the request’s environment table. Typically called with or after ap_add_cgi_vars before executing a CGI/CGI-like program.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec for the current request.
r must have an allocated subprocess_env table; this function will add/overwrite entries there.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err
functions.description: Read and validate HTTP header lines produced by a script from the given file handle. On success, merges them into r->headers_out and returns HTTP_OK. If the method is GET/HEAD and conditions fail, may return a conditional status (HTTP_NOT_MODIFIED or HTTP_PRECONDITION_FAILED). On error, returns 5xx and stores the offending text in buffer.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
f must reference a readable apr_file_t positioned at the start of the script’s header output.
buffer must point to writable storage; on error the problematic header line/string is written there. The caller should initialize it empty before the call (per documentation).
The caller must check the return value and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses (304/412), or 5xx errors appropriately.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_ex
functions.signature: int ap_scan_script_header_err_ex(request_rec *r, apr_file_t *f, char *buffer, int module_index);
functions.description: Like ap_scan_script_header_err() but logs using the provided module_index. Reads/validates script headers from a file, populates response headers, and may return conditional statuses for GET/HEAD requests.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
f must reference a readable apr_file_t positioned at the start of the script’s header output.
buffer must point to writable storage; on error the problematic header line/string is written there. Caller should pass it empty.
module_index should be a valid module index for logging in this server build.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_brigade
functions.description: Read and validate HTTP header lines produced by a script from an APR bucket brigade. On success, merges them into r->headers_out and returns HTTP_OK. For GET/HEAD, may return a conditional status. On error, returns 5xx and places the offending text in buffer.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade supplying the script’s header output at its current read position.
buffer must point to writable storage and should be empty on input; on error it will contain the offending string.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_brigade_ex
functions.description: Like ap_scan_script_header_err_brigade() but logs using the provided module_index. Reads/validates script headers from an APR brigade and updates response headers.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade positioned to read the script header output.
buffer must point to writable storage; pass empty on input. It receives the offending string on error.
module_index should be a valid module index for logging.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_strs
functions.description: Parse and validate HTTP header lines from a sequence of strings (varargs), adding them to r->headers_out. The varargs must be C strings terminated by a NULL pointer. For GET/HEAD, may return conditional statuses. On error, returns 5xx and stores the offending text in buffer. Also reports the last character and argument parsed via termch and termarg.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
buffer must point to writable storage and should be empty on input; on error it contains the offending string.
termch, if non-NULL, must point to storage where the last parsed character can be stored.
termarg, if non-NULL, must point to storage where the index (or related value) of the last parsed vararg can be stored.
The varargs list must consist of zero or more const char* strings terminated by a NULL sentinel (required).
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_strs_ex
functions.signature: int ap_scan_script_header_err_strs_ex(request_rec *r, char *buffer, int module_index, const char **termch, int *termarg, ...);
functions.description: Like ap_scan_script_header_err_strs(), but logs using the provided module_index. Parses headers from a NULL-terminated varargs list of strings and updates r->headers_out.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
buffer must point to writable storage and should be empty on input.
module_index should be a valid module index for logging.
termch and termarg, if provided, must be valid pointers to writable storage.
The varargs list must be a sequence of const char* strings terminated by a NULL sentinel.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_core
functions.signature: int ap_scan_script_header_err_core(request_rec *r, char *buffer, int (*getsfunc)(char *, int, void *), void *getsfunc_data);
functions.description: Core routine to read and validate HTTP header lines produced by a script using a user-supplied line-reading function. On success, merges headers into r->headers_out and returns HTTP_OK. For GET/HEAD, may return conditional statuses. On error, returns 5xx and stores the offending text in buffer.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
buffer must point to writable storage and should be empty on input; on error it receives the offending string.

getsfunc must be a function that acts like gets() for script header lines, with signature int(char *buf, int buflen, void *ctx). Exact return/EOF semantics are not documented here; it must be suitable for line-based header reading.
