getsfunc_data is passed through to getsfunc as its third parameter.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_scan_script_header_err_core_ex
functions.signature: int ap_scan_script_header_err_core_ex(request_rec *r, char *buffer, int (*getsfunc)(char *, int, void *), void *getsfunc_data, int module_index);
functions.description: Core routine like ap_scan_script_header_err_core() but logs using the provided module_index. Uses a caller-supplied gets-like function to obtain header lines, validates and merges them into r->headers_out.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec.
buffer must point to writable storage and should be empty on input.
getsfunc must behave like gets() for line-based header reading with signature int(char *buf, int buflen, void *ctx). Exact return/EOF semantics are not documented here.
getsfunc_data is an opaque context passed to getsfunc.
module_index should be a valid module index for logging.
The caller must check and handle HTTP_OK, conditional statuses, or 5xx returns.

functions.name: ap_args_to_table
functions.description: Parse the request’s query string (args) into a newly created APR table allocated from the request’s pool. Parameters without an explicit value are stored with the value "1". If no query args are present, returns an empty table.
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized request_rec with its pool available; the new table is allocated from the request pool.
table must be a non-NULL pointer to an apr_table_t*; on return, *table is set to the new table.
The caller must not free the returned table directly; it is managed by the request pool’s lifetime.

functions.name: ap_explode_recent_localtime
functions.description: Converts a recent apr_time_t to its exploded (human-readable) components in the local timezone using an internal cache for speed. Intended for repeatedly exploding near-current times (e.g., logging) as a faster alternative to apr_time_exp_lt. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success.
requirements: tm must be a valid, writable pointer to apr_time_exp_t.
t MUST be within the last AP_TIME_RECENT_THRESHOLD (15) seconds.
Caller should use this only for recent times; for arbitrary times use apr_time_exp_lt instead.
Check the returned apr_status_t for success.

functions.name: ap_explode_recent_gmt
functions.description: Converts a recent apr_time_t to its exploded (human-readable) components in GMT using an internal cache for speed. Intended for repeatedly exploding near-current times (e.g., logging) as a faster alternative to apr_time_exp_gmt. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success.
requirements: tm must be a valid, writable pointer to apr_time_exp_t.
t MUST be within the last AP_TIME_RECENT_THRESHOLD (15) seconds.
Caller should use this only for recent times; for arbitrary times use apr_time_exp_gmt instead.
Check the returned apr_status_t for success.

functions.name: ap_recent_ctime
functions.description: Formats a recent apr_time_t into a ctime()-style string, using an internal recent-time cache for efficiency. Consider using ap_recent_ctime_ex for extended formatting options. Returns APR_SUCCESS if successful.
requirements: date_str must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the formatted string including the terminating NUL (size not specified here).
t is expected to be a recent time; function is optimized for near-current timestamps.
Check the returned apr_status_t for success.

functions.name: ap_recent_ctime_ex
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_recent_ctime_ex(char *date_str, apr_time_t t, int option, int *len);
functions.description: Formats a recent apr_time_t into an extended ctime()-style string with optional microseconds, compact ISO 8601 format, and/or GMT offset. Uses a recent-time cache for efficiency. On success, writes the string to date_str and updates *len to the number of bytes written including the trailing NUL. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success or APR_ENOMEM if the buffer is too short.
requirements: date_str must point to a writable buffer whose size is provided via *len on input.
len must be a non-NULL pointer to an int initialized with the size (in bytes) of the date_str buffer before the call; on success it is set to the number of bytes written including the NUL terminator.
option is a bitmask of AP_CTIME_OPTION_* values (AP_CTIME_OPTION_NONE, AP_CTIME_OPTION_USEC, AP_CTIME_OPTION_COMPACT, AP_CTIME_OPTION_GMTOFF).
If the buffer is too small for the requested formatting, the function returns APR_ENOMEM and does not overrun the buffer.
t is expected to be a recent time; function is optimized for near-current timestamps.
Check the returned apr_status_t for APR_SUCCESS or APR_ENOMEM.

functions.name: ap_recent_rfc822_date
functions.description: Formats a recent apr_time_t into an RFC 822 date string. Uses recent-time optimizations. The caller must provide a buffer large enough for an RFC 822 date.
requirements: date_str must point to a writable buffer with length >= APR_RFC822_DATE_LEN.
t is an apr_time_t timestamp; function is optimized for recent times.
Check the returned apr_status_t for success (exact status values not documented here).

functions.name: ap_force_set_tz
functions.description: Forces an unset TZ environment to UTC. Uses the provided APR pool for any required allocations or environment setup. Intended to ensure consistent time behavior when TZ is not set.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool pointer.
Call when TZ is unset and UTC behavior is desired; has no documented return value, so errors (if any) are not reported via return code.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_init
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_varbuf_init(apr_pool_t *pool, struct ap_varbuf *vb, apr_size_t init_size);
functions.description: Initialize a resizable ap_varbuf associated with an APR pool. Safe to call on a previously used ap_varbuf; old memory is released when the pool is cleared. The buffer remains valid until its pool is cleared, even if the ap_varbuf goes out of scope. Typical usage: declare a struct ap_varbuf, then call ap_varbuf_init(pool, &vb, initial_capacity).
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized apr_pool_t* with a lifetime covering the intended use of vb.
vb must point to writable storage for a struct ap_varbuf.
init_size specifies the initial buffer capacity; actual capacity may grow later via ap_varbuf_grow().
Callers must not assume the buffer persists beyond pool clearance.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_grow
functions.description: Ensure the ap_varbuf has at least new_size bytes of capacity (excluding the trailing NUL). May grow in place or reallocate; in the latter case, the first vb->strlen + 1 bytes (or the whole buffer if vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN) are copied to the new location. Designed to over-allocate (typically doubling) to reduce reallocations.
requirements: vb must have been initialized with ap_varbuf_init().
new_size is the minimum required capacity; the function may allocate more than requested.
If the buffer is reallocated, any previously taken raw pointers into vb->buf become invalid and must not be used.
On out-of-memory, the function will invoke vb->pool's abort function; callers should assume it does not return in that case.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_free
functions.description: Release memory from an ap_varbuf immediately when possible (primarily for large allocations backed by allocator mem nodes), without waiting for the pool to be cleared. Intended to proactively free large buffers.
requirements: vb must have been initialized with ap_varbuf_init().
After ap_varbuf_free() returns, vb must not be used again unless ap_varbuf_init() is called on it to reinitialize.
Only larger allocations using mem nodes will actually be freed; small pool allocations may persist until pool cleanup.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_strmemcat
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(void) ap_varbuf_strmemcat(struct ap_varbuf *vb, const char *str, int len);
functions.description: Append len bytes from str to the ap_varbuf. The append position is determined by vb->strlen, or the first NUL in vb->buf if vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN. If len != 0, the buffer is guaranteed to remain NUL-terminated and vb->strlen is updated to the new string length.
requirements: vb must have been initialized with ap_varbuf_init().
str must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; may contain embedded NULs.
len may be 0, in which case the function performs no operation.

If vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN, the function will search for the first NUL in vb->buf to determine the append position; callers should ensure vb->buf contains a NUL-terminated sequence in that case.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_pdup
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(char *) ap_varbuf_pdup(apr_pool_t *p, struct ap_varbuf *vb, const char *prepend, apr_size_t prepend_len, const char *append, apr_size_t append_len, apr_size_t *new_len);
functions.description: Duplicate the current content of an ap_varbuf into pool memory, optionally prepending and/or appending additional buffers. Works with arbitrary binary data and uses vb->strlen to determine how many bytes to copy. Returns a newly allocated buffer from p and optionally returns the total length via new_len.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized apr_pool_t*.
vb must be initialized; the amount copied is vb->strlen bytes. If vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN, it will be set to strlen(vb->buf), which requires vb->buf to be NUL-terminated at the logical end.
If prepend is non-NULL, it must reference at least prepend_len bytes.
If append is non-NULL, it must reference at least append_len bytes.
new_len may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be set to the total length of the resulting data (prepend_len + vb->strlen + append_len).

functions.name: ap_varbuf_regsub
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_varbuf_regsub(struct ap_varbuf *vb, const char *input, const char *source, apr_size_t nmatch, ap_regmatch_t pmatch[], apr_size_t maxlen);
functions.description: Perform regex-based substitution like ap_pregsub(), but append the result to an ap_varbuf. Replaces $1..$9 in input with corresponding sub-expressions matched in source per pmatch/nmatch. Does not copy the portion of source prior to pmatch[0].rm_so. Respects maxlen (0 means unlimited). Updates vb->strlen to include the appended data.
requirements: vb must be initialized; if vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN, it will first be set to strlen(vb->buf).
pmatch must point to an array with at least nmatch valid entries produced by a successful regex match against source (via ap_pregex or compatible).
input may contain $1..$9 placeholders; placeholders beyond available matches are treated per ap_pregsub semantics.
source must be the string used to produce pmatch; behavior depends on correct correspondence.
maxlen limits the number of bytes appended; 0 means no limit.
Callers must check the returned apr_status_t for APR_SUCCESS before using the appended result.

functions.name: ap_varbuf_cfg_getline
functions.signature: AP_DECLARE(apr_status_t) ap_varbuf_cfg_getline(struct ap_varbuf *vb, ap_configfile_t *cfp, apr_size_t max_len);
functions.description: Read a line from an ap_configfile_t and append it to an ap_varbuf, setting vb->strlen to the line length. Returns the same status codes as ap_cfg_getline(). If vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN, it will be set to strlen(vb->buf) before appending.
requirements: vb must be initialized; if vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN, it will first be set to strlen(vb->buf).
cfp must be a valid, open ap_configfile_t* ready for reading.
max_len specifies the maximum allowed line length including leading/trailing whitespace; callers should choose an appropriate bound.
Callers must handle the apr_status_t result according to ap_cfg_getline() semantics (e.g., success, EOF, truncation/error conditions).

functions.name: ap_varbuf_strcat
functions.signature: void ap_varbuf_strcat(struct ap_varbuf *vb, const char *str)  /* macro mapping to ap_varbuf_strmemcat(vb, str, strlen(str)) */
functions.description: Concatenate a C-string to an ap_varbuf. This is a convenience macro that calls ap_varbuf_strmemcat(vb, str, strlen(str)). It appends at the current end of the buffer (as tracked by vb->strlen, or at the first NUL if vb->strlen is AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN), growing the buffer as needed. After the call, vb->strlen is updated to the new string length and vb->buf remains NUL-terminated. Usage: ensure vb was initialized with ap_varbuf_init and pass a NUL-terminated string in str.
requirements: vb must point to a valid, initialized ap_varbuf (initialized via ap_varbuf_init).
str must be a valid, non-NULL, NUL-terminated C-string (strlen(str) is evaluated by the macro).
If vb->strlen == AP_VARBUF_UNKNOWN before the call, the append position is the first NUL byte currently in vb->buf (behavior of ap_varbuf_strmemcat).
The call may grow the buffer and allocate from vb->pool; on out-of-memory, the pool’s abort function may be invoked (via ap_varbuf_grow).
Do not use vb after ap_varbuf_free() unless it has been re-initialized.

functions.name: ap_xml_parse_input
functions.description: Parses the XML entity body of the current Apache httpd request and returns an HTTP status code. On success, stores the parsed APR XML document into *pdoc. Typical usage is within a request handler to obtain and process XML POST data. The resulting apr_xml_doc is allocated from the request’s APR pool (via the httpd/APR XML facilities).
requirements: r must be a valid, initialized pointer to an active request_rec for the current request.
pdoc must be a non-NULL pointer to an apr_xml_doc* where the parsed document pointer can be stored.
The request should provide an XML entity body (e.g., POST data) readable via standard input filters; otherwise parsing will fail and an error HTTP status code is returned.
Caller must check the returned HTTP status code; non-HTTP_OK indicates failure and *pdoc should not be used.
The lifetime of the returned apr_xml_doc is tied to the request’s APR pool; do not free it manually and do not use it after the pool is cleared or destroyed.

functions.name: apreq_value_table_add
functions.signature: static APR_INLINE void apreq_value_table_add(const apreq_value_t *v, apr_table_t *t)
functions.description: Adds the given apreq_value_t (key/value) into an APR table by passing v->name and v->data to apr_table_addn. Intended for efficiently inserting parsed parameter/cookie values into an apr_table_t without copying strings.
requirements: v must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized apreq_value_t.
t must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized apr_table_t.
v->name must point to a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
v->data must point to a valid, NUL-terminated C string (the value).
Because this uses apr_table_addn ("add, no copy"), the storage for v->name and v->data must remain valid for at least as long as the table entry may be read (i.e., they are not duplicated).
No return value; callers cannot detect insertion errors through this function.

functions.name: apreq_initialize
functions.description: Initializes libapreq2 for use. Applications (except Apache modules using mod_apreq) should call this exactly once before using any libapreq2 modules. If the supplied APR pool is later destroyed and libapreq2 is still needed, this must be called again with a new pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid, live apr_pool_t* that persists while libapreq2 is in use.
Should be called exactly once before using libapreq2 modules (except when running under mod_apreq which initializes automatically).
If the pool is destroyed and libapreq2 will continue to be used, the function must be called again with a new pool.
Caller should check the returned apr_status_t and handle non-success values appropriately.

functions.name: apreq_pre_initialize
functions.description: Pre-initializes libapreq2 prior to registering custom parsers. Call exactly once before calling apreq_register_parser. In Apache (mod_apreq2), this is performed automatically during post-config; modules that need to register parsers should do so in a post-config hook (APR_HOOK_MIDDLE). If the pool is later destroyed and libapreq2 is still needed, call again with a new pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid, live apr_pool_t* that persists while libapreq2 is in use.
Should be called exactly once before registering custom parsers via apreq_register_parser.
In typical use, apreq_post_initialize must later be called with the same pool used here.
If the pool is destroyed and libapreq2 will continue to be used, the function must be called again with a new pool.
Caller should check the returned apr_status_t and handle non-success values appropriately.

functions.name: apreq_post_initialize
functions.description: Completes initialization after apreq_pre_initialize; call exactly once before using libapreq2 modules for parsing. The pool argument must be the same pool that was used for apreq_pre_initialize.
requirements: pool must be the same apr_pool_t* previously passed to apreq_pre_initialize.
Should be called exactly once before using libapreq2 modules for parsing.
Caller should check the returned apr_status_t and handle non-success values appropriately.

functions.name: apreq_parse_cookie_header
functions.description: Parses a Cookie header string and stores the parsed cookies into the provided apr_table_t (jar). Intended for server-side extraction of incoming cookies, returning APR status codes to indicate success or specific parse errors.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized APR pool used for all allocations made during parsing.
jar must be a valid, mutable apr_table_t that will receive parsed cookies as entries.
header should be the raw Cookie header value to parse; its content must conform to Netscape/RFC cookie grammar to avoid parse errors.

Callers must check the returned apr_status_t; APR_SUCCESS indicates success, while documented errors include APREQ_ERROR_BADSEQ, APREQ_ERROR_MISMATCH, APR_ENOTIMPL, APREQ_ERROR_NOTOKEN, and APREQ_ERROR_BADCHAR.
Do not assume any particular value type stored in jar beyond what this API documents; use library helpers to access entries as apreq_cookie_t when needed.

functions.name: apreq_cookie_make
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apreq_cookie_t *) apreq_cookie_make(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *name, const apr_size_t nlen, const char *value, const apr_size_t vlen);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new cookie object from the provided name/value and their lengths, using the given APR pool. Intended for constructing outgoing cookies programmatically.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized APR pool; the returned apreq_cookie_t is allocated from this pool and shares its lifetime.
name and nlen together specify the cookie name; nlen should match the actual byte length of name.
value and vlen together specify the cookie value; vlen should match the actual byte length of value.
Callers should treat the returned pointer as owned by the pool; do not free it manually.
Callers should ensure the name/value satisfy cookie syntax constraints expected by downstream serializers (not enforced here).

functions.name: apreq_cookie_as_string
functions.description: Serializes a cookie into the textual form used in a Set-Cookie/Set-Cookie2 header and returns the resulting string allocated from the provided pool. Useful for emitting response headers.
requirements: c must point to a valid, initialized apreq_cookie_t.
p must be a valid APR pool that will own the returned string.
The returned string is pool-allocated; do not free it manually.
Callers should expect that cookie attributes (e.g., expires/max-age, secure, HttpOnly) present in c will be reflected in the output.

functions.name: apreq_cookie_serialize
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(int) apreq_cookie_serialize(const apreq_cookie_t *c, char *buf, apr_size_t len);
functions.description: Serializes a cookie into its Set-Cookie* header representation, writing into the caller-provided buffer up to len bytes. The return value follows apr_snprintf semantics, including special handling when len == 0.
requirements: c must point to a valid, initialized apreq_cookie_t.
If len > 0, buf must point to writable storage of at least len bytes.
When len == 0, the function behaves like apr_snprintf: it returns the length that would have been written; callers may pass buf as NULL in this case if following apr_snprintf conventions.
Callers must check the return value to determine truncation and/or required buffer size.

functions.name: apreq_cookie_expires
functions.description: Sets or clears the cookie’s expiration. Passing NULL makes it a session cookie (no expires/max-age). A non-NULL time_str resets expiration to an offset from now as parsed by apreq_atoi64t (e.g., +10m, -2h, 30d), or to a fixed date parsed by apr_date_parse_rfc.
requirements: c must point to a valid, initialized apreq_cookie_t.
If time_str is NULL, the cookie becomes a session cookie (expires/max-age not serialized).
If time_str is non-NULL, it must be parseable either as an offset matching /[+-]?\d+\s*[YMDhms]/ by apreq_atoi64t(), or as a fixed date in a format accepted by apr_date_parse_rfc().
Callers should ensure the provided time string reflects the intended expiration semantics; invalid strings will prevent setting a valid expiration.

functions.name: apreq_strerror
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(char *) apreq_strerror(apr_status_t s, char *buf, apr_size_t bufsize);
functions.description: Wrapper around apr_strerror that formats a human-readable error message for the provided APR/apreq status code. Unlike apr_strerror’s return type, this wrapper returns a char* and recognizes APREQ_ERROR_* codes defined in this header, in addition to standard APR codes. Typical usage is to pass an apr_status_t result along with a caller-provided buffer and its size; the function writes a textual description into the buffer and returns a pointer to the resulting string (usually buf). If the buffer is too small, the message may be truncated (library-defined behavior).
requirements: s must be a valid apr_status_t value (may be an APR_* or APREQ_ERROR_* code).
buf must be a non-null pointer to writable memory.
bufsize must specify the number of writable bytes available at buf and must be greater than 0.
The memory referenced by buf must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: apreq_module_status_is_error
functions.description: Classifies a module status code as fatal (error) or non-fatal. Returns 0 for commonly non-fatal statuses (APR_SUCCESS, APR_INCOMPLETE, APR_EINIT, APREQ_ERROR_NODATA, APREQ_ERROR_NOPARSER, APREQ_ERROR_NOHEADER), and 1 otherwise. Use this to decide whether to treat a status from an apreq_module_t method as an error.
requirements: s is an apr_status_t value returned by an apreq_module_t method or related API; no additional constraints.

functions.name: apreq_jar
functions.description: Exposes the parsed Cookie header as an APR table for the given request handle. It forwards to the module’s jar vtable function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t whose module pointer is set and whose module->jar function is implemented.
t must be a non-NULL output parameter; on return it will be NULL or a valid apr_table_t.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t; on non-success, table contents may be module-specific.

functions.name: apreq_args
functions.description: Exposes the parsed query string (args) as an APR table for the given request handle, via the module’s args vtable function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->args implementation.
t must be a non-NULL output parameter; on return it will be NULL or a valid apr_table_t.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t; on error, table contents may be undefined.

functions.name: apreq_body
functions.description: Exposes the parsed request body parameters as an APR table for the given request handle, via the module’s body vtable function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->body implementation.
t must be a non-NULL output parameter; on return it will be NULL or a valid apr_table_t.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t; on error, table contents may be undefined.

functions.name: apreq_jar_get
functions.description: Returns the first cookie matching the given name (case-insensitive) from the request’s cookie jar, via the module’s jar_get function. Returns NULL if none match.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->jar_get implementation.
name must be a non-NULL cookie name string; matching is case-insensitive.
Caller must handle a NULL return when no match exists.

functions.name: apreq_args_get
functions.description: Returns the first query-string parameter matching the given name (case-insensitive) via the module’s args_get function. Returns NULL if none match.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->args_get implementation.
name must be a non-NULL parameter name string; matching is case-insensitive.
Caller must handle a NULL return when no match exists.

functions.name: apreq_body_get
functions.description: Returns the first body parameter matching the given name (case-insensitive) via the module’s body_get function. Returns NULL if none match.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->body_get implementation.
name must be a non-NULL parameter name string; matching is case-insensitive.
Caller must handle a NULL return when no match exists.

functions.name: apreq_parser_get
functions.description: Fetches the active body parser for the request via the module’s parser_get function and stores it in parser.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->parser_get implementation.
parser must be a non-NULL output pointer; on success it will point to the active parser (may be NULL depending on module state).
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t; on error, parser may be undefined.

functions.name: apreq_parser_set
functions.description: Sets the body parser for the request via the module’s parser_set function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->parser_set implementation.
parser is the new parser to use; must be a valid apreq_parser_t object appropriate for the handle’s module. Exact constraints are module-specific and not documented here.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for success or module-specific errors.

functions.name: apreq_hook_add
functions.description: Adds a parser hook for the request via the module’s hook_add function. Hooks can observe/modify parsing behavior.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->hook_add implementation.
hook must be a valid apreq_hook_t instance; exact lifecycle/ownership rules are module-specific and not documented here.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_limit_set
functions.description: Sets the maximum in-memory bytes that a brigade may use for this request via the module’s brigade_limit_set function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->brigade_limit_set implementation.
bytes is an apr_size_t (non-negative by type); no explicit upper bound is documented.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_limit_get
functions.description: Retrieves the current in-memory brigade limit via the module’s brigade_limit_get function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->brigade_limit_get implementation.
bytes must be a non-NULL output pointer; on success receives the current limit.
On module-specific error, bytes may be left undefined; caller must check apr_status_t before using it.

functions.name: apreq_read_limit_set
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of bytes that will be fed into a parser for this request via the module’s read_limit_set function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->read_limit_set implementation.
bytes is an unsigned 64-bit limit; no explicit maximum is documented.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t.

functions.name: apreq_read_limit_get
functions.description: Retrieves the active read limit via the module’s read_limit_get function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->read_limit_get implementation.
bytes must be a non-NULL output pointer; on success receives the current limit.
On module-specific error, bytes may be left undefined; caller must check apr_status_t before using it.

functions.name: apreq_temp_dir_set
functions.description: Sets the directory used by the parser for temporary files via the module’s temp_dir_set function. The path may be NULL to clear/reset per module semantics.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->temp_dir_set implementation.
path may be NULL or a valid C string path; interpretation is module-specific.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t.

functions.name: apreq_temp_dir_get
functions.description: Retrieves the directory used by the parser for temporary files via the module’s temp_dir_get function.
requirements: req must be a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t with a valid module->temp_dir_get implementation.
path must be a non-NULL output pointer; on APR_SUCCESS, the returned path pointer is valid and may be NULL (meaning no temp dir set).
On non-success return, path may be left undefined; caller must check apr_status_t before using it.

functions.name: apreq_handle_cgi
functions.description: Creates (or returns a cached) apreq handle suitable for a CGI program; it reads input from stdin and writes output to stdout. The handle is cached in the provided APR pool’s userdata so subsequent calls with the same pool return the same handle.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized APR pool whose lifetime should encompass the handle’s usage.
Caller must check for a NULL return only in the event of pool allocation failure.
Intended for CGI environments; input is read from stdin and output to stdout.

functions.name: apreq_handle_custom
functions.signature: apreq_handle_t *apreq_handle_custom(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *query_string, const char *cookie, apreq_parser_t *parser, apr_uint64_t read_limit, apr_bucket_brigade *in)
functions.description: Creates a custom apreq handle initialized with static values, useful for testing the parser or handling data from non-Apache/CGI sources. It can parse a provided query string and cookie header, uses the provided body parser, enforces the provided read limit, and consumes the provided input brigade for the request body.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized APR pool; the handle’s parsed data will be allocated from it.
query_string may be NULL or a C string to be parsed into the args table.
cookie may be NULL or a C string representing the Cookie header value.
parser must be a valid apreq_parser_t appropriate for parsing the provided body data; exact module-specific constraints are not documented.
read_limit is an unsigned 64-bit maximum of bytes to read from the body.
in must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade containing the request body; ownership/lifetime must outlive parsing operations.

functions.name: apreq_param
functions.description: Finds and returns the first parameter (query string first, then body) matching the specified name (case-insensitive). Returns NULL if no match is found.
requirements: req must be a valid apreq_handle_t.
key must be a non-NULL parameter name string; matching is case-insensitive.
Caller must handle a NULL return when no match exists.

functions.name: apreq_cookie
functions.signature: apreq_cookie_t *apreq_cookie(apreq_handle_t *req, const char *name)  // macro alias to apreq_jar_get(req, name)
functions.description: Convenience API macro that returns the first cookie with the specified (case-insensitive) name from the request. This macro expands to apreq_jar_get(req, name) and therefore behaves identically to that inline function. Use it to quickly fetch a single cookie by name; returns NULL if no matching cookie is found. Notes: This is a function-like macro, not a link-time symbol; the underlying implementation is the module’s jar_get vtable method invoked via apreq_jar_get.
requirements: req must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized apreq_handle_t associated with a module that implements jar_get.
name must be a valid, null-terminated C string; matching is case-insensitive.
Caller must handle a NULL return value when no matching cookie exists.
The returned apreq_cookie_t pointer’s ownership/lifetime is tied to the request handle’s internals (exact lifetime not specified here).

functions.name: apreq_params
functions.description: Builds and returns an APR table containing key-value pairs for the full request (combining args and body). The returned table is allocated from the provided pool and is never NULL.
requirements: req must be a valid apreq_handle_t.
p must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the returned table.
Caller can assume a non-NULL return; contents depend on available args/body parameters.

functions.name: apreq_cookies
functions.description: Returns an APR table containing all request cookies, allocated from the provided pool.
requirements: req must be a valid apreq_handle_t.
p must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the returned table.
Caller should not assume non-NULL unless module guarantees it; the header comment does not state the return is never NULL.

functions.name: apreq_param_is_tainted
functions.description: Returns 1 if the parameter’s taint flag is set, 0 otherwise. Intended to allow callers to check whether a parameter value has been marked as tainted (e.g., untrusted).
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.
No side effects; safe to call multiple times.

functions.name: apreq_param_tainted_on
functions.description: Sets the parameter’s taint flag. Use to mark a parameter as untrusted/tainted.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.

functions.name: apreq_param_tainted_off
functions.description: Clears the parameter’s taint flag. Use to mark a parameter as not tainted.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.

functions.name: apreq_param_charset_set
functions.description: Sets the character encoding flag for a parameter and returns the previous charset value.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.
c must be a valid apreq_charset_t value supported by the library (exact set is library-defined).

functions.name: apreq_param_charset_get
functions.description: Returns the parameter’s character encoding setting.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.

functions.name: apreq_value_to_param
functions.description: Upgrades/casts an args/body table value to an apreq_param_t pointer. This is for converting values fetched from parameter tables into full parameter objects.
requirements: val must be a pointer obtained from an apreq_value_t data field originating from apreq parameter/args/body tables (i.e., values returned by apreq_args(), apreq_body(), or apreq_params()).
Passing arbitrary strings not originating from apreq tables results in undefined behavior.
The underlying parameter must still be alive (allocated pool not destroyed).

functions.name: apreq_param_make
functions.signature: apreq_param_t *apreq_param_make(apr_pool_t *p, const char *name, const apr_size_t nlen, const char *val, const apr_size_t vlen);
functions.description: Creates a parameter from raw name/value data allocated from the given APR pool.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-NULL APR pool.
name may be NULL only if nlen is 0; otherwise name must reference at least nlen bytes.
val may be NULL only if vlen is 0; otherwise val must reference at least vlen bytes.
nlen and vlen specify byte lengths; data need not be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: apreq_param_decode
functions.signature: apr_status_t apreq_param_decode(apreq_param_t **param, apr_pool_t *pool, const char *word, apr_size_t nlen, apr_size_t vlen);
functions.description: URL-decodes a name=value pair into an apreq_param_t allocated from pool. On success stores the resulting param in *param and returns APR_SUCCESS; returns APREQ_ERROR_BADSEQ or APREQ_ERROR_BADCHAR on malformed input.
requirements: param must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to receive the result.
pool must be a valid APR pool.
word must point to the start of the URL-encoded name=value pair and reference at least nlen + (vlen ? 1 : 0) + vlen bytes.
Unless vlen == 0, there must be exactly one '=' separator between name and value (i.e., at offset nlen).
nlen is the length of the URL-encoded name; vlen is the length of the URL-encoded value.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for success or specific error codes.

functions.name: apreq_param_encode
functions.description: URL-encodes the given parameter as a single name=value pair string allocated from the provided pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool.
param must be a valid, non-NULL apreq_param_t pointer.
Caller owns the returned string’s lifetime via the pool; treat as immutable.

functions.name: apreq_parse_query_string
functions.description: Parses a URL-encoded query string into a parameter table. Tokens are split on '&' or ';'. Words without '=' are treated as name-value pairs with value length 0.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool used to allocate parameter data.
t must be a valid, non-NULL APR table to which parameters will be added.
qs should point to a URL-encoded query string; behavior for NULL is library-defined and not documented here.
Caller must check the returned apr_status_t for success.

functions.name: apreq_params_as_array
functions.description: Returns an array of apreq_param_t* matching the given key (case-insensitive). If key is NULL, returns all parameters. May trigger parsing if not already parsed.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the returned array header and contents.
t must be a parameter table returned by apreq_args(), apreq_body(), or apreq_params().
key may be NULL to fetch all; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle an empty array when no matches exist.

functions.name: apreq_params_as_string
functions.signature: const char *apreq_params_as_string(apr_pool_t *p, const apr_table_t *t, const char *key, apreq_join_t mode);
functions.description: Returns a joined string (typically ", " separated; join behavior per apreq_join()) containing all parameter values for the given key (case-insensitive). If none are found, returns an empty string. May parse the request if needed. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the result string.
t must be a parameter table returned by apreq_args(), apreq_body(), or apreq_params().
key may be NULL to fetch all values; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string.
mode must be a valid apreq_join_t specifying the join strategy.
Caller must handle NULL as an error condition and an empty string for "no matches".

functions.name: apreq_uploads
functions.description: Returns a table of all parameters in the body that have non-NULL upload brigades (i.e., file uploads). May parse the request if necessary.
requirements: body must be a parameter table returned by apreq_body() or apreq_params().
pool must be a valid APR pool to allocate the returned table structure.
Caller should not modify the returned table keys/values outside documented APIs.

functions.name: apreq_upload
functions.description: Returns the first parameter in the body that matches the given name (case-insensitive) and has a non-NULL upload brigade. If name is NULL, returns the first upload. May parse the request if necessary.
requirements: body must be a parameter table returned by apreq_body() or apreq_params().
name may be NULL to select the first upload; otherwise must be a NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle NULL when no matching upload exists.

functions.name: apreq_parser_run
functions.signature: static APR_INLINE apr_status_t apreq_parser_run(apreq_parser_t *psr, apr_table_t *t, apr_bucket_brigade *bb)
functions.description: Runs the parser associated with the given parser instance over the provided bucket brigade, inserting parsed parameters into the table. Parsers may consume all buckets or leave "rejected" data in the brigade; callers must manage any remaining buckets. Passing bb == NULL is valid and causes the parser to report its public status (APR_INCOMPLETE, APR_SUCCESS, or an error). Typically invoked repeatedly as input arrives.
requirements: psr must be a valid, initialized apreq_parser_t with its parser callback set.
t should be a valid apr_table_t to receive parsed parameters.
bb may be NULL to query status; if non-NULL it should be a valid apr_bucket_brigade.
Do not pass any "rejected" buckets left in bb back to the parser on subsequent calls.

functions.name: apreq_hook_run
functions.signature: static APR_INLINE apr_status_t apreq_hook_run(apreq_hook_t *h, apreq_param_t *param, apr_bucket_brigade *bb)
functions.description: Invokes a single hook with the current parameter and incoming bucket brigade. Hooks may modify the brigade; after all hooks complete, the brigade contents are appended to the parameter's internal brigade (param->bb). Returns APR_SUCCESS on success; other values indicate errors.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized apreq_hook_t whose hook callback is set.
param must be a valid apreq_param_t corresponding to the current field being processed.
bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade; hooks may modify it.
Callers should check the return value and treat non-APR_SUCCESS as an error.

functions.name: apreq_parse_headers
functions.description: Parses RFC 822-style headers from the body stream, rejecting all data after the first CRLF CRLF (empty line). Intended to be used as a request-body parser via apreq_parser_run. May leave rejected data in bb.
requirements: parser must be a valid apreq_parser_t configured to use this parser function.
t must be a valid apr_table_t to receive parsed header fields.
bb may be NULL to query status; if non-NULL it should contain body data to parse.
Do not re-feed any rejected buckets left in bb back to the parser.

functions.name: apreq_parse_urlencoded
functions.description: Parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded data (RFC 2396-style percent-encoding) from the request body into parameters stored in t. Used via apreq_parser_run and subject to the general parser contract (may leave rejected data).
requirements: parser must be a valid apreq_parser_t configured to use this parser function.
t must be a valid apr_table_t to receive parsed parameters.
bb may be NULL to query status; otherwise should be a valid brigade containing urlencoded data.
Do not re-feed any rejected buckets left in bb back to the parser.

functions.name: apreq_parse_multipart
functions.description: Parses multipart/form-data (RFC 2388) and XForms 1.0 multipart/related bodies. It rejects buckets comprising preamble and postamble text (normal, not an error). Often used with hooks to process file uploads. May leave rejected data in bb.
requirements: parser must be a valid apreq_parser_t configured to use this parser function.
t must be a valid apr_table_t to receive parsed form fields and file metadata.
bb may be NULL to query status; otherwise should be a valid brigade containing multipart data.
Do not re-feed any rejected (e.g., preamble/postamble) buckets left in bb back to the parser.

functions.name: apreq_parse_generic
functions.description: Generic pass-through parser. It does not add entries to the request body table. It creates a dummy apreq_param_t to pass to configured hooks; if no hooks are configured, the dummy param’s brigade will contain a copy of the request body. The dummy param can be retrieved by casting parser->ctx to (apreq_param_t **).
requirements: parser must be a valid apreq_parser_t; to retrieve the dummy param, treat parser->ctx as (apreq_param_t **).
t is accepted but will not receive entries from this parser.
bb may be NULL to query status; otherwise should be a valid brigade containing body data.
If no hooks are configured, expect a copy of the request body in the dummy param’s bb; manage its lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: apreq_hook_apr_xml_parser
functions.description: Hook that parses incoming data into an apr_xml_doc using APR’s XML parser. It parses until EOS is encountered; the parsed document is available only after successful completion. The hook’s ctx can be cast to (apr_xml_doc **) to retrieve the parsed document.
requirements: hook must be a valid apreq_hook_t; its ctx may be used as an (apr_xml_doc **) out-parameter to retrieve the result.
param is provided by the parsing pipeline; it must be valid.
bb must be a valid brigade; the hook expects to see the EOS bucket before the document is available.
Callers should only read the parsed document after the hook has completed successfully.

functions.name: apreq_parser_make
functions.signature: apreq_parser_t * apreq_parser_make(apr_pool_t *pool, apr_bucket_alloc_t *ba, const char *content_type, apreq_parser_function_t pfn, apr_size_t brigade_limit, const char *temp_dir, apreq_hook_t *hook, void *ctx)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a new request-body parser instance. The parser uses the provided bucket allocator, content type, parser function, in-memory brigade limit, optional temp directory, initial hook list, and an initial context pointer.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t used to allocate the parser and associated structures.
ba should be a valid apr_bucket_alloc_t for creating bucket brigades.
content_type should name the content type this parser handles.
pfn should be a valid apreq_parser_function_t to perform parsing.
brigade_limit sets the maximum in-memory bytes a brigade may use; choose an appropriate value for your environment.
temp_dir, if non-NULL, should be a valid directory path for temporary files.
hook may be NULL or a valid hook chain head to associate with the parser.
ctx is stored as the parser’s internal context and may be NULL or any user data pointer.

functions.name: apreq_hook_make
functions.signature: apreq_hook_t * apreq_hook_make(apr_pool_t *pool, apreq_hook_function_t hook, apreq_hook_t *next, void *ctx)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a new hook. The hook wraps a callback function, an optional next-hook pointer to form a chain, and a context pointer passed to the callback.
requirements: pool must be a valid apr_pool_t used to allocate the hook.
hook must be a valid apreq_hook_function_t (callback) to invoke for incoming data.
next may be NULL or a valid apreq_hook_t to chain after this hook.
ctx is stored as the hook’s context and may be NULL or any user data pointer.

functions.name: apreq_parser_add_hook
functions.description: Appends a new hook to the end of the parser’s hook list.
requirements: p must be a valid apreq_parser_t.
h must be a valid apreq_hook_t to append.
Caller should check the returned apr_status_t for success or failure.

functions.name: apreq_parser
functions.description: Returns the default parser function associated with the given MIME type or full Content-Type header. Returns NULL if the enctype is unrecognized.
requirements: enctype should be a MIME type string or a full Content-Type header value.
Callers must check for a NULL return to handle unknown or unregistered types.

functions.name: apreq_register_parser
functions.description: Registers or removes a parser function for a given MIME enctype in the apreq_parser() internal lookup table. Passing pfn == NULL removes any existing parser for that enctype.
requirements: enctype must be a MIME type string identifying the parser mapping.
pfn is the parser function to register; set pfn to NULL to remove an existing mapping.
Caller should check the returned apr_status_t for success or failure.

functions.name: apreq_hook_disable_uploads
functions.description: Hook that forces upload handling to fail when a file-upload field is present by returning APREQ_ERROR_GENERAL, effectively disabling the multipart/form-data parser for uploads.
requirements: Use this as a hook in a parser’s hook chain when uploads must be disallowed.
Callers should expect APREQ_ERROR_GENERAL when a file-upload field is encountered and handle the error accordingly.
hook, param, and bb must be valid as per the general hook contract.

functions.name: apreq_hook_discard_brigade
functions.description: Hook that calls apr_brigade_cleanup on the incoming brigade after passing it to any subsequent hooks. Useful to free memory after downstream processing concludes.
requirements: Expect the brigade to be cleaned up by this hook; do not use bb after this hook completes unless it has been repopulated downstream.
hook, param, and bb must be valid as per the general hook contract.

functions.name: apreq_hook_find_param
functions.description: Special-purpose hook used to locate a parameter by name during parsing. The hook’s ctx must be an apreq_hook_find_param_ctx_t* with name set to the sought parameter, param set to NULL, and prev set to the previous hook pointer. When the parameter is found, ctx->param is set and the hook removes itself from the chain.
requirements: Initialize hook->ctx to an apreq_hook_find_param_ctx_t* with: ctx->name set to the target parameter name; ctx->param set to NULL; ctx->prev set to the address of the previous hook pointer.
This hook should be the first one invoked; add it manually with ctx->prev = &parser->hook instead of using apreq_parser_add_hook.
hook, param, and bb must be valid as per the general hook contract.

functions.name: apreq_join
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(char *) apreq_join(apr_pool_t *p, const char *sep, const apr_array_header_t *arr, apreq_join_t mode);
functions.description: Join an array of apreq_value_t entries into a single string, inserting sep between values. Returns an empty string if there are no values, or NULL on error. Intended for building delimited strings from arrays.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool used to allocate the returned string.
arr must point to an apr_array_header_t whose elements are apreq_value_t entries.
sep is the separator inserted between joined values; behavior for NULL is unspecified.
mode selects the join behavior as defined by apreq_join_t.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect allocation or processing errors.

functions.name: apreq_index
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_ssize_t) apreq_index(const char* hay, apr_size_t hlen, const char* ndl, apr_size_t nlen, const apreq_match_t type);
functions.description: Search hay for the substring/pattern ndl according to the specified match type, returning the offset of the first match or -1 if no match is found.
requirements: hay must point to a buffer of at least hlen bytes.
ndl must point to a buffer of at least nlen bytes; nlen should be > 0 for a meaningful search.
type specifies the matching algorithm as an apreq_match_t.
Return value is -1 when no match is found; non-negative offsets are valid indices into hay.

functions.name: apreq_quote
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_size_t) apreq_quote(char *dest, const char *src, const apr_size_t slen);
functions.description: Copy src into dest with embedded double quotes escaped by a backslash, and append a trailing null byte. Returns the length of the quoted copy placed in dest.
requirements: dest must have enough space to hold the quoted result and the trailing null byte.
src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes representing the string to quote.
The function writes a trailing '\0' terminator to dest.
In-place operation (dest == src) is not documented; callers should provide a distinct buffer or ensure it is safe.

functions.name: apreq_quote_once
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_size_t) apreq_quote_once(char *dest, const char *src, const apr_size_t slen);
functions.description: Same as apreq_quote, except if src begins and ends with quotes it assumes src is already correctly quoted and copies it to dest without adding escapes. Returns the length of the copy in dest.
requirements: dest must be large enough to hold the copy and trailing null byte.
src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
Behavior depends on whether src begins and ends in quote marks; otherwise it escapes quotes like apreq_quote.
In-place operation (dest == src) is not documented; callers should provide a distinct buffer or ensure it is safe.

functions.name: apreq_encode
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_size_t) apreq_encode(char *dest, const char *src, const apr_size_t slen);
functions.description: URL-encode src into dest. Returns the length of the encoded string written to dest; it will not exceed 3*slen. A trailing '\0' is written.
requirements: dest must be large enough to hold up to 3*slen bytes plus the trailing '\0'.
src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
Caller should use the returned length to know the actual size written.

functions.name: apreq_cp1252_to_utf8
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_size_t) apreq_cp1252_to_utf8(char *dest, const char *src, apr_size_t slen);
functions.description: Convert a Windows-1252 (CP1252) encoded string to UTF-8, storing the result in dest. Returns the length of the UTF-8 string written; it does not exceed 3*slen. A trailing '\0' is written.
requirements: dest must be large enough to hold up to 3*slen bytes plus the trailing '\0'.
src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
Caller should use the returned length to determine the number of bytes written.

functions.name: apreq_charset_divine
functions.description: Heuristically determine the character set of the input string. Returns APREQ_CHARSET_ASCII for 7-bit content only, APREQ_CHARSET_UTF8 for valid UTF-8 sequences, APREQ_CHARSET_LATIN1 if no control characters are present, or APREQ_CHARSET_CP1252 if control characters are present.
requirements: src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
Return value is an apreq_charset_t indicating the detected charset; the heuristic may misclassify ambiguous data.

functions.name: apreq_decode
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_status_t) apreq_decode(char *dest, apr_size_t *dlen, const char *src, apr_size_t slen);
functions.description: URL-decode src into dest, writing the decoded length to dlen. Supports decoding of %uXXXX sequences into UTF-8 per ECMA-262 B.2.1. Returns APR_SUCCESS on success; APR_INCOMPLETE if input ends mid-escape; APREQ_ERROR_BADSEQ or APREQ_ERROR_BADCHAR on malformed input. On non-success, dlen is set to the number of bytes successfully decoded.
requirements: dest must be large enough to hold the decoded string and a trailing null character.
dlen must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resultant decoded length.
src must point to a buffer of at least slen bytes.
In-situ decoding (dest == src) is supported, as used by apreq_unescape.
Caller must handle non-success APR status codes and consult dlen for the number of bytes decoded before the error.

functions.name: apreq_decodev
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_status_t) apreq_decodev(char *dest, apr_size_t *dlen, struct iovec *v, int nelts);
functions.description: URL-decode a source string provided as an array of iovec segments, writing the result into dest and the decoded length to dlen. Supports %uXXXX decoding into UTF-8 per ECMA-262 B.2.1. Returns APR_SUCCESS, APR_INCOMPLETE if an iovec ends mid-escape, or APREQ_ERROR_BADSEQ/APREQ_ERROR_BADCHAR on malformed input. On non-success, dlen includes the last successfully decoded value.
requirements: dest must be large enough to hold the fully decoded data and a trailing null character.
dlen must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resultant decoded length.
v must point to an array of nelts iovec entries that together represent the source string.
nelts must be non-negative and match the number of valid iovec entries provided.
Caller must handle non-success APR status codes and use dlen to determine how much was decoded.

functions.name: apreq_escape
functions.signature: static APR_INLINE char *apreq_escape(apr_pool_t *p, const char *src, const apr_size_t slen)
functions.description: Allocate and return a URL-encoded copy of src from pool p. Internally allocates 3*slen+1 bytes and calls apreq_encode. Returns NULL if src is NULL.
requirements: p must be a valid APR pool; memory for the returned string is allocated from p.
src may be NULL; if NULL, the function returns NULL without allocating.
slen must be the length of src in bytes when src is non-NULL.
Caller should not free the returned string directly; it is managed by the pool.

functions.name: apreq_unescape
functions.description: In-situ URL-decode the given null-terminated string. Returns the decoded length on success, or -1 on error. Internally calls apreq_decode with dest == src.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, mutable, null-terminated buffer.
Buffer must be large enough to hold the decoded result in-place (decoding does not increase length).
Caller must check for a return value < 0 to detect errors.

functions.name: apreq_atoi64f
functions.description: Convert a human-readable file size string (using suffixes K, M, or G and optional trailing 'b', case-insensitive) to a 64-bit byte count.
requirements: s should match the pattern ^\d+[KMG]b?$ (case-insensitive) as documented; behavior for malformed input is unspecified.
Caller should validate input format before calling to avoid undefined/unspecified behavior.

functions.name: apreq_atoi64t
functions.description: Convert a human-readable time duration string to seconds. Accepted format is an optional leading '+', followed by digits and a unit one of Y, M, D, h, m, or s.
requirements: s should match the pattern ^\+?\d+[YMDhms]$ as documented; behavior for malformed input is unspecified.
Caller should validate input format before calling to avoid undefined/unspecified behavior.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_fwrite
functions.description: Write the contents of the bucket brigade bb to the file f. On success, wlen is set to the total length written. Returns APR_SUCCESS or an error from apr_bucket_read or apr_file_writev. Note: if the final bucket in bb is a spool bucket, this leaks a bucket brigade into bb->p.
requirements: f must be a valid, open apr_file_t suitable for writing.
wlen must be a non-NULL pointer; on success it receives the total bytes written.
bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade containing readable buckets.
Caller must handle non-success APR status codes.
Be aware of the documented leakage behavior when the last bucket is a spool bucket.

functions.name: apreq_file_mktemp
functions.description: Create a temporary file associated with pool. On success, *fp receives the created apr_file_t. If path is NULL, the directory is chosen via tempnam(). The file will be closed and deleted when the associated pool is destroyed. Returns APR_SUCCESS or errors from apr_filepath_merge or apr_file_mktemp.
requirements: fp must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting apr_file_t*.
pool must be a valid APR pool; the temp file's lifetime is bound to this pool.
path, if not NULL, must name a base directory in which to create the temp file; if NULL, tempnam() is used to select the directory.
Caller must check the APR status return and only use *fp on success.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_setaside
functions.description: Set aside all buckets in the brigade into the specified pool p by calling apr_bucket_setaside on each bucket.
requirements: bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade.
p must be a valid APR pool into which the buckets can be set aside.
Caller must handle non-success APR status codes if any bucket could not be set aside.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_copy
functions.description: Append copies of all buckets from source brigade s to destination brigade d using apr_bucket_copy. Returns APR_SUCCESS or the error from apr_bucket_copy. Using the same brigade for both s and d is undefined behavior.
requirements: d must be a valid destination apr_bucket_brigade.
s must be a valid source apr_bucket_brigade.
s must not be the same brigade as d (s == d produces undefined behavior).
Caller must handle non-success APR status codes and the fact that copied buckets are appended to d.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_move
functions.signature: static APR_INLINE void apreq_brigade_move(apr_bucket_brigade *d, apr_bucket_brigade *s, apr_bucket *e)
functions.description: Move the front portion of source brigade s to destination brigade d. All buckets in s before bucket e are appended to d. If e is the sentinel of s, all buckets are moved. If the first bucket equals e, nothing is moved.
requirements: d must be a valid destination apr_bucket_brigade.
s must be a valid source apr_bucket_brigade.
e must be either APR_BRIGADE_SENTINEL(s) or a bucket that belongs to s.
After the call, the moved buckets are removed from s and appended to d.

functions.name: apreq_header_attribute
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_status_t) apreq_header_attribute(const char *hdr, const char *name, const apr_size_t nlen, const char **val, apr_size_t *vlen);
functions.description: Search the header string hdr for the first value of a named attribute. On success, returns APR_SUCCESS and sets *val to the start of the value and *vlen to its length. Returns APREQ_ERROR_NOATTR if the attribute is not found, or APREQ_ERROR_BADSEQ if an unpaired quote was detected.
requirements: hdr must point to a valid null-terminated header string to scan.
name must point to the attribute name to search for; nlen must be its length in bytes.
val must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the pointer to the first matching value.
vlen must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the length of the matching value.
Caller must handle non-success status codes and should not modify the memory referenced by *val unless the underlying buffer is mutable.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_concat
functions.signature: APREQ_DECLARE(apr_status_t) apreq_brigade_concat(apr_pool_t *pool, const char *temp_dir, apr_size_t brigade_limit, apr_bucket_brigade *out, apr_bucket_brigade *in);
functions.description: Concatenate brigade in onto out. If the resulting length of out would exceed brigade_limit, the appended data are spooled into a temporary file (APREQ_SPOOL bucket) created using pool and temp_dir. Returns APR_SUCCESS or an error from apr_brigade_length, apreq_file_mktemp, apreq_brigade_fwrite, or apr_file_seek.
requirements: pool must be a valid APR pool used for creating a tempfile bucket if spooling is needed.
temp_dir should be a valid directory path for tempfile creation when spooling; exact behavior if NULL is not specified.
brigade_limit specifies the maximum in-memory size for out; exceeding it triggers spooling.
out must be a valid destination apr_bucket_brigade.
in must be a valid source apr_bucket_brigade.
Caller must handle returned APR status codes and be prepared for out to use a spool file when the limit is exceeded.

functions.name: apreq_brigade_spoolfile
functions.description: Return the spool file used by the brigade if it is spooled in a file (i.e., uses an APREQ_SPOOL bucket); otherwise return NULL.
requirements: bb must be a valid apr_bucket_brigade.
Caller must handle a NULL return when the brigade is not using a spool file.

import random
import struct
import string

# Target: ap_slotmem_provider_t::create fuzzer stub
# The stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for the name and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for sizes/flags.
# We should provide initial bytes that, when consumed by the harness, yield:
# - Reasonable non-empty name strings (ASCII identifiers)
# - Unsigned ints for item_size, item_num, flags with values that keep total size small
# The harness already bounds sizes using modulo and caps total bytes, but good seeds help exercise code paths.
# We will generate a compact binary format of our own that typical FUZZ framework will split into
# strings and integers in order. To maximize usefulness across both provided stubs, we place several
# candidate strings and a series of unsigned ints.

# Layout we’ll emit:
# [header]
#   1 byte: count of strings (nstr in 1..5)
#   1 byte: count of uint32 values (nint in 3..8)
# [strings]
#   For each string: 1 byte length L (1..32), followed by L bytes [A-Za-z0-9_-]
# [uints]
#   For each int: 4 bytes little-endian uint32 with values chosen to small range for item sizes/counts
# This generic buffer is friendly to typical fuzz param extractors that scan sequences of
# strings and integers from the input stream.

def _rand_ident(rng, min_len=2, max_len=16):
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L)).encode('ascii')


def _pick_small_uint(rng):
    # Favor small sizes to keep buffers small, but include occasional larger values
    choices = [rng.randint(1, 64), rng.randint(1, 32), rng.randint(0, 15), rng.randint(0, 255)]
    v = rng.choice(choices)
    return v & 0xFFFFFFFF


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide counts
    nstr = rng.randint(2, 5)
    nint = rng.randint(3, 8)

    out = bytearray()
    out.append(nstr)
    out.append(nint)

    # Emit strings: ensure first is non-empty identifier likely used as name
    for i in range(nstr):
        # Make the first string a likely provider/instance name like "sm" or custom id
        if i == 0:
            name = rng.choice([b"sm", b"slot", b"mem", _rand_ident(rng, 2, 8)])
        else:
            name = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 24)
        L = max(1, min(len(name), 32))
        out.append(L)
        out.extend(name[:L])

    # Emit integers: ensure first two help sizes (small), then some variety, then a flags uint
    ints = []
    # Preferred small item_size and item_num
    ints.append(rng.randint(1, 32))
    ints.append(rng.randint(1, 16))
    # Additional values
    while len(ints) < nint - 1:
        ints.append(_pick_small_uint(rng))
    # A flags-ish value (bitmask-ish)
    flag_bits = 0
    for bit in [0, 1, 2, 3]:
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            flag_bits |= (1 << bit)
    ints.append(flag_bits)

    for v in ints[:nint]:
        out.extend(struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF))

    # Ensure total size under 4KB
    return bytes(out[:4096])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting ASCII strings for strchr/strrchr/strstr use cases.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used to form C strings; we keep them under small limits
# and include patterns that exercise edge cases: empty, single-char, repeated
# chars, mixed cases, unicode-like bytes, long runs, and embedded NUL (though
# stubs use std::string then c_str(), so embedded NULs will truncate; still
# include to vary prefix behavior).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_common_needles = [
    "a", "A", "\x00", "\n", "\r", " ", "\t", ",", ".", "-", "_",
    "0", "1", "9", "z", "Z", "~", "*", "/", "?"
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # bias towards tokens useful for search
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " \t\n,.-_/?:;|[](){}<>\"'" + "\x00"
    s = []
    for i in range(length):
        ch = r.choice(alphabet)
        s.append(ch)
    return "".join(s)

def _make_hay_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    vars: List[str] = []
    # empty
    vars.append("")
    # single char
    vars.extend(["a", "\x00", "\n", " "])
    # repeated runs
    vars.append("a" * r.randint(1, 100))
    vars.append("abc" * r.randint(1, 50))
    # pattern with separators
    vars.append("alpha,beta,gamma,delta")
    # path-like
    vars.append("/usr/local/bin:/bin:/usr/bin")
    # mixed case
    vars.append("CaseSensitiveCASE")
    # include NUL mid-string (will truncate for c_str usage but useful when copied to vector and then NUL added)
    vars.append("prefix\x00suffix")
    # random ascii
    vars.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 256))
    # long random with repeated token
    token = r.choice(["abc", "XYZ", "needle", "test"])
    vars.append((token + "_") * r.randint(5, 50))
    return vars

def _make_needle_variants(r: random.Random, hay: str) -> List[str]:
    vars: List[str] = []
    vars.append("")
    # choose substrings from hay if possible
    if hay:
        start = r.randrange(0, len(hay))
        end = r.randrange(start, len(hay))
        vars.append(hay[start:end] or hay[start:start+1])
        # take exact token if exists
        for t in ["abc", "XYZ", "needle", "test", ",", "/", " "]:
            if t in hay:
                vars.append(t)
                break
    # common needles
    vars.extend(_common_needles)
    # random short
    vars.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8))
    return vars

def _pack_strings(pairs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as newline-separated corpus entries: the harness will consume them
    # as successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls (first is hay, then needle, etc.).
    data = "\n".join(pairs).encode("latin1", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build two strings: one for haystack and one for needle, but stubs request
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times independently. We provide a bundle with
    # multiple lines so the fuzzer can pick sequentially.
    hay_choices = _make_hay_variants(r)
    hay = r.choice(hay_choices)
    needle_choices = _make_needle_variants(r, hay)
    needle = r.choice(needle_choices)

    # Also include additional variants to seed different paths across stubs
    extra_hays = _make_hay_variants(r)
    extra_needles = _make_needle_variants(r, r.choice(extra_hays))

    # Ensure manageable sizes matching stub truncations
    def clamp(s: str, n: int) -> str:
        return s[:n]

    hay = clamp(hay, 1024)
    needle = clamp(needle, 256)

    lines: List[str] = []
    # Provide several entries to feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in order
    lines.append(hay)
    lines.append(needle)
    # Add diverse extras
    lines.extend([clamp(x, 1024) for x in extra_hays[:4]])
    lines.extend([clamp(x, 256) for x in extra_needles[:4]])

    # Add single-character lines to exercise ap_strchr/rchr with different bytes
    for ch in ["a", "\x00", "\n", " ", ",", "/", "Z"]:
        lines.append(ch)

    # Final sanity: ensure at least two lines
    if not lines:
        lines = ["", "a"]

    return _pack_strings(lines)
